records.name: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships)
records.official_source: Defense Language and National Security Education Office (DLNSEO), National Security Education Program; administered by the Institute of International Education (IIE)
records.region: Overseas study outside Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand (preferred regions: Africa, Asia, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East). Applicants must be U.S. citizens enrolled at a U.S. institution.
records.duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study; 25-52 weeks preferred; minimum 12 weeks for most applicants (8 weeks minimum for undergraduate STEM summer programmes).
records.deadline: National deadlines for the 2027 Boren Awards: Boren Fellowships January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships January 27, 2027 - both 5pm Eastern time.
records.application_period: The 2027-2028 Boren Scholarship and Boren Fellowship application cycle is open as of 2026-10-01. National deadlines are January 20, 2027 (Fellowships) and January 27, 2027 (Scholarships), 5pm Eastern time. Selected applicants are notified in mid-to-late April. Campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that applicants are asked to respect.
records.description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and research or language study for U.S. graduate students (Boren Fellowships). They pay a fixed grant of $8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on the duration of overseas study, and the programme states plainly that the award "is not all-inclusive" and is designed to cover only the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses. In exchange, recipients commit to at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation.
records.best_fit: U.S. citizens aged 18 or over who are matriculated at an accredited U.S. undergraduate or graduate degree programme, can commit 8-52 weeks to overseas study of a Boren-preferred language in a Boren-preferred region, and intend to pursue a federal national-security career.

records.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by IIE-organized regional merit review panels made up of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The panels make recommendations on each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know must be stated in the essays and other application materials. Selection preference is given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.
records.notes: Non-deferrable in practice: recipients must remain matriculated at their U.S. institution for the whole funded period and may not graduate until the award is complete, and overseas programmes must be approved by a Boren Program Advisor before travel. Not renewable as published - the award is a fixed one-time grant tier set by overseas duration, and requests to increase awards above the published maximums are contingent upon availability of funds. No return-home obligation is published; instead recipients must complete at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation, with preference given to a longer-term commitment. Internships conducted during a Boren-funded period may not be remunerated nor conducted with the U.S. or a foreign government, and Boren Fellows may not work as journalists while abroad, even freelance or unpaid. Funding for programme expenses incurred after May 31, 2028 is contingent upon availability and cannot be guaranteed at the time of award.

official_details.description: The Boren Awards are a component of the National Security Education Program (NSEP) that funds the intensive study of language abroad by U.S. undergraduate and graduate students who commit to federal service. Boren Scholarships support undergraduates and Boren Fellowships support graduate students; both require a continuous period of overseas study with at least 15-20 weekly language contact hours. The award is a fixed grant tier determined by duration of overseas study ($8,000 / $12,500 / $25,000) and is explicitly not all-inclusive: the programme states that funding "is designed to cover the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses" and lists a closed set of eligible and ineligible costs.
purpose: The National Security Education Program (NSEP) awards Boren Scholarships and Fellowships to U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study and to federal service
The Boren Awards fund the intensive study of language abroad by U.S. undergraduate or graduate students

The Boren Awards promote long-term linguistic immersion and regional experience; proposed programs of two or more semesters are strongly encouraged and preference is given to programs of at least 25 weeks
The Boren Awards invest in linguistic and cultural knowledge for aspiring federal government employees
One objective of the Boren Scholarship is to expand international educational opportunities for students who have not studied abroad and who may require financial assistance to do so
The Boren Awards award scholarships and fellowships that have launched alumni careers into the federal workforce

official_details.degree_award: Not a degree award. The Boren Awards fund overseas study or research undertaken alongside a U.S. degree programme; recipients must remain matriculated in a U.S. degree programme and may not graduate until the award is complete.
official_details.duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study. Minimum 12 weeks for most applicants; a special exception allows undergraduate STEM majors to propose summer programmes of 8 weeks or longer. Preference is given to 25 weeks or more. 2027-cycle funding may be applied to programmes starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028.
official_details.application_cycle: Annual. The 2027-2028 cycle covers both Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships.
official_details.deadline_central_display: Boren Fellowships: January 20, 2027, 5pm Eastern time. Boren Scholarships: January 27, 2027, 5pm Eastern time.

official_details.funding_label: Boren Scholarships: $8,000 for 8-11 weeks (summer programme, STEM majors only); $12,500 for 12-24 weeks; $25,000 for 25-52 weeks. Boren Fellowships: $12,500 for 12-24 weeks; $25,000 for 25-52 weeks. Regional Flagship Language Initiative: approved summer domestic cost PLUS $12,500 (12-24 weeks overseas) or $25,000 (25-52 weeks overseas).
official_details.tuition_coverage: Approved program tuition and fees are eligible, plus home institution matriculation fees up to $2,500 per semester ($5,000 overall cap). This is reimbursement against a closed list of eligible costs, not a tuition waiver at either institution.
official_details.living_cost_coverage: Room and board (housing and food) and books and supplies are eligible expenses, but the award is capped and the programme states the award "is not all-inclusive".
official_details.travel_coverage: Fly America Act compliant round-trip airfare at the lowest cost unrestricted class (basic economy). The page states explicitly that the Open Skies Agreement does not apply to Boren funding. Visa and visa-related costs, checked luggage (up to 2 bags), local transportation and one flight-change fee related to approved travel or approved date changes are also eligible.
official_details.tuition_rule: Nobody waives tuition. The applicant must remain matriculated at an accredited U.S. institution for the whole funded period, and overseas program tuition and fees plus home-institution matriculation fees (capped) are reimbursable eligible costs against the fixed grant.
official_details.home_tuition_rule: Home-institution obligations continue: Boren Scholars and Fellows must stay matriculated at their U.S. institution and may not graduate until the scholarship or fellowship is complete. selection_criteria: Boren Scholarships criterion 1: Does the applicant provide a clear and compelling explanation of the significance of their overseas destination, region, language, field of study, and overseas study to U.S. national security? Priority organizations (Tier One) are the Departments of War, State, and Homeland Security, as well as the Intelligence Community.

Boren Scholarships criterion 2: Does the applicant demonstrate an understanding of how they might fulfill the one-year federal service requirement and a longer-term commitment to the federal government? Consider the leadership potential the applicant would bring to the federal government.

Boren Scholarships criterion 3: Does the applicant demonstrate a serious commitment to language study, before, during, and after their overseas study? The Boren Awards require a minimum of 15-20 contact hours per week. Does the applicant have realistic expectations for the proficiency level obtainable abroad?

Boren Scholarships criterion 4: Has the applicant proposed a study plan in a preferred overseas destination, region, and language, with a preferred major or field of study, meeting the preferred duration of 25+ weeks? If not, have they made a compelling argument on the basis of U.S. national security?
Boren Scholarships criterion 5: Does the applicant possess the appropriate academic preparation, adaptability, flexibility, and maturity required to succeed abroad?

Boren Fellowships criterion 4 (additional): If proposing research in addition to language study, does the applicant have a comprehensive, clear and feasible overseas plan, with language study being the primary purpose of their overseas plan?
Veteran Preference: Veterans of the U.S. armed forces are encouraged to apply, and selection preference will be given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.

Preference factors: the Boren Awards give preference based on program duration, focus on intensive study of a preferred language in a preferred overseas destination, the applicant's field of study, and applicants with longer-term interest in a federal career.
official_details.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated on these criteria by IIE-organized regional merit review panels consisting of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The regional panels make recommendations for each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know should be stated clearly in the essays and other application materials. Applicants are notified if they have been selected in mid-to-late April.

application_steps: 1. Create a new application at https://apply.iie.org/borenscholarship (Boren Scholarships) or https://apply.iie.org/borenfellowship (Boren Fellowships)
2. Pass the Eligibility Determination section - you must answer all of these questions to unlock the rest of the application

3. Enter personal information (name, permanent and mailing address, email, telephone, sex as it appears on your birth certificate, birthdate, country of residence, veteran/reservist/active-service status)

4. Enter academic information (academic level, degree type, major, GPA, maximum possible GPA, institution location, dates attended/graduation date) and upload an UNOFFICIAL transcript of the current institution
5. List up to three relevant jobs and up to three relevant activities, 50-100 words each

6. Enter programme information: study abroad city, program sponsor, program name, proposed overseas institution, Study Plan Summary (max 250 words), upload the Study Abroad Program Description (max 5 pages), weekly contact hours of formal language acquisition, and any alternate study abroad program
7. Write and submit Essay 1 (National Security, max 800 words) and Essay 2 (Motivation and Public Service Careers, max 800 words for Scholarships / 1000 words for Fellowships)
8. Complete the Language Self-Assessment for the Boren language plus up to four additional languages

9. Complete Additional Information: up to three overseas countries, up to five honours and awards, optional other scholarships, ROTC participation, how you learned about Boren, prior NSEP participation
10. Add recommenders, select the type (Letter of Recommendation or Language Evaluation), and click 'Send to Recommender'
11. Read and agree to the Submission Agreement policies
12. Review the application, fix any errors flagged, and click 'Submit Application'

records.region: United States (applicants must be U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or permanent residents; study must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico)

records.description: The NSF GRFP funds full-time graduate students pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees in NSF-supported STEM fields at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period: a $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow and a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees, so there is no tuition or mandatory-fee cost to the student. There is no post-graduate study service requirement, and fellows may transfer to a different institution after completion of the first fellowship year. Estimated 1,500 awards for the 2027 solicitation (NSF 26-526), pending availability of funds.
records.best_fit: Final-year undergraduates, bachelor's degree holders with no prior graduate degree enrollment, joint bachelor's-master's students in their final undergraduate or first graduate year, and first-year graduate students in their first research-based graduate degree program, who are U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or permanent residents.
records.funding_period: per year for each of three years of support over a five-year fellowship period (plus a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance to the institution, $53,000 total per year of support)
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens, nationals or permanent residents who will enroll full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral STEM program and have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program.
eligibility: At the time of submission, must be a U.S. citizen, national, or a permanent resident ("green-card" holder).
Must intend to enroll or be enrolled full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM.
Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.
Must have declined any previously offered NSF Graduate Research Fellowship by the deadline (if applicable).

Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program according to the institution's academic calendar; non-degree coursework must be clearly identified in the transcript and does not count toward this limit.
Must not be a current NSF employee.

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
An eligible applicant can submit only one application per annual competition.

Fellowships may only be used for an eligible graduate degree program at a nonprofit academic institution accredited in, and having a campus located in, the U.S., its territories, possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
coverage: $37,000 stipend paid to the fellow for each of the three years of financial support.
$16,000 cost-of-education allowance provided to the institution of higher education in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each fellow using the support in a fellowship year.
Access to professional development opportunities and the NSF GRFP community.
Access to supplemental funding to sustain research while on medical leave.
benefits: Five-year award with three years of financial support.
No post-graduate study service requirement.
Access to supplemental funding to sustain research while on medical leave.

The fellowship is portable and can be transferred to a different institution of higher education; fellows can transfer after completion of the first fellowship year.
requirements: Prepare and submit the application in the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov.
Create a Research.gov account to access the module.
Provide accurate personal information: full legal name, mailing address, permanent address, date of birth, high school location, and demographic information.
Select a level (Level 1 undergraduate, or Level 2 graduate) in the application.
Provide the list of institutions, enrollment status, enrollment dates and degree conferred (if applicable) for all degree-granting undergraduate and graduate institutions attended.
Provide significant academic honors, fellowships, scholarships, publications and presentations.
Select the Major Field of Study most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program and research plan; the Major Field of Study determines the application deadline and the reviewers.

Request reference letters in the GRFP Application Module and rank them in order of preference; three reference writer names and contact information are required, and two reference letters must be received by NSF.
Provide a Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement of a maximum of three pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Provide a Graduate Research Plan Statement of a maximum of two pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Reference letters are due before the NSF GRFP application deadlines, by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on the reference letter date in the Notice of Funding Opportunity.
All materials are submitted through the GRFP Application Module; emailed and/or physically mailed applications will not be accepted.
Applications are automatically checked by the GRFP Application Module for compliance with the format requirements; documents that are not compliant will not be accepted by the module.
application_method: Create a Research.gov account if you do not already have one.
Access the GRFP Application Module, which usually opens in July or August.
Enter accurate personal information.
Select your eligibility level (Level 1 or Level 2).
Enter education, work and other experience, including all degree-granting institutions attended.
Upload official undergraduate transcripts in PDF format, and graduate transcripts where applicable.
Select the Major Field of Study and subfield that is most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program and research plan; this fixes your deadline and reviewer panel.

Enter the names, organizational affiliations and email addresses of three reference writers, ranked in order of preference, and submit the request; reference writers are notified by email with instructions.
Draft and upload the Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement (three pages maximum, PDF only).
Draft and upload the Graduate Research Plan Statement (two pages maximum, PDF only).
Receive at least two reference letters by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on October 16, 2026.
Submit the completed application package in the GRFP Application Module by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on the deadline for your Major Field of Study (October 19, 20, 22 or 23, 2026).
Track your application status in the GRFP Application Module; NSF typically notifies applicants in the spring.
records.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure no conflicts of interest. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant, using the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes). Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM.
records.notes: No post-graduate study service requirement. Fellowship funds are awarded to the institution of higher education at which the fellow is enrolled, and the institution is responsible for disbursing the stipend to the fellow; the fellowship is therefore only usable at an eligible accredited nonprofit U.S. institution. The fellowship period is five years with three years of financial support, so fellows must plan for two unfunded years. Fellows may transfer to another institution after completing the first fellowship year. Practice-oriented professional degree programs (medical, dental, law, public health, MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, DDS) are excluded at any time during the fellowship, as are joint science-professional degree programs. Applicants may submit only one application per annual competition, and only in the first year of their first graduate degree program (joint bachelor's-master's students are limited to one application). No clinical or medical-school pathway is eligible.

official_details.description: The purpose of the U.S. National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP) is to help ensure the quality, vitality, and strength of the scientific and engineering workforce of the United States. Since 1952, the program recognizes and supports outstanding graduate students pursuing full-time research-based master's and doctoral degrees in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM. Each Fellowship provides three years of support over a five-year Fellowship period. For each of the three years of support, NSF provides a $37,000 stipend and a $16,000 Cost of Education allowance provided to the institution of higher education (IHE) in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each Fellow using the support in a Fellowship year. While the Fellowship is offered to the individual, the Fellowship funds are awarded to the IHE at which a Fellow is enrolled, and the IHE is responsible for disbursement of the stipend to the Fellow.
purpose: Help ensure the quality, vitality, and strength of the scientific and engineering workforce of the United States.
Support outstanding graduate students in NSF-supported STEM disciplines who are pursuing research-based master's and doctoral degrees at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions of higher education.
Support outstanding graduate students pursuing research-based degrees.
Increase participation in science, technology, education, and mathematics (STEM).
Build the next generation of scientific leaders.
Recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM.
Recognize the potential of individuals based on their demonstrated potential for significant achievements in science and engineering, rather than funding specific projects.
study_type: Full-time enrollment in a research-based graduate degree program
Research-based STEM study in an eligible Major Field of Study
official_details.degree_award: Full graduate degree (research-based master's or doctoral). The GRFP itself is not a degree; the fellowship funds study toward a degree at an eligible institution.
official_details.duration: Five-year award with three years of financial support. $37,000 stipend plus $16,000 cost of education (COE) paid to the institution for each year of funding support; $53,000 each year for three years over a five-year period.
official_details.application_cycle: Annual competition. The GRFP Application Module usually opens in July or August. For the 2027 competition (solicitation NSF 26-526) reference letters are due October 16, 2026 and applications are due October 19-23, 2026 depending on Major Field of Study.
official_details.deadline_central_display: October 16, 2026 by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time (all reference letters due). Application deadlines follow by field of study.
official_details.deadline_institutional: None published. Applications are submitted directly by the applicant in the GRFP Application Module rather than through an institutional office.
official_details.deadline_note: The deadline depends on the applicant's Major Field of Study: October 19, 2026 for Life Sciences; October 20, 2026 for Computer and Information Science and Engineering, Materials Research, Psychology, Social Sciences; October 22, 2026 for Engineering; October 23, 2026 for Chemistry, Geosciences, Mathematical Sciences, Physics and Astronomy. All applications must be received by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the applicable deadline date; the module does not accept applications after the deadline. November 15, 2026 is the last day to withdraw an application and have it not count towards the number of times an individual may apply.
official_details.funding_type: Stipend plus tuition and mandatory fee coverage via cost-of-education allowance
official_details.funding_label: $37,000 stipend + $16,000 cost of education allowance per year, for three years over a five-year fellowship period
official_details.funding_period: per year of funding support (three years of support within a five-year fellowship period); $53,000 total per year including the COE allowance
official_details.tuition_coverage: Full tuition and mandatory fees. NSF provides a $16,000 Cost of Education allowance to the institution of higher education in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each Fellow using the support in a fellowship year. The COE payment covers all tuition and mandatory fees (no cost to student).
official_details.living_cost_coverage: A $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow for each of the three years of financial support. The pages read do not publish a separate housing, meals or books allowance.
official_details.tuition_rule: The $16,000 cost-of-education allowance is provided to the institution of higher education (IHE) in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each fellow using the support in a fellowship year, so there is no tuition or mandatory-fee cost to the student. Because the fellowship is offered to the individual but the funds are awarded to the IHE, the institution is responsible for disbursement of the stipend to the fellow.
official_details.host_institution_fee: No fee payable to the host is published. The cost-of-education allowance is paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees.
covered_expenses: All tuition and mandatory fees, through the $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution of higher education.
A $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow for each of the three years of support.
not_covered_or_excluded: The fellowship period is five years but only three years carry financial support, so fellows must fund two years of the fellowship period themselves.
No published coverage for health insurance, room and board, books, computers, or travel on the pages read; these costs must be met from the $37,000 stipend or other sources.
No international or overseas travel or placement funding is published.
Practice-oriented professional degrees are excluded entirely (medical, dental, law, public health, MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, DDS).
GRE scores are not part of the application and are not funded or required.
Applicants cannot obtain copies of past successful applications from NSF.
benefits: Access to professional development opportunities and the NSF GRFP community.
Access to supplemental funding to sustain research while on medical leave.
No post-graduate study service requirement.
Portability: the fellowship can be transferred to a different institution of higher education; fellows can transfer to another institution after completion of the first fellowship year.
Reputation and network effects: GRFP alumni include over 40 Nobel Prize recipients and over 450 members of the National Academy of Sciences.
eligibility: At the time of submission, must be a U.S. citizen, national, or a permanent resident ("green-card" holder).
Must intend to enroll or be enrolled full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM.
Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.
Must have declined any previously offered NSF Graduate Research Fellowship by the deadline (if applicable).

Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program according to the institution's academic calendar; non-degree coursework must be clearly identified in the transcript and does not count toward this limit.
Must not be a current NSF employee.

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
An eligible applicant can submit only one application per annual competition.

Select the Major Field of Study and subfield most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program of study and research plan; if a subfield is not listed in the Appendix of the Notice of Funding Opportunity, it is not eligible.
Interdisciplinary research is allowed, but the application is reviewed based on the first Major Field of Study selected.

By signing and submitting the application, the applicant certifies meeting the NSF GRFP eligibility criteria; willful provision of false information is a criminal offense under U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001.
general_eligibility: One application per annual competition.
Full-time enrollment in an eligible research-based graduate degree program.
U.S. citizenship, nationality or permanent residency required.

The applicant questionnaire on the eligibility page is a tool only and is not an official determination of an individual's eligibility; the Notice of Funding Opportunity contains the official eligibility guidelines.
ineligibility_conditions: Individuals who are not U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, or permanent residents, including foreign nationals in the U.S. on a student visa and those awaiting green cards.
Individuals who do not intend to enroll or be enrolled in a research-based graduate degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM.
Individuals who have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship offer.
Individuals who were awarded the fellowship and did not notify NSF of their intention to accept or decline by the published deadline for accepting the fellowship.
Individuals who have previously applied while enrolled in a degree-granting graduate program.
Individuals who have earned a master's, doctoral, or terminal degree in any field.
Individuals who are current NSF employees.

Individuals who will be enrolled in a practice-oriented professional degree program such as medical, dental, law, and public health degrees at any time during the fellowship, including but not limited to MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, and DDS programs.

Individuals who plan to pursue a joint science-professional degree program (such as an MD/Ph.D. or JD/Ph.D.) even if proposing to use the GRFP only for the Ph.D. part; also applicants enrolled in, or planning to enroll in, a graduate degree program while on a leave of absence from a professional degree program or professional degree-graduate degree joint program.

Applicants who completed more than one academic year of graduate study: all enrollment in graduate degree-granting programs counts toward the limit regardless of field of study, including study in non-NSF-supported fields.
Applicants who hold a master's degree, even if in the first year of a Ph.D. program.
Applicants whose statement documents are not compliant with the published formatting requirements: documents that are not compliant will not be accepted by the GRFP Application Module.
Applications submitted after the deadline, or submitted by email or physical mail, are not accepted.
official_details.citizenship_residency: U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, or permanent resident ("green-card") holders only. Foreign nationals on student visas and those awaiting green cards are not eligible. The degree program must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
official_details.international_eligibility: None. The program is restricted to U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals and permanent residents studying at accredited nonprofit institutions with a campus in the U.S., its territories or possessions, or Puerto Rico.

undergraduate: Level 1: Undergraduate students in the final (senior) year of a bachelor's degree program.
Level 1: Bachelor's degree holders with no enrollment in a graduate degree program (non-degree graduate coursework allowed).

No restrictions on the number of times an undergraduate senior in a bachelor's degree program, or a bachelor's degree holder with no prior graduate degree enrollment, can apply before enrolling in a graduate degree-granting program.
masters: Level 2: Joint bachelor's-master's degree students in the final undergraduate or first graduate year; they must be in the final undergraduate or first graduate year of the joint degree program as of the application deadline.
Joint bachelor's-master's degree students are considered graduate students and can apply only once.
First-year graduate students in their first graduate degree program with less than one academic year completed in the degree program may apply (a research-based master's degree program is eligible).
Applicants who have earned a master's degree in any field are not eligible.
phd: Level 2: First-year graduate students in their first graduate degree program with less than one academic year completed according to the institution's academic calendar.
Individuals enrolled in graduate degree programs can apply only once, in the first year of their first graduate program.
Doctoral students who have completed more than one academic year of graduate study, or who previously earned a master's, doctoral or terminal degree, are not eligible.

host_requirements: The institution must be a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
The Fellowship funds are awarded to the institution of higher education at which the Fellow is enrolled, and the IHE is responsible for disbursement of the stipend to the Fellow.
The fellowship may be transferred to a different institution of higher education, and fellows can transfer after completion of the first fellowship year.
Recipients are covered by the GRFP Administrative Guide for fellows and coordinating officials.
requirements: Prepare and submit the application in the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov; the module usually opens in July or August.
Create a Research.gov account if you do not already have one.
Provide accurate personal information: full legal name, mailing address, permanent address, date of birth, high school location, demographic information.
Select Level 1 (Undergraduate) or Level 2 (Graduate) in the application.
Provide the list of institutions, enrollment status, enrollment dates and degree conferred (if applicable) for all degree-granting undergraduate and graduate institutions attended.
Provide significant academic honors, fellowships, scholarships, publications and presentations.
Select the Major Field of Study, which determines the application deadline and the reviewing panel.

Request up to five reference letters and rank them in order of preference; three reference writer names and contact information are required and two letters must be received. Family members cannot be reference writers. Reference writers are notified by email of the request along with instructions.
Prepare the Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts, maximum three pages.

Prepare the Graduate Research Plan Statement with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts, maximum two pages; it should include the research idea and proposed approach, resources needed, potential to advance knowledge, and potential to benefit society.
Both statements must be in PDF format and comply with the page size, margin, font and spacing requirements.
Submit only through the GRFP Application Module; emailed and/or physically mailed applications will not be accepted.
You may revise your application until the deadline, but can make no changes after the deadline passes.
documents: Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement (maximum three pages).
Graduate Research Plan (maximum two pages).
Official undergraduate academic transcripts.
Graduate transcripts, if applicable; these may be unofficial if the institution of higher education does not provide official transcripts for first-year, first-academic-term graduate students.

Two reference letters (two must be received by NSF for the application to be reviewed; the module permits requesting up to five, and only the top three are considered if more than three are received).
Three reference writer names and contact information.
Completed application package.
document_format_rules: PDF format only for the statement documents.
Official transcripts should be uploaded in PDF format.

Page limits: Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement three pages; Graduate Research Plan two pages. The page limits include all references, citations, charts, figures, images, and lists of publications and presentations.
Page size: standard 8.5" x 11" page size.

Margins: 1" margins on all sides, with no text inside the 1" margins (no header, footer, name, or page number). Remove page numbers; stray images or shapes can violate the margin rule even when the page margin is set to 1 inch.

Fonts: Arial (not Arial Narrow), Courier New, or Palatino Linotype in 10-point or larger; Times New Roman or Computer Modern family, 11-point or larger. Symbol or Cambria Math fonts are accepted for Greek letters or special characters. Smaller than 10-point fonts are accepted for mathematical formulas, equations, figures, tables or diagram captions.
Spacing: no less than single-spacing (approximately 6 lines per inch). Do not use line spacing options such as "exactly 11 point," that are less than single spaced.
Equations and symbols should be inserted as a non-editable image to bypass compliance checking and avoid font type and size errors.
Provide descriptive alternative text (alt text) for all images, graphs and charts, and use sufficient colour contrast for legibility.
Do not include links to supplemental materials (papers, videos); reviewers are instructed to evaluate only the evidence provided within the application.

Google Docs may not properly export bulleted text and should not be used; OpenOffice inserts an unallowable font for superscripts and subscripts; certain LaTeX-generated PDF elements are not yet supported and LaTeX fonts in formulas are not supported; Microsoft Word 2007 or earlier may produce font errors.
In Microsoft Office, "Select All" does not include inserted images, shapes, numbered lists or bullets, which carry their own fonts and must be updated to accepted fonts and sizes.
If text is inside an image, it must be part of the image and not editable, otherwise font errors can result.
Do not use 'Print as PDF'; use 'Export' / 'Create PDF'. On Mac, avoid 'Save as PDF' set to 'Best for Printing'; choose 'Best for electronic distribution and accessibility'.
To check fonts: open the PDF, right click the document content, select 'Document Properties', open the 'Fonts' tab and review the font types.
Blank pages within a PDF cause upload errors; export the PDF to Word, delete the blank page and re-save as PDF.
Applications are automatically checked by the GRFP Application Module for compliance; documents that are not compliant will not be accepted.
selection_criteria: Intellectual Merit: the potential to advance knowledge.
Broader Impacts: the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
official_details.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers, and experts in STEM fields. Reviewers are selected by NSF Program Officers charged with oversight of the review process, and care is taken to ensure that reviewers have no conflicts of interest with the applicants. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study the applicant selected, using all available information in the completed application. Intellectual Merit factors may include the applicant's ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as a part of a team, interpret and communicate research (e.g. through publications or presentations), take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors may include the likelihood that the applicant's activities will increase participation in STEM, improve STEM education in schools through outreach and mentoring, increase public scientific literacy and public engagement with STEM through community outreach, increase collaboration among academia, industry and other types of organizations, improve education and educator development at any level in STEM, improve the well-being of individuals in society, develop a globally competitive STEM workforce, improve national security, increase the economic competitiveness of the U.S., and enhance infrastructure for research and education. NSF does not provide past applications or statements. GRFP funds people, not specific projects; the plan demonstrates potential, not a binding commitment. The program is highly competitive. NSF typically notifies applicants in the spring. Estimated number of awards under the 2027 solicitation: 1500, pending availability of funds.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a U.S. citizen, U.S. national or permanent resident; if not, stop — this programme excludes student visa holders and green-card pending applicants.
Confirm you have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree-granting programme, or that you have never enrolled in one.
Confirm you hold no master's, doctoral or terminal degree in any field.

Confirm you are not entering or currently enrolled in a practice-oriented professional degree (MD, JD, MPH, MBA, MSW, DVM, DDS, public health, dental or law) at any point during the fellowship, and are not planning an MD/Ph.D. or JD/Ph.D.
Confirm you have never applied to the GRFP while enrolled in a degree-granting graduate programme, and that this is your only GRFP application this cycle.
Create or locate your Research.gov account before the module opens.

Agree your Major Field of Study with your adviser before you start writing, because it fixes your deadline and your reviewer panel; check the Appendix of the NSF 26-526 Notice of Funding Opportunity for eligible subfields, since an unlisted subfield is ineligible.
Order official undergraduate transcripts early and have them ready as PDF.
Ask three potential referees for their agreement before the cycle, and confirm none of them is a family member.
Draft both statements against the official DOCX templates from the beginning, not at the end.
Leave time for at least two reference letters to arrive before October 16, 2026, 8:00 p.m. Eastern time — referees are contacted by email by the module, not by you attaching letters.
important_advice_for_students: Start from the official templates linked on the How to Apply page; the module runs automated compliance checks on page count, margins and fonts, and non-compliant documents are rejected rather than flagged.
Do not use Google Docs for the statements — NSF states it may not properly export bulleted text — and do not use 'Print as PDF' in Microsoft Office; use 'Export'/'Create PDF'.
Insert equations, formulas and special symbols as non-editable images rather than relying on Cambria Math or Symbol fonts.
Strip all page numbers, headers and footers, and check that inserted images or shapes do not break the 1-inch margin.
Decide your Major Field of Study once and check the deadline calendar against it, rather than assuming a single closing date.
Do not waste time hunting for past successful applications — NSF does not provide them.
Do not submit by email or post; the module is the only accepted route.
Budget for the fact that the fellowship period is five years but only three years are funded; the $37,000 stipend must also absorb books, equipment and any uninsured health costs.
Attend the NSF GRFP applicant webinars and office hours if you can — several were held in September 2026 for this cycle.
Submit well before 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on your deadline day; the module will not accept late applications.
common_rejection_risks: Ineligible status: not a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident; on a student visa; awaiting a green card.
Ineligible academic level: more than one academic year completed in a graduate degree-granting programme, or a previous master's degree in any field.
Enrolment in, or plan to enter, a practice-oriented professional degree, or a joint science-professional degree such as MD/Ph.D. or JD/Ph.D.
A second application in the same annual competition, or a prior application made while enrolled in a degree-granting graduate programme.

Blank pages in the uploaded PDF, which trigger upload errors.
Fewer than two reference letters received by the reference letter deadline — the application can be submitted but will not be reviewed.
Selecting a Major Field of Study whose subfield is not listed in the Notice of Funding Opportunity Appendix, which makes the research topic ineligible.
Including external links to supplemental material, which reviewers are instructed to ignore.
Missing the field-specific deadline or submitting after 8:00 p.m. Eastern time; the module does not accept late submissions.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Two of the five fellowship years carry no financial support.
Room and board, books, supplies, computers and equipment — not itemised as covered on the pages read; expected to come out of the $37,000 stipend.
Health insurance, where not provided by the institution.
Any travel, conference or relocation costs, for which no published coverage exists.
Fees the institution may charge that are not mandatory fees covered by the cost-of-education allowance — confirm with the institution.
Application costs are nil, but any costs of obtaining official transcripts.

Meet the programme's expectation of contributing to breakthrough discovery, technological innovation and national security, STEM outreach and mentorship, and U.S. economic competitiveness.

records.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review conducted by the AEF Programme to verify applicant eligibility and ensure all required materials have been provided; only applications meeting all requirements are advanced for merit-based evaluation. Merit review is a thorough, consistent and objective examination by evaluators who must be independent of the applicants and of the sponsoring agencies, applying pre-established criteria in four areas: the applicant's teaching experience, professional accomplishments, demonstrated leadership qualities, and interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Programme. Sponsoring federal agencies then review the highly reviewed applications on overall professional experience and demonstrated leadership qualities, the applicant's interest in and preparedness for the fellowship, alignment of the applicant's experience and subject matter expertise with the interests of the host office, and quality of recommendations, and select the top candidates as semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC. Semi-finalists are invited to Washington, DC for three days of individual interviews and information sessions. Following interviews, final selections are made at the discretion of the sponsoring federal agencies; finalists are contacted by ORISE regarding offers. DOE selects the finalists for Congressional office placements. Recruitment and selection is done without regard to race, gender, age, colour, religion, national origin, mental or physical disability, or status as a veteran.
records.notes: Not deferrable and not renewable: the fellowship is for a single eleven-month period from mid-August with initial programme Orientation, and there is no flexibility in start and end dates. There is no return-home requirement, but relocation to the Washington, DC area is a programme requirement if the Fellow does not already live there. The Fellow cannot maintain a teaching position while serving; a leave of absence must be secured or employment terminated. The AEF Programme does not arrange housing. Fellows receive a monthly stipend and are not considered employees of the hosting office, so they do not earn sick or annual leave, although up to ten personal days and ten sick days are allowed without stipend reduction. All stipends are reportable to the Internal Revenue Service and the AEF Programme does not withhold taxes; fellows may need to file Form 1040-ES and pay estimated income tax. Current and former AEF Fellows are not eligible to apply for a second fellowship. No clinical restriction is published.

official_details.description: The Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program provides a unique opportunity for accomplished K-12 educators in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) to serve in the national education arena. Fellows spend eleven months working in Federal agencies or in U.S. Congressional offices, applying their extensive knowledge and classroom experiences to national education program and/or education policy efforts. At the end of the Fellowship, educators are equipped with access to a national network of education leaders and programs, a better understanding of the challenges and possibilities in STEM education, and a renewed passion for teaching, ready to make significant contributions to the educational community. The Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship Act (Fellowship Act Public Law 103-382, Improving America's Schools Act of 1994) was signed into law in November 1994 and gives the DOE the responsibility for managing the program. The DOE Office of Science's Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS) manages this program for DOE in collaboration with the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) and other partners.
purpose: Provide a unique opportunity for accomplished K-12 educators in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) to serve in the national education arena.

Support the intellectual and professional development of K-12 STEM teachers who have the desire to share their education and classroom expertise with Federal agencies and U.S. Congressional offices.

Advance national K-12 STEM education through contributions to programme design, legislation and policy, federal agency partnerships, web-based science education tools, and evaluation of national and regional school reform and teacher preparation programmes.
Inspire the next generation of scientific and technological leaders by strengthening K-12 STEM teaching.

Complete the eleven-month full-time appointment (mid-August through mid-July) in Washington, DC.
Meet the Terms and Conditions in the offer letter of appointment, including requirements for ethical conduct and financial disclosure and conflict of interest.
Participate in the official professional development meetings, conferences, field trips, etc., organized for Fellows by the AEF Program.
Have health care coverage during the Fellowship appointment; Fellows are eligible to participate in the ORISE health insurance plan if they do not have other coverage.
Establish an individual Professional Development Plan for the year, which must be completed by early October.
Submit the requested written reports, presentations, and surveys related to the Fellowship experience before the published deadlines.
Represent themselves as educators in a responsible and professional manner.
Only use the AEF Program name or the Fellow's affiliation with the AEF Program in an authorized manner.
Give priority to the duties assigned by the host office when managing fellowship responsibilities.
Comply with all legal and ethical requirements subject to the individual appointment, including ORISE ethics guidance for DOE sponsored Fellows.
arrival_rules: Fellows arrive in Washington, DC in mid-August 2027; the fellowship begins on the third Monday in August with the initial program Orientation.
Semi-finalists must travel to Washington, DC on Saturday February 27, 2027 for orientation on Sunday February 28 and interviews on Monday March 1 and possibly Tuesday March 2.
Candidates selected for a Congressional office placement return to Washington, DC for one week in June 2027 for placement interviews.

Relocation to the Washington, DC area is required if the Fellow does not already reside there. Relocation expenses are reimbursed up to $3,500 for inbound and outbound movement when the distance is more than 50 miles one way. Housing is not arranged by the AEF Program; resources and connections to outgoing Fellows are provided.
Candidates who accept a Congressional fellowship appointment must relocate for the June-July time frame of placement interviews as well as for the fellowship year.
There is no flexibility in start and end dates.
timeline_rules: Online application opens August 3, 2026.
Application deadline 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026.
Completion of notifications to selected semi-finalists, with travel arrangements made for interviews in Washington, DC: February 24, 2027.
Interviews in Washington, DC: February 27 - March 1, 2027 (semi-finalists travel Saturday February 27; orientation Sunday February 28; interviews Monday March 1 and possibly Tuesday March 2).
Finalist notifications: March 9, 2027.
Congressional Fellows placement interviews: mid-June 2027.
Fellows arrive in Washington, DC: mid-August 2027.
Orientation meeting for the 2026-2027 AEF Program Fellows: August 23-26, 2027.
Individual Professional Development Plan must be completed by early October during the fellowship year.
AEF Virtual Office Hours are held at 7pm EST on August 26, September 9, September 23, October 7, October 14, October 21, October 28, November 4 and November 11, 2026.
Fellows are expected to observe the federal holidays recognised by the hosting site, and to attend the official twice monthly professional development opportunities.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you will hold U.S. citizenship by the November 5, 2026 deadline; naturalising later does not help.
Confirm you will have completed five full years of full-time classroom teaching by the deadline, excluding student teaching and assistant teaching.
Confirm at least five of your last seven years were full-time STEM teaching in a U.S. public or private elementary or secondary school.
Confirm you are currently employed full-time in a U.S. K-12 school or school district right now.

Line up a school district official today - principal, superintendent, deputy/assistant superintendent, or school board member qualify; department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals and vice-principals do not.
Secure your school's or district's agreement to an eleven-month leave of absence, starting mid-August 2027, because you cannot hold your post while serving.
Create your online application account now and submit your three recommendation requests immediately; do not wait until your essays are finished.
Draft all five essay responses offline in Word, spell-check, then paste into the system, because it logs you out after 60 minutes.
Budget for Washington, DC living costs against the $8,200 monthly stipend and start housing research early, because the programme does not arrange housing.
Register for the AEF Virtual Office Hours at 7pm EST on one of the remaining autumn dates if you have questions.
important_advice_for_students: This is not a graduate scholarship and not a degree programme; it is an eleven-month paid appointment that ends your teaching job for a year, so treat it as a career decision rather than funding for study.
Do not count on it for tuition - there is no tuition element whatsoever.
Do not assume housing is covered; the programme explicitly does not arrange housing, and only $3,500 of relocation is reimbursed for moves over 50 miles one way.
Request your three recommendations first, not last; once a letter is received it cannot be removed, and all three must be in the system by the deadline.
Save your essay text locally before pasting, because the system times out after 60 minutes and unsaved work is lost.
Check your Check Your Status page yourself; the programme does not email you about missing components.
Prepare for interview travel; semi-finalists fund their own trip to Washington, DC in late February, and the $5,000 travel allowance is a fellowship benefit, not an application reimbursement.
Plan for federal ethics and financial disclosure compliance once in the role; the appointment carries 10 CFR Part 1010 and 5 CFR Part 2635 obligations.
Track the three-applications-in-six-years cap carefully, because a rejected application is not kept on file for the following year.
common_rejection_risks: Not a U.S. citizen by the deadline; a pending naturalisation does not qualify.
Fewer than five completed years of full-time classroom teaching, or relying on student teaching or assistant teaching to reach five years.
Fewer than five of the last seven years spent teaching STEM full-time in a U.S. K-12 school.
Not currently employed full-time in a U.S. public or private elementary or secondary school or school district, for example teaching abroad this year.
Recommendation set that does not include a qualifying school district official, or one that includes only department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals or vice-principals.
Incomplete application at the deadline: any missing field, essay, or letter of recommendation means the application is not considered, and uploaded materials are the sole basis for evaluation.
Recommendation letters sent by mail or email instead of through the online system; WDTS does not accept them.
Applying more than three times within a six year period, or applying as a current or former Fellow.
Inability to secure an eleven-month leave of absence or to relocate to Washington, DC for the full appointment.
A final letter arriving after 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing in the Washington, DC area, which the AEF Program does not arrange or fund beyond a capped $3,500 relocation reimbursement.
Any health insurance cost above the $550/month individual or $1,300/month family stipend, including the cost of joining the ORISE health insurance plan.
Federal, state and local income tax on the stipend and allowances; the program does not withhold and fellows may need Form 1040-ES quarterly payments.
Personal and professional travel beyond the $5,000 host-agency travel allowance, including the applicant's own trip for semi-finalist interviews.
Professional development spending beyond the $1,000 education allowance.
School or district pension and benefits contributions that stop during the leave of absence, and any loss of seniority, which the programme does not compensate.
Relocation costs if the distance is 50 miles one way or less, or above the $3,500 cap.
Costs of maintaining or terminating employment arrangements at the home school.
Any dependent or partner costs beyond the family-plan health insurance stipend.
document_audit: Online application fields: contact information; education background (formal education and continuing education); teaching and professional experience; professional awards and recognition; citizenship status; interest in Federal Agency and/or Congressional Office placement. Every field must be complete by the deadline.
Five essay questions: responses must be typed into the online system. Draft offline and paste in, because the system logs out after 60 minutes of inactivity.

Three letters of recommendation, submitted electronically by the recommenders. Mailed or emailed letters are not accepted. A letter already received cannot be removed; a recommender can be swapped only until they submit.

At least one letter must be from a school district official - school principal, district superintendent, deputy or assistant superintendent, district board of education member, or equivalent. Department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals and vice-principals do not qualify. At an independent school, a headmaster/headmistress or equivalent senior executive qualifies: select 'Other' in the Type drop-down and type the position title in the Other District Official box.
For personal references such as a parent of a student, select 'Non-District Non-School Official' in the Type drop-down.
Proof of U.S. citizenship is not part of the application package but must be provided upon accepting a Fellowship offer.
No transcript, test score, publication list, or file-format/size specification is published for this application; only the essays and recommendation letters are required.
Retain a copy of your submitted application and of your essay drafts; applications are kept on record for the current year only and are not carried over.

referee_tracking.instructions: Must be a school principal, district superintendent, deputy or assistant superintendent, district board of education member, or equivalent. Department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals and vice-principals do not qualify. At an independent school with no district structure, a headmaster/headmistress or equivalent senior executive qualifies; select 'Other' in the Type drop-down and enter the position title in the Other District Official text box. The recommender receives a unique URL by email and must submit through the online system before the deadline; you cannot view or remove the letter once submitted.

Should be individuals familiar with the applicant's professional and education background and their experience, aptitude or promise relevant to the AEF Program. Select the appropriate Type option in the Request Recommendations drop-down (for example 'Non-District Non-School Official' for personal references). Each recommender receives instructions by email and submits online before 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026.

Fellowship offers begin and finalists are contacted by email and phone by ORISE. Keep your contact details current in the application and respond quickly, as the decision window is limited.

submission_workflow: Create your account in the online application system.
Immediately submit requests for three recommendations, including one qualifying school district official, since requests can be made before the application is complete.
Confirm each recommender received the email with a unique submission URL and that their Type option is correct.
Complete contact information, education background, teaching and professional experience, professional awards and recognition, citizenship status and placement interest.
Draft the five essays offline in word processing software, save, spell-check, and paste into the application.
Periodically check the Check Your Status page for completeness and for received recommendations; resend reminder emails where needed.
Submit the application before 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026 and confirm your status shows everything received.
Save a local copy of your essays and your submitted application for your records.
If selected as a semi-finalist, book travel to Washington, DC for February 27, 2027 and attend orientation and interviews.
If selected as a finalist, respond promptly to the ORISE offer and, where relevant, arrange the mid-June return for congressional placement interviews.
post_award_requirements: Provide proof of U.S. citizenship upon accepting the Fellowship offer.
Secure a leave of absence from teaching for the full fellowship year; it is not possible to maintain a teaching position while serving as a Fellow.
Complete the eleven-month full-time appointment in Washington, DC, from mid-August through mid-July, starting on the third Monday in August with Orientation.
Give priority to the duties assigned by the host office and represent yourself as an educator in a responsible and professional manner.

Meet the terms and conditions in the offer letter, including ethical conduct, financial disclosure and conflict of interest, and comply with 10 CFR Part 1010 and 5 CFR Part 2635 for DOE-sponsored Fellows.
Maintain health care coverage for the duration of the appointment, using the ORISE plan if you have no other coverage.
Establish an individual Professional Development Plan and complete it by early October, using the $1,000 education allowance within that plan with prior approval.
Attend the official twice monthly professional development meetings and other AEF Program organised meetings, conferences and field trips.
Submit the requested written reports, presentations and surveys before the published deadlines.
Request and receive pre-approval from the AEF Program for any travel before making arrangements, and use only the authorised form of the AEF Program name and affiliation.
Relocate to the Washington, DC area if required, and submit allowable relocation expenses for reimbursement within the $3,500 cap.
There is no return-home obligation and the fellowship cannot be deferred or renewed; a second fellowship is not permitted.
