records.name: Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) Program
records.official_source: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS), administered with Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE)
records.region: United States (applicants must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents and enrolled at a U.S. accredited college or university; host is a participating DOE national laboratory or facility)
records.duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months of research at a DOE laboratory/facility, within a project period bounded by published earliest and latest start dates
records.deadline: Applications are due November 4, 2026, at 5:00PM ET. This is 2026 Solicitation 2. The online application system closes at 5:00 PM Eastern Time and no additional materials will be accepted after it. 2027 Solicitation 1 dates are published but all tentative: application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027.
records.application_period: 2026 Solicitation 2: online application opened August 12, 2026 and closes 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026. Offer notifications April 1 - 16, 2027. Proposed project periods may start as early as June 7, 2027 and must start no later than October 4, 2027. 2027 Solicitation 1 (tentative): application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027, offers September 2027, project periods starting November 2027 and ending no later than March 2028.
records.description: SCGSR provides supplemental awards to thesis-based doctoral students to conduct part of their dissertation research at a DOE national laboratory or facility, in collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist, in a DOE Office of Science priority research area. Awardees receive a monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 while at the host laboratory, plus up to $3,000 total for inbound and outbound transportation if the host laboratory is more than 50 miles from their home graduate institution. The award does not pay tuition or fees, does not cover supplies and materials, and does not cover travel during the project; the student must remain enrolled full-time at their home institution and keep paying their own tuition. Successful applicants are considered guest scientists at the host laboratory, not employees.
records.best_fit: Full-time U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents who have already obtained Ph.D. candidacy with an approved thesis topic, are enrolled in a thesis-based research Ph.D. in a DOE-supported STEM field at an accredited U.S. institution, and can arrange a 3 to 12 month in-person research residency with a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist at a participating laboratory.
records.funding_period: per month during the award period (up to $3,600), plus up to $3,000 total inbound and outbound travel reimbursement per award
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents aged 18 or older, full-time enrolled in a qualified thesis-based Ph.D. programme in a DOE-supported STEM field, have obtained Ph.D. candidacy with an approved thesis topic, and secure a collaborating scientist at a participating DOE national laboratory.
eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age at the time of applying.
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a Qualified Graduate Program with the Ph.D. as their degree objective.
At the time of application, applicants must have obtained the Ph.D. candidacy at their home institution, and must have established a defined graduate thesis project and graduate thesis advisor.
The applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor must provide a Letter of Support.

Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
The Ph.D. degree program pursued must require a research thesis/dissertation, with an emphasis on fundamental experimental or theoretical research.

Applicants must demonstrate that their graduate thesis research is in an area of fundamental research aligned with the DOE Office of Science Priority Research Areas identified for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2.
The applicant and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for identifying a collaborating research scientist at a DOE laboratory and jointly developing the research proposal.
Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientists may be from any of the participating DOE national laboratories/facilities.
The duration of the proposed research to be conducted at the DOE laboratory/facility may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.
For applications in BES priority research areas, eligibility depends also on proximity between the applicant's university and the host DOE national laboratory.
Applicants must remain enrolled as a full-time graduate student in a qualified graduate program during the duration of the proposed SCGSR research project period at the host DOE laboratory/facility.
coverage: A monthly stipend in the amount of up to $3,600 for general living expenses while at the host DOE laboratory/facility during the award period.

Reimbursement for in-bound and out-bound transportation to the host DOE laboratory/facility, limited to a total travel benefit of up to $3,000 per award, available only if the host DOE national laboratory/facility is greater than 50 miles from the awardee's home graduate institution.
The opportunity, after receiving the award, to apply for further funding to conduct a brief (6 weeks maximum) research visit to select research institutions abroad, such as CERN or RIKEN.
benefits: Access to DOE national laboratory expertise, user facilities, instrumentation and leadership-class computing systems.
Professional network expansion and access to scientific user facilities not available at most universities.
The possible opportunity for a short international research visit of 6 weeks maximum to an institution such as CERN or RIKEN, applied for after the award is received.
Weekly virtual office hours and application assistance workshops offered by the SCGSR Program.
A running list of collaborating laboratory scientists who are ready to work with SCGSR awardees.
requirements: All applications must be completed through the online application system; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for review.
Materials uploaded into the online application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Complete all required fields: Contact Information; Academic Information including Current Graduate Program Information; Citizenship or Permanent Residency Status; Professional Information such as Scientific Publications and Awards; Graduate Thesis Advisor and Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist Contact Information.

Submit the SCGSR research proposal, co-developed by the applicant and the collaborating DOE laboratory research scientist in consultation with the primary graduate thesis advisor, as a PDF through the online application.
Upload a PDF copy of current official graduate transcripts.
Provide official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as an official, signed letter from the Registrar's office or from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of the applicant's academic department.
Submit two Letters of Support, one from the primary graduate thesis advisor and one from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, both completed through the online application system.
Indicate in the online application system which Office of Science priority research area the proposed project aligns with.
List citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, in the appropriate section of the online application; do not submit supplemental materials.

The research proposal must address the stated aims in at least one of the SCGSR Priority Research Areas and must identify how the proposed research will take advantage of the DOE laboratory/facility's research capabilities and assets.

The proposed research must be an integral part of the applicant's overall doctoral thesis project and must be approved by the primary graduate thesis advisor, whose approval is made through the thesis advisor's Letter of Support.
Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline and become familiar with the application information requested.
application_method: Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline.
Review the eligibility rules, priority research areas and merit review criteria before writing anything.

Identify a collaborating research scientist at a participating DOE national laboratory or facility, or ask the SCGSR Program Manager or the laboratory point of contact for candidates, and agree the project scope with them.
Consult your primary graduate thesis advisor and confirm Ph.D. candidacy, an approved thesis topic, and that the proposed laboratory work is part of your thesis project.
Obtain official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as a signed letter from the Registrar or the Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies, including the date of thesis committee approval of your topic.
Obtain your official graduate transcript stamped with the university seal, and redact Social Security numbers and dates of birth while keeping your name visible.

Co-develop the research proposal with the collaborating scientist, in consultation with your thesis advisor, addressing the stated aims of at least one priority research area and identifying how the laboratory's capabilities and assets will be used; keep it to three pages plus a one-page reference list.

Ensure both your thesis advisor and the collaborating scientist review and approve the final proposal PDF before uploading it, because they receive an automatic notification when you upload or update it.

Enter your thesis advisor's contact information under 'Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor Information' and the collaborating scientist's contact information under 'Host DOE Laboratory', then use 'Send Email' on the Request Letters of Support tab to send both requests.
Monitor the receipt of both letters of support through the online system and send reminder emails where needed.
Review and print or export your application as a PDF using the 'Print your Application' option before submitting.

Submit the complete application, including transcripts, proof of candidacy, research proposal and both letters of support, by 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026, and confirm the Status page shows 'Submitted'.
If selected, respond to the DOE Office of Science notification promptly; you will be given about a week to decide whether to accept.
records.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review. All eligible and compliant applications are then reviewed externally by subject matter experts in the field of the proposed research, using the DOE Office of Science's standard merit review processes. Two merit review criteria apply: (1) Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research, asking whether the research is well-conceived with a clear understanding of the scientific and technical challenges, whether the method and approach are appropriate, whether the graduate student is sufficiently well prepared, and whether DOE laboratory resources are adequate, including whether necessary access to a scientific user facility has been secured by the collaborating scientist; and (2) Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training, asking whether the proposed research can make a significant contribution to the applicant's thesis project and whether it will enhance the applicant's graduate training and research skills. Applications are selected for award based on the results of peer review and other program policy factors, including availability of funds and balance of portfolio. The application materials received, including the research proposal, provide the sole basis for evaluation. Participation in other DOE programmes is collected for internal purposes only and does not affect selection.
records.notes: Not deferrable in the ordinary sense, but the award period may be changed under exceptional circumstances, such as unexpected schedule changes at scientific user facilities, with the support of both the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist and the primary graduate thesis advisor; such requests must reach the SCGSR Program Manager at least 20 business days in advance with signed consent letters from both, and the overall project period must remain the same length as proposed. Cumulative SCGSR award periods across all awards may not exceed 12 months. The award is not an internship and not a full graduate fellowship: the SCGF programme, which provided a stipend and tuition support for up to three years, is no longer accepting applications. Awardees are not employees of the host laboratory or DOE and are not entitled to employee benefits. Regular travel between the host laboratory and the university during the award period violates the terms and conditions, because a full-time schedule at the host is required during normal laboratory business hours; awardees may observe the host's holidays but must report any expected interruption to the collaborating scientist and the SCGSR Program Manager. Awardees become ineligible if, after applying, they accept a separate non-SCGSR appointment from the host laboratory, such as an hourly paid intern or a full-time or temporary position. Medical research, or biological research on model systems for the purpose of understanding disease or pathogens, is not eligible, which excludes clinical and medical-degree routes; joint MD/PhD, joint JD/PhD, DVM, MBA, MD, JD and joint BS/MS programmes are all ineligible. Published work based on the research should carry the SCGSR acknowledgement statement, including contract number DE-SC0014664.

official_details.description: The SCGSR program provides supplemental funds for U.S. graduate awardees (U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents) to conduct part of their PhD thesis research at a host DOE laboratory/facility in collaboration with a DOE National Laboratory scientist within a defined award period. The award period for the proposed research project may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months. The program is sponsored and managed by the DOE Office of Science's Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS), in collaboration with the six Office of Science research programs, the Isotope R&D and production program, and the DOE National Laboratories and User Facilities. Online application and awards administration support is provided by Oak Ridge Institute of Science and Education (ORISE) under Oak Ridge Associated Universities (ORAU). The program creates a pathway for a student to advance their PhD thesis research while working at a DOE National Laboratory, collaborating with world-class scientists, and using state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge scientific instrumentation.
purpose: Create a pathway for graduate students to advance their PhD thesis research while working at a DOE National Laboratory, collaborating with world-class scientists and using state-of-the-art facilities and scientific instrumentation.
Support the goal of developing a new generation of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) experts who are critically important to the DOE Office of Science mission.
Strengthen the connection between university research and national laboratory capabilities while preparing the next generation of scientific leaders.

Support extended research visits aligned with DOE mission priorities, including high-performance computing, AI and data science, quantum science, fusion energy science and engineering, nuclear energy, and critical materials and technologies.
Prepare graduate students for STEM careers of critical importance to the DOE Office of Science mission through extended graduate research residence at DOE national laboratories and facilities.
Enable training graduate students at the convergence of multiple- and trans-disciplinary scientific areas and communities as a priority for U.S. workforce development.
Expand the awardee's professional network and develop new opportunities for their future.
study_type: Extended in-person graduate research residence at a DOE national laboratory or facility
Thesis-based fundamental experimental or theoretical research in a DOE Office of Science priority research area
official_details.degree_award: Not a degree award. The award is supplemental support for part of the applicant's existing PhD thesis research at a host DOE laboratory; no degree is conferred by the programme.
official_details.duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months of research at a DOE laboratory/facility. Proposed project periods may not begin before the published earliest start date and must begin no later than the published latest start date.
official_details.application_cycle: Two solicitations per year. 2026 Solicitation 2: application opened August 12, 2026 and applications are due November 4, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET, with offers April 1-16, 2027 and project periods starting between June 7, 2027 and October 4, 2027. 2027 Solicitation 1 (all dates tentative): application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027, offers September 2027, project periods starting November 2027 and ending no later than March 2028.
official_details.deadline_central_display: November 4, 2026, at 5:00PM ET
official_details.deadline_institutional: None published. The applicant submits directly through the SCGSR online application system. DOE verifies enrollment with the host academic institution prior to issuing the award and at the beginning of each academic term, but the institution does not submit the application.
official_details.deadline_note: At the submission deadline the online application system closes and no additional materials are accepted; the system closes at 5:00 PM Eastern Time. The complete application includes all required fields, official graduate transcripts, the research proposal, and both letters of support, and both letters must be received before the deadline. Letters of support cannot be submitted outside the online application system. Applications sent by email or postal mail will not be considered. Applications are kept on record for the current application period only and are not carried into later cycles.
official_details.funding_type: Monthly living stipend plus capped inbound/outbound travel reimbursement
official_details.funding_label: Monthly stipend up to $3,600 for general living expenses while at the host laboratory, plus up to $3,000 total inbound and outbound travel reimbursement per award; no tuition, no supplies, no in-project travel
official_details.funding_period: per month during the award period (maximum monthly amount up to $3,600); separate travel benefit of up to $3,000 total per award
official_details.living_cost_coverage: A monthly stipend in the amount of up to $3,600 for general living expenses while at the host DOE laboratory/facility during the award period. The actual monthly stipend amount will be based on an assessment of the individual's situation, with factors under consideration including, but not limited to: duration of proposed research, location of home residence, and concurrent federal funding (under normal circumstances, awardees will receive the maximum monthly stipend). Stipends are provided directly to the awardees through direct deposit to the awardee's designated bank account.
official_details.travel_coverage: Reimbursement for in-bound and out-bound travel expenses to the host DOE laboratory/facility, limited to a total travel benefit of up to $3,000 per award, and available only if the host DOE national laboratory/facility is greater than 50 miles from the awardee's home graduate institution. The reimbursement applies to transportation costs only (i.e. not other relocation costs). In-bound travel is transportation from the awardee's home graduate institution to the host laboratory at the beginning of the award term; out-bound travel is transportation back at the end of the award term. Reimbursements are made for actual travel expenses according to the standard DOE travel policy. Separately, awardees may apply, only after receiving the award, for further funding to conduct a brief (6 weeks maximum) research visit to select research institutions abroad.
official_details.tuition_rule: The award does not pay tuition. The awardee and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for any tuition or fees required by the graduate institution for the awardee to remain enrolled in the graduate program during the award term. The graduate student's home institution and primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for ensuring the student's tuition and other student expenses are provided to maintain full-time graduate enrollment status.
official_details.home_tuition_rule: Tuition continues at the home institution and is NOT paid by SCGSR. Awardees may continue to receive funding from sources other than the SCGSR program for tuition payment at home institutions and/or support to meet the student's home residence obligations while staying in temporary accommodations during the award period. Applicants are required to disclose current sources and levels of graduate student support at the time of applying, awardees must update this information at the time of the award, and awardees must provide a summary of actual expenses incurred during the award period. SCGSR awards are not intended to provide dual compensation for activities sponsored by other sources.
official_details.tax_status: Stipend payments may be taxable to the awardee in full or in part. DOE/ORISE does not withhold taxes from these payments. Each awardee is personally responsible for his/her individual tax preparation and payment. Specific questions regarding the tax treatment of this award should be directed to a tax advisor or the Internal Revenue Service. This statement is provided for information only and is not intended as legal or tax advice, or as a definitive interpretation of the law.
covered_expenses: Monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 for general living expenses while at the host DOE laboratory/facility during the award period.
In-bound transportation from the awardee's home graduate institution to the host DOE laboratory/facility at the beginning of the award term, up to the shared $3,000 travel benefit.
Out-bound transportation from the host DOE laboratory/facility back to the awardee's home graduate institution at the end of the award term, up to the shared $3,000 travel benefit.
Access to DOE laboratory scientific user facilities, instrumentation and computing resources for the proposed research.
The option, after the award, to apply for separate funding for a brief international research visit of 6 weeks maximum.
not_covered_or_excluded: Tuition and fees charged by the awardee's home graduate institution during the award term; the awardee and thesis advisor are responsible for these.

Supplies, materials and consumables needed to conduct the proposed research: the SCGSR program does not provide additional support for supplies, materials, or travel while conducting the SCGSR research project at the host DOE laboratory/facility during the award period.
Travel other than inbound and outbound transportation to and from the host laboratory.
Relocation costs beyond transportation; the travel reimbursement applies to transportation costs only.
Travel reimbursement where the host laboratory is 50 miles one way or less from the home graduate institution.

Housing and lodging: awardees are responsible for arranging their own lodging accommodations and for their own housing costs during their award term at the host DOE laboratory/facility. Some sites have secured or onsite housing that may be available; other sites require the awardee to find housing independently, although most sites generally provide information to help.

Health insurance and employee benefits: awardees remain full-time graduate students at their institution and are considered an SCGSR program participant and a guest scientist at the laboratory, not an employee of the host laboratory or DOE.
Any funding that would duplicate or dual-compensate activities sponsored by other funding sources.
Any funding for laboratory work that is not an integral part of the applicant's approved doctoral thesis project.
Medical research, or biological research on model systems for the purpose of understanding disease or pathogens, is not eligible.
Biomedical sciences, social sciences and some areas of environmental science, which are not a mission responsibility of the Department of Energy.
Graduate programmes in joint BS/MS, DVM, MBA, MD, joint MD/PhD, JD, or joint JD/PhD degree types.
Students who are not full-time enrollees, who have not obtained Ph.D. candidacy at the time of application, who are in a Master's programme, or who are pursuing a second Ph.D.
benefits: Access to the expertise, resources, and capabilities available at DOE national laboratories and facilities, described by the program as a combination not found anywhere else in the country.
The opportunity for a short international research visit to a prestigious institution abroad such as CERN or RIKEN, applied for separately after the award is received, limited to 6 weeks maximum.
The possibility of securing access to scientific user facilities through the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, which the merit review criteria treat favourably.
Professional network expansion and development of new opportunities for the future.
Weekly virtual SCGSR Program office hours every Friday 1:00-2:00 PM ET from September 4, 2026, plus Application Assistance Workshops.
A published running list of potential collaborating scientists who are ready to collaborate with SCGSR awardees.
eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age at the time of applying.
Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a Qualified Graduate Program with the Ph.D. as their degree objective.
At the time of application, applicants must have obtained the Ph.D. candidacy at their home institution, and must have established a defined graduate thesis project and graduate thesis advisor.
The applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor must provide a Letter of Support.

Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.

Applicants must demonstrate that their graduate thesis research is in an area of fundamental research aligned with the DOE Office of Science Priority Research Areas identified for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2.
The Ph.D. degree program pursued must require a research thesis/dissertation, with an emphasis on fundamental experimental or theoretical research.

One or more of the following must apply: the applicant is in the university group of a faculty member who is currently a PI on an Office of Science research award; or the faculty member is currently funded by an Office of Science research award but may not be the PI; or the applicant's thesis research is significantly well aligned with an Office of Science research programme in one or more priority research areas but the applicant is not in a university group funded by the Office of Science. In each case the applicant must propose to do part of their thesis research in collaboration with a DOE national laboratory scientist in a priority research area.
The applicant and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for identifying a collaborating research scientist at a DOE laboratory and jointly developing the research proposal.
Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientists may be from any of the participating DOE national laboratories/facilities.
The duration of the proposed research to be conducted at the DOE laboratory/facility may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.
Applicants must remain enrolled as a full-time graduate student in a qualified graduate program during the duration of the proposed SCGSR research project period at the host DOE laboratory/facility.
For applications in BES priority research areas, eligibility depends also on proximity between the applicant's university and the host DOE national laboratory.

The number of semester credits that constitute full-time enrolment is determined by the student's graduate institution, typically 9 credits for graduate studies, and DOE SCGSR adopts the definition of the student's graduate institution.
Graduate students who are more than five years into their graduate programme remain eligible if they satisfy all the posted eligibility requirements.

Holding other graduate fellowship support does not make an applicant ineligible; applicants must disclose current sources and levels of graduate student support and are responsible for coordinating with the sponsor of any other fellowship to ensure compliance.
general_eligibility: U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent resident status, and at least 18 years old, at the time of applying.
Full-time enrolment in a qualified thesis-based research Ph.D. programme at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
Ph.D. candidacy already obtained, with a defined graduate thesis project and thesis advisor, and an approved thesis research topic.
Thesis research in fundamental research aligned with a DOE Office of Science priority research area for the current solicitation.
An established collaboration with a scientist at a participating DOE national laboratory or facility who will co-develop the proposal and submit a letter of support.
One application per award cycle only.
Cumulative SCGSR award periods across all awards may not exceed 12 months.
ineligibility_conditions: Foreign students studying in the U.S. on a student visa (F1) are not eligible; applicants must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident at the time of application.

Applicants who have not obtained Ph.D. candidacy at the time of application submission, including students still preparing for a qualifying exam or who have established a thesis topic but not candidacy.
Applicants in a Master's degree program with a Master's as the terminal degree.
Applicants in a Master's degree program with no thesis research requirement where the program is not a pathway to the Ph.D. degree.
Applicants seeking to pursue a second Ph.D. degree.
Part-time graduate students; full-time enrolment is required at the time of application and during the award period.
Students enrolled in joint BS/MS, DVM, MBA, MD, joint MD/PhD, JD, or joint JD/PhD degree programs.
Graduate programs in the social sciences, biomedical sciences, and some areas of environmental science, which are not DOE Office of Science mission areas.
Medical research, or biological research on model systems for the purpose of understanding disease or pathogens.
Graduate students currently conducting research at the DOE laboratory/facility they propose to apply to; they may apply to a different laboratory/facility.
Applicants whose past research collaboration with the DOE laboratory scientist was 3 months in duration or more at the laboratory/facility they propose to apply to.
Applicants whose current research grant from the Office of Science specifically includes funding for extended travel for graduate students to do their thesis research at a DOE laboratory/facility.
Applicants in BES priority research areas who fail the proximity requirement between their university and the host laboratory.
Applicants submitting more than one application per award cycle.

Duplicate proposals: an application whose SCGSR research proposal has the same scope as that of a previously awarded SCGSR application, or the same as an SCGSR application already awarded from a previous solicitation cycle, will not be considered in any SCGSR solicitation cycle.

Applicants who, after applying, accept a separate non-SCGSR appointment from the host DOE laboratory/facility to work or conduct research, such as an hourly paid intern or a full-time or temporary position.
Graduate students who previously worked with a proposed collaborating scientist on their graduate research for more than three months in total.
Applications that are incomplete, or in which transcripts contain Social Security numbers or dates of birth (PII), which will be deemed non-compliant and will not be considered.
Applications with research proposals exceeding three pages excluding references, or a reference section exceeding one page; additional proposal pages are simply not included in the application.
Supplemental materials, including publications or research results submitted with the application, which will not be reviewed.
Applications sent by email or postal mail.
official_details.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age. Lawful permanent residents are explicitly eligible. Foreign students on an F1 student visa are not eligible. Applicants with LPR status are encouraged to contact their DOE National Laboratory/facility of interest during the application period because of the lead time for foreign national site-access processes, and offers are subject to change based on approval for site access prior to the planned start date. Graduate enrolment must be at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
official_details.international_eligibility: U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents only. No foreign nationals, including students on F1 visas, may apply. Travel to institutions abroad is only possible after the award, through a separate application for a brief (6 weeks maximum) research visit.

undergraduate: Not applicable; the programme is restricted to graduate students pursuing a Ph.D.
masters: Not eligible. Applicants in a Master's degree program with a Master's as the terminal degree, and applicants in a Master's program with no thesis research requirement that is not a pathway to the Ph.D., are excluded.

Note that the predecessor Office of Science Graduate Fellowship (SCGF) programme provided a stipend and tuition support for up to three years but is no longer accepting applications for new fellowships.
phd: Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a qualified Ph.D. programme with the Ph.D. as the degree objective, and must have obtained Ph.D. candidacy at the time of application.

Ph.D. candidacy generally means completing all coursework requirements and focusing primarily on doctoral thesis research, qualified through discipline-specific or program-defined measures such as an oral and/or written comprehensive qualifying exam, a thesis prospectus, or a preliminary paper.
Applicants must have an established defined graduate thesis project, an approved thesis research topic approved by their official PhD thesis committee, and a primary graduate thesis advisor.

The Ph.D. programme must require a research thesis/dissertation with an emphasis on fundamental experimental or theoretical research, in physics, chemistry, material sciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences.
Applicants seeking a second Ph.D. degree are not eligible, and part-time enrolment is not eligible.
The proposed laboratory research must be an integral part of the applicant's overall doctoral thesis project.
The research proposal must explicitly address the stated aims of at least one Office of Science priority research area for the current solicitation; proposals that do not will not be considered.

host_requirements: The host must be one of the participating DOE national laboratories/facilities listed by the programme, and each laboratory/facility has its own point of contact.

The applicant must have an identified collaborating research scientist employed by the DOE laboratory/facility, with all salary and benefits provided by that laboratory/facility, spending at least 50 percent of their time at the laboratory/facility; joint academic appointments are allowed as long as the employer is the laboratory.

A postdoctoral researcher may serve as the collaborating scientist only if their committed tenure at the laboratory exceeds the length of the proposed research project; the supervisor's contact information is then required in the application.

The collaborating scientist must be a full-time staff member at the DOE laboratory/facility for the complete duration of the award period, so a scientist planning to retire during the award cannot be the collaborator.

The proposal must identify how the proposed research will take advantage of the DOE laboratory/facility's research capabilities and assets, and access to any scientific user facilities involved must be secured before the project period starts, confirmed by the collaborating scientist.
The proposed research project must be conducted in person at a DOE national laboratory.
Awardees must undergo a routine background assessment conducted by the host DOE laboratory/facility in order to be granted access to enter the site during the award term.

The awardee must conduct the independent SCGSR research project defined in the application with the collaborating scientist, and any significant change to the approved proposal scope after the award starts must be reported to and approved by the SCGSR Program Manager.

The awardee must maintain a full-time schedule at the host site during normal laboratory business hours, may take the normal holidays recognized by the host, and must report any expected interruptions to the collaborating scientist and the SCGSR Program Manager.
requirements: All applications to the SCGSR program must be completed through the online application system.
Applicants should create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the application deadline and become familiar with the application information requested.
Only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for review.
Materials uploaded into the online application system provide the sole basis for evaluation.

Complete all required fields: Contact Information; Academic Information, including Current Graduate Program Information; Citizenship or Permanent Residency Status; Professional Information, such as Scientific Publications and Awards; Graduate Thesis Advisor and Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist Contact Information.

Submit the SCGSR research proposal, co-developed by the applicant and the collaborating DOE laboratory research scientist in consultation with the primary graduate thesis advisor, uploaded as a PDF into the online application system.
The proposal must be responsive to the required elements outlined in the full research proposal guidance document.
Upload a PDF copy of current official graduate transcripts; undergraduate transcripts are not requested or required.

Provide official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as an official, signed letter from the Registrar's office, or from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of the academic department, certifying that the applicant has completed all required PhD coursework and has a PhD thesis research topic approved by their official PhD thesis committee, including the date of official approval. Letters signed by administrative staff will not be accepted.

Submit two Letters of Support, from the primary graduate thesis advisor and from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, through the online application system; they cannot be submitted outside the online system.
Letters of Support are due before the application closing date.
Indicate in the online application system which Office of Science priority research area the proposed project is aligned with.
List citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, in the appropriate section of the online application; do not submit supplemental materials, which will not be reviewed.

Prove eligibility for the Priority Research Area selection: applications with a proposed research project that does not explicitly address an Office of Science research priority area and/or does not make specific reference to the stated aims of one of the listed areas will NOT be considered.

Choose a project start and end date that fall on business days, not holidays or weekends observed by the host, not earlier than the published Earliest Start Date and not later than the Latest Start Date, with a total duration of not less than 3 and not more than 12 consecutive months including both dates.
documents: Completed online application with all required fields: contact information; academic information including current graduate program information; citizenship or permanent residency status; professional information such as scientific publications and awards; graduate thesis advisor and collaborating DOE laboratory scientist contact information.
SCGSR research proposal, uploaded as a PDF file, limited to three pages excluding references, with references in a separate section of no more than one page.
Official graduate transcripts stamped with the college/university Registrar seal, uploaded as a PDF copy, with Social Security numbers and dates of birth redacted and the applicant's name retained.

Official proof of Ph.D. candidacy: an official, signed letter from the applicant's university/college Registrar's office, or an official, signed letter from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of the applicant's academic department, certifying completion of all required PhD coursework and that a PhD thesis research topic has been approved by the official PhD thesis committee, including the date of official approval.
Letter of Support from the applicant's primary graduate thesis advisor, completed through the online form.
Letter of Support from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, completed through the online form.
Citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, entered in the appropriate online application sections.
document_format_rules: Official graduate transcripts must be stamped with the college/university Registrar seal and submitted in PDF form; unofficial electronic transcripts are not accepted. Undergraduate transcripts are not requested or required.

Submitted official transcripts must have all Social Security numbers and dates of birth redacted or removed (blanked out, blackened out, made non-visible) prior to uploading. Applications containing PII in the form of Social Security numbers and/or dates of birth will be deemed non-compliant and will not be considered.
The applicant's name must not be redacted on the transcript, otherwise it will be impossible for reviewers to confirm that the transcript corresponds to the applicant.

If the submitted official transcript does not explicitly show the applicant's Ph.D. candidacy status, and the date or academic term when candidacy was achieved, then additional official proof for validating Ph.D. candidacy must be submitted in the online application.

Proof of Ph.D. candidacy must be an official signed letter from the Registrar's office or from the Chair of the academic department (or Head/Director of Graduate Studies); letters signed by administrative staff will not be accepted. The letter must describe the institution's, department's and programme's requirements for Ph.D. candidacy (including the URL if the requirements are online), how the applicant fulfills the requirements, and the date or academic term when candidacy was achieved.

The SCGSR research proposal must be uploaded as a PDF file into the online application system and is limited to a total of three pages excluding references; if the PDF contains more than three pages of proposal, all additional pages will not be included as part of the application.
References may be provided in a separate page and do not count toward the three-page limit, but the reference section cannot exceed one page.

Letters of support can only be received through the online application system using the access information in the request email; letters in any other format, including by email or post, will not be accepted. A letter of support cannot be deleted once submitted.
Applicants can print or export their application as a PDF using the 'Print your Application' option to review it as the SCGSR program manager will see it.
No translation requirement is published; applicants must submit English-language transcripts and letters through the English-language online system.
No file size limits are published on the pages read; the online system will not permit final submission until all required elements are completed.
selection_criteria: Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research, under which reviewers ask: Is the proposed research well-conceived, and does it demonstrate a clear understanding of the scientific and technical challenges involved? Is the proposed method and approach for the proposed research appropriate? Is the applicant (graduate student) sufficiently well prepared to conduct the proposed research? Are the DOE laboratory resources adequate, and if applicable, has the necessary access to a scientific user facility been secured by the DOE laboratory collaborating scientist?

Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training, under which reviewers ask: Does the proposed research have the potential to make a significant contribution to the applicant's (graduate student's) thesis research project? Will the proposed research enhance the applicant's graduate training and research skills?
Applications must explicitly address the stated aims of at least one Office of Science priority research area for the current solicitation; proposals that do not will not be considered.
official_details.selection_notes: Completed applications submitted before the application deadline are evaluated using the DOE Office of Science's standard merit review processes. Each application is reviewed by external subject matter experts based on the established merit review criteria, and the application materials received, including the applicant's SCGSR research proposal, provide the sole basis for the evaluation. Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review; all eligible and compliant applications are then reviewed externally by experts in the field of the proposed research. Applications are selected for award based on the results of peer review and other program policy factors, including balance of portfolio and availability of funds. The research proposed is explicitly the scope of the research to be conducted by the applicant at the DOE laboratory/facility. DOE collects information on prior participation in other DOE programmes for internal purposes only; the answer will not affect selection. An applicant selected for award receives an email notification from DOE Office of Science and is given about a week to decide whether to accept. Applicants who are not selected must reapply and submit a new application to a later solicitation; there is no automatic carry-over.
application_method: Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline.
Study the priority research areas for the current solicitation and the merit review criteria before writing anything.

Identify a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, using the programme's running list of potential collaborating scientists, the laboratory point of contacts, or by asking the SCGSR Program Manager for recommendations based on your thesis research.
Agree the scope of the laboratory research with that scientist and your primary graduate thesis advisor, and confirm it is an integral part of your thesis project.
Obtain official proof of Ph.D. candidacy as a signed letter from the Registrar or the Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies, and request it early because it depends on a third-party signature.
Obtain your official graduate transcript with the Registrar seal, and redact Social Security numbers and dates of birth before uploading.

Co-develop the research proposal with the collaborating scientist in consultation with your thesis advisor; address the stated aims of at least one priority research area and explain how the laboratory's capabilities and assets will be used; keep the proposal to three pages plus a one-page reference section.
Have both your thesis advisor and the collaborating scientist review and approve the final proposal PDF, because they receive an automated notification when you upload or replace it.
Complete all required online fields, including the Office of Science priority research area your project aligns with and up to three publication and award citations each.

Enter contact information for your thesis advisor under 'Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor Information' and for the collaborating scientist under 'Host DOE Laboratory', then click 'Send Email' on the Request Letters of Support tab to send both requests.
Monitor the receipt of both letters of support in the online system and send reminders where necessary; letters cannot be replaced once submitted.
Print or export your application to PDF for a final review, then press 'Submit' by 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026 and confirm the Status page shows 'Submitted'.
If selected, respond to the DOE Office of Science notification within about a week to accept or decline the award.
application_steps: Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the application deadline.
Read the Eligibility page, the Priority Research Areas for the current solicitation, and the Application Evaluation and Selection page before drafting.

Identify and commit a collaborating research scientist at a participating DOE national laboratory/facility; if you need help, contact the SCGSR Program Manager, who will ask about your thesis research and recommend potential scientists, or consult the laboratory point of contacts.
Confirm you have obtained Ph.D. candidacy, have an approved thesis topic, and that the proposed laboratory work forms an integral part of your thesis project.
Discuss the proposed project with your thesis advisor and the collaborating scientist, and have both agree to submit letters of support.

Obtain the official proof of Ph.D. candidacy letter from the Registrar or the Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies, including the date of thesis committee approval; letters signed by administrative staff will not be accepted.
Obtain official graduate transcripts stamped with the Registrar seal and redact Social Security numbers and dates of birth, keeping your name visible.

Co-develop the research proposal with the collaborating scientist and in consultation with the thesis advisor; ensure it addresses the stated aims of at least one priority research area, identifies how the laboratory's research capabilities and assets will be used, and contains only research to be conducted by you at that laboratory during the proposed dates.
Format the proposal to a maximum of three pages excluding references, with references in a separate section of no more than one page, and export it as a PDF.
Ensure both your thesis advisor and the collaborating scientist have read and approved the final proposal PDF; they receive automatic notifications when you upload or update the file.

Complete the required online application fields: contact information; academic information and current graduate program information; citizenship or permanent residency status; professional information including up to three publication citations and three award citations; thesis advisor and collaborating laboratory scientist contact information; and the selected Office of Science priority research area.

Enter the thesis advisor contact information under 'Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor Information' and the collaborating scientist contact information under 'Host DOE Laboratory' in the 'Complete your Application' tab.
Use the 'Send Email' button on the Request Letters of Support tab to send requests; the automated emails provide each person a link and access code for the online form.
Check that the proposal will use any required scientific user facilities, since the collaborating scientist must confirm in their letter that access will be secured before the project start date.
Choose a project start and end date on business days, within the published earliest and latest start-date window, totalling 3 to 12 consecutive months.
Upload the proposal PDF and the redacted official transcript to the online application system.
Monitor the status of both letters of support in the online system and send reminder emails; the deadline for both is 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026.
Print or export your application as a PDF using 'Print your Application' to check everything as the program manager will see it.
Press 'Submit' on the final submission page by 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026, then confirm the Status page shows 'Submitted' with a blue check mark.
If selected, you will receive an email from DOE Office of Science and will be given about a week to decide whether to accept the award.
applicant_submission_route: The applicant submits the application personally through the SCGSR online application system; applications sent by email or postal mail will not be considered.

Letters of support are submitted electronically by the thesis advisor and the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist through unique URLs sent by the system; letters in any other format are not accepted.

The home graduate institution does not submit the application, although DOE verifies the applicant's enrolment with the institution before issuing the award and at the beginning of each academic term during the award.
award_holder_conditions: Provide proof of U.S. Citizenship or Lawful Permanent Residency (LPR) once selected; acceptable forms of proof are provided with the award notification.

Remain enrolled as a full-time student in a qualified graduate program at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories during the award period, and remain in good academic standing.

Continue to carry out the independent SCGSR research project defined in the application proposal with the Collaborating DOE Scientist at the host DOE national laboratory/facility, and report and obtain approval for any significant change to the approved proposal scope.

Conduct research and remain at the host DOE Laboratory/Facility site during the entire award period, maintaining a full-time schedule during normal laboratory business hours, observing the host's normal holidays, and reporting any expected interruptions to the collaborating scientist and the SCGSR Program Manager.

Agree to the terms contained in the Letter of Appointment and the 'Terms of Agreement' from the DOE Office of Science, which outline the award period, the award benefits, and the conditions for accepting the award, including continuing to meet all eligibility requirements and Federal requirements.

Remain enrolled full-time in a qualified Ph.D. program at the home academic institution, disclose and update current sources and levels of graduate student support at the time of the award, and provide a summary of actual expenses incurred during the award period.
Submit an end-of-award report through the SCGSR online system using the provided templates; research awards greater than 6 months in duration also require a mid-term progress report.
Respond to requests for information about their experience conducting research at the DOE laboratory/facility.

Undergo and complete the routine background assessment conducted by the host DOE laboratory/facility in order to be granted access to enter the site during the award term, responding in a timely manner so access is gained before the planned start date.
Acknowledge WDTS support in publications and presentations using the published SCGSR acknowledgement statement including contract number DE-SC0014664.
arrival_rules: Awardees are expected to conduct their research and remain at the host DOE Laboratory/Facility site during the entire award period and avoid obligations that may interrupt their SCGSR research project.
Awardees must maintain a full-time schedule during normal laboratory business hours and may take the normal holidays recognized by their host DOE laboratory/facility.
Any expected interruption to the full-time attendance schedule must be reported to the Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist and the SCGSR Program Manager.

Awardees are responsible for arranging their own lodging accommodations and housing costs at the host site; some sites have secured or onsite housing, others require the awardee to find housing independently, and most sites provide information to help. Contact the host DOE Laboratory/Facility POC for local lodging and transportation options.
Proposed start and end dates must fall on business days, not holidays or weekends observed by the host laboratory/facility, which generally observe most Federal holidays.
For 2026 Solicitation 2, the earliest start date for proposed project periods is June 7, 2027 and the latest start date is October 4, 2027.

No immigration or visa pathway is published for international awardees, because only U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents may apply; lawful permanent residents must allow lead time for the host laboratory's foreign national site-access processes, and offers are subject to change if site access is not approved before the planned start date.

By participating, awardees do not become an employee of the host laboratory/facility or of DOE; they remain full-time graduate students at their home institution and are considered an SCGSR program participant and a guest scientist at the laboratory.

coverage: Monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 for general living expenses while at the host DOE laboratory/facility during the award period.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident and 18 or older; an F1 visa holder cannot apply.
Confirm you have already been granted Ph.D. candidacy, with an approved thesis topic and an established thesis advisor. Candidacy in the future is not acceptable.

Confirm you are enrolled full-time at an accredited U.S. college or university in a thesis-based research Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, non-medical biology, mathematics, engineering, computer/computational sciences, or select environmental sciences.

Confirm your degree programme is not a joint BS/MS, DVM, MBA, MD, MD/PhD, JD, or JD/PhD, and that your field is not in the social sciences, biomedical sciences, or excluded areas of environmental science.
Identify and commit a collaborating scientist at a participating DOE national laboratory who is a full-time staff member for the whole proposed award period and will submit a letter of support.
Agree the laboratory scope with your thesis advisor so the work is an integral part of your doctoral thesis, and obtain your advisor's agreement to write the letter of support.

Request the official proof-of-candidacy letter from the Registrar or your department Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies now, because it needs a third-party signature and must include the date your thesis topic was approved.
Order your official graduate transcript stamped with the Registrar seal, and plan to redact Social Security numbers and dates of birth before uploading.
Choose a project start and end date on business days, between June 7, 2027 and October 4, 2027, totalling 3 to 12 consecutive months.
Pick the Office of Science priority research area your project addresses and read its full description and exclusions, because the proposal must explicitly reference the stated aims.
If you are applying to a BES priority area, check the proximity requirement between your university and the host laboratory.
Confirm you have not already spent more than 3 months doing graduate research with that scientist at that laboratory.
Budget realistically: this award pays no tuition, no supplies, and no housing, so your advisor's funding must cover tuition and your own money must cover living costs above the stipend.
important_advice_for_students: This is not a full scholarship. The $3,600 monthly stipend is for living at the lab; your tuition and fees at your home university remain your and your advisor's responsibility, and supplies, materials and housing are not covered.

Start the collaboration early. Identifying a cooperating scientist and jointly developing the proposal is described as the most time-consuming part of the application, and both letters of support depend on the proposal already existing.
Never upload an unredacted transcript. Social Security numbers or dates of birth in the transcript make the application non-compliant and it will not be considered.
Do not redact your name on the transcript, because reviewers then cannot match it to you.
Submit your application before 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026; the system shuts off exactly then, and both letters of support must already be in.
Do not attach publications or extra materials as attachments; they will not be reviewed. List up to three publication citations and three award citations in the online fields instead.

Do not plan to travel back and forth between the lab and your university during the award. A full-time schedule at the host site during business hours is a term of the award, and interrupting it can jeopardise it.
Do not accept any separate paid intern or temporary position at the host laboratory after applying, because doing so makes you ineligible for the award.
If your advisor's grant already funds extended lab travel for graduate students, you may be ineligible for the relevant priority area, so ask them first.
Use the weekly Friday office hours and the October 1, 2026 workshop; the programme also publishes a running list of scientists willing to collaborate.
common_rejection_risks: Not a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident, or under 18, at the time of application.
Ph.D. candidacy not yet obtained at the time of application submission, including candidates still preparing for qualifying exams.
Enrolled in a master's programme, a part-time programme, a second Ph.D., or a joint BS/MS, MD, MD/PhD, JD, JD/PhD, DVM or MBA programme.

Field of study outside the DOE Office of Science mission, including social sciences, biomedical sciences, and excluded areas of environmental science, or medical research and disease/pathogen model-system biology.
Proposed research that does not explicitly address the stated aims of at least one Office of Science priority research area, which is stated to mean the application will not be considered.
Applying to a BES priority area without meeting the university-to-laboratory proximity requirement.
Currently conducting research at the same laboratory being proposed, or having previously collaborated with the proposed scientist there for 3 months or more.

No committed collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, or a collaborator who will not be a full-time staff member for the entire award period, or a postdoctoral collaborator whose tenure is shorter than the project.
Research proposal longer than three pages excluding references, or a reference section longer than one page; extra pages are simply dropped from the application.
Proposal PDF not approved by both the thesis advisor and the collaborating scientist before upload, since both must confirm they have reviewed and approved it.
Missing or late letters of support; letters submitted outside the online system are not accepted and cannot be deleted once submitted.
Proof of Ph.D. candidacy letter signed by administrative staff rather than the Registrar or the Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies, or missing the thesis approval date.
Official transcript missing the Registrar seal, unofficial transcript, or a transcript still showing Social Security numbers or dates of birth.
Submitting supplemental materials such as full publications or research results, which will not be reviewed.
More than one application in a cycle, or a duplicate proposal whose scope matches a previously awarded SCGSR application.
Accepting a separate non-SCGSR paid position at the host laboratory after applying.
Missing the 5:00 PM ET deadline, or trying to submit by email or post.
estimated_uncovered_costs: All tuition and fees at your home graduate institution for the duration of the award term, which the awardee and thesis advisor are responsible for.
Room and board at the host laboratory location; awardees arrange their own lodging and pay their own housing costs, and only some sites have onsite or secured housing.
Research supplies, materials, consumables and compute charges, none of which SCGSR supports.
Any travel to conferences, collaborators or user facilities during the award period, which the programme does not cover.
Relocation costs beyond transportation; the travel reimbursement covers transportation only.
Health insurance, since awardees are participants and guest scientists rather than employees of the laboratory or DOE.
Living costs at your home residence if you maintain a home, though support from other sources for home residence obligations during the award is permitted.
Living costs above the stipend if your local cost of living exceeds $3,600 a month, or if your stipend is reduced below the maximum because of concurrent federal funding or home-residence location.
Income tax on the stipend, which may be taxable in full or in part and is not withheld by DOE/ORISE.
Any costs of securing access to scientific user facilities not confirmed in advance by the collaborating scientist.
document_audit: Official graduate transcript: must be stamped with the college/university Registrar seal and submitted as a PDF. Redact or remove all Social Security numbers and dates of birth before uploading; leave your name visible. Undergraduate transcripts are not required. If the transcript does not show your Ph.D. candidacy status and the date or academic term it was achieved, add separate official proof.

Proof of Ph.D. candidacy: an official, signed letter from the Registrar's office, or from the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies of your department. It must certify that you have completed all required PhD coursework and that a PhD thesis research topic has been approved by your official thesis committee, and must include the date of official approval. Administrative-staff signatures are rejected.

SCGSR research proposal: PDF, maximum three pages excluding references, with references in a separate section of no more than one page. Must address the stated aims of at least one priority research area, identify how the laboratory's capabilities and assets will be used, and contain only research you will conduct at that laboratory during the proposed dates. Both your advisor and the collaborating scientist must have approved the final PDF.

Letter of Support from the primary graduate thesis advisor: completed on the online form via the unique link and access code emailed by the system. Covers how long they have known you, your preparedness for the proposed project, the importance of the research to your thesis, and confirmation they have read and approved the proposal.

Letter of Support from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist: completed on the online form via their unique link. Covers how long they have known you, your preparedness, the scientific merit of the project as part of your thesis, how the project uses the laboratory's capabilities and assets, and confirmation they have read and approved the proposal; plus confirmation of user facility access where applicable.
Citations: up to three publication citations and three award citations, entered in the online fields only. No attachments.

Required online fields: contact information; academic information including current graduate program information; citizenship or permanent residency status; professional information; thesis advisor and collaborating laboratory scientist contact information; and the chosen Office of Science priority research area.
Project dates: start and end dates on business days, within June 7, 2027 to October 4, 2027 for this solicitation, totalling 3 to 12 consecutive months.
Proof of citizenship or permanent residency is not part of the application package but is required upon award notification; acceptable forms are provided with the notification.

referee_tracking.instructions: Submit their contact information under 'Primary Graduate Thesis Advisor Information', then use the 'Send Email' button on the Request Letters of Support tab. The system emails them a unique link and access code to the online form. They must address how long they have known you, your preparedness for the proposed SCGSR research, the importance of the proposed research to your doctoral thesis project, and confirm they have read and approved the proposal. Their letter is also their formal approval of the proposed research scope. Letters cannot be deleted once submitted, and must arrive before 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026.

Submit their contact information in the 'Collaborating DOE Laboratory Scientist' section under 'Host DOE Laboratory', then send the request through the online system. They receive a unique link and access code and complete the online form covering how long they have known you, your preparedness, the scientific merit of the proposed project as part of your thesis, how the project will use the laboratory's research capabilities and assets, and confirmation they have read and approved the proposal. If the project uses scientific user facilities, they must also confirm in the form that access will be secured before the project start date. Letters in any format other than the online form are rejected.

alerts.message: Contact the SCGSR Program Manager or a laboratory point of contact if you do not yet have a collaborating scientist; the programme manager will recommend candidates based on your thesis research. This is the long-lead item.

alerts.trigger: As soon as you start drafting
alerts.message: Send the two letters-of-support requests as early as possible. Both referees must see and approve a completed proposal, so requesting letters before the proposal exists will fail.
Redact all Social Security numbers and dates of birth. Applications containing that PII are deemed non-compliant and will not be considered, but keep your name visible.
Start and end dates must be business days at the host, cannot start before June 7, 2027 or after October 4, 2027, and must total 3 to 12 consecutive months.
Final submission deadline. The system closes at 5:00 PM Eastern and accepts nothing after; all fields, the transcript, the proposal and both letters of support must be in.
Offer notifications go out. You will have about a week to accept or decline, so check your email including spam.

submission_workflow: Create your account on the SCGSR online application system now.
Confirm eligibility: citizenship or LPR, age 18+, full-time thesis-based Ph.D., Ph.D. candidacy obtained with an approved topic.
Identify and commit a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, then agree the project scope with them and with your thesis advisor.
Request the official proof-of-candidacy letter from the Registrar or your department Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies, including the thesis approval date.
Obtain your official Registrar-sealed graduate transcript and prepare a redacted PDF copy.

Co-develop the three-page research proposal (plus up to one page of references) with your collaborating scientist and thesis advisor; upload the PDF and confirm both have received the notification and approved it.
Complete all required online fields, including the selected Office of Science priority research area and up to three publication and three award citations.
Enter your thesis advisor and collaborating scientist contact details, then send both letters-of-support requests through the Request Letters of Support tab.
Track both letters in the online system and send reminders; letters cannot be replaced once submitted.
Upload the redacted official transcript and proof-of-candidacy letter.
Print or export your application as a PDF to review it as the program manager will see it.
Press Submit by 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026 and verify the Status page shows 'Submitted'.
If selected, respond to the DOE notification within about a week to accept the award.
post_award_requirements: Provide proof of U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency when the award notification arrives; acceptable forms will be provided with the notification.

Remain enrolled full-time in a qualified graduate program at your home institution throughout the award and remain in good academic standing; DOE verifies enrolment before issuing the award and at the start of each academic term.

Maintain a full-time schedule at the host laboratory during normal business hours for the whole award period, observing the host's holidays, and report any expected interruption to your collaborating scientist and the SCGSR Program Manager.
Carry out the research as approved; report and obtain Program Manager approval before making any significant change to the approved proposal scope.
Agree to and comply with the Letter of Appointment and the DOE Office of Science 'Terms of Agreement', including continued eligibility and Federal requirements.

Continue to disclose and update your other sources and levels of graduate support, and provide a summary of actual expenses incurred during the award period; SCGSR funding is not intended to dual-compensate other sources.
Submit an end-of-award report through the online system, and a mid-term progress report as well if the award exceeds 6 months; have your collaborating scientist review the reports before submission.
Respond to requests for information about your experience conducting research at the laboratory.
Complete the host laboratory's routine background assessment promptly so site access is in place before your start date.
Acknowledge the SCGSR programme, Office of Science and WDTS support, with contract number DE-SC0014664, in all publications and presentations based on the award-period research.
Do not accept a separate paid position at the host laboratory, and do not interrupt your lab schedule with regular commuting or other commitments.
questions_to_ask_host: Can my thesis advisor's existing grant cover my tuition and fees for the full award period, and is that confirmed in writing?
Who at the host laboratory can confirm user facility access for my project, and is it secured before my start date?
What is on-site or secured housing availability at this laboratory, and what is the realistic monthly cost against the $3,600 stipend?
What are the badge/background assessment lead times, and when should I start them relative to a June 2027 start?
Which fiscal calendar will pay the stipend, and are there any pay periods before my start date?
Which Office of Science priority research area does my project best fit, and does my project satisfy the stated aims closely enough?
If I am applying to a BES priority area, does the distance between my university and this laboratory satisfy the proximity requirement?
Is scientific user facility time already allocated for my project, and are there facility charges I will have to pay?
What is the local cost of commuting and whether the laboratory provides shuttle or transport options?
What reporting templates and due dates will I need to meet, and what format do the mid-term and end-of-award reports take?

records.description: The Chevening ASEAN Scholarship is the ASEAN variant of the UK government-funded Chevening Scholarship programme. Applicants from ASEAN member states or Timor-Leste apply through the standard Chevening Scholarship process and, on top of all standard Chevening benefits, are considered for an enhanced UK programme of exclusive events, priority invitations, the ASEAN Chevening Conference and access to the global Chevening alumni community. Chevening states the scholarship is fully funded, covering a one-year UK master's degree; the highest-ranking applicant(s) from each participating country are considered for the ASEAN element. Chevening does not publish the monthly stipend figure on its public pages - the amount is stated in the applicant's Final Award Letter.
records.best_fit: Citizens or residents of an ASEAN member state or Timor-Leste who hold an undergraduate degree qualifying them for a UK master's programme, have at least two years (2,800 hours) of post-degree work experience, can commit to returning home for at least two years, and can apply to three different eligible UK taught master's courses. Opting in for the ASEAN element does not affect your chances of a standard Chevening Scholarship.
records.eligibility_summary: Must be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory (ASEAN member state or Timor-Leste for the ASEAN element), with an undergraduate degree, two years' work experience, three eligible UK master's course choices and a commitment to return home for two years.
eligibility: Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory.

If applying for an award from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country. This does not have to be the country of citizenship, but all applicants must show a clear intention to support their country of award.
Commit to returning to your home country (country of award) for at least two years after your scholarship ends.
Have at least two years' work experience, acquired after completing your undergraduate degree, equivalent to 2,800 hours.

Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme. You must have finished your undergraduate studies at least two years before the application deadline, even if you have not yet received your certificate; you will need the certificate by the time of your interview.
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses.
You must have received an unconditional offer from at least one of these course choices by the deadline listed on the application timeline.
The ASEAN element is for outstanding individuals from ASEAN member states or Timor-Leste; the highest-ranking applicant(s) from each participating country will be considered.

A monthly stipend, stated in the Final Award Letter, which Chevening says is intended to cover all living costs including accommodation
Return flights between the nearest airport in the home country and the nearest airport to the UK university, booked by Chevening's designated travel agency, where confirmed in the Final Award Letter
Student visa application fee and Immigration Health Surcharge ('you don't need to pay the visa fee or the Immigration Health Surcharge')
