records.name: Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships
records.official_source: Alberta Innovates (Government of Alberta provincial agency), delivered through participating Alberta post-secondary institutions
records.region: Canada (Alberta; open to Canadian, permanent resident and international graduate students at participating Alberta post-secondary institutions)
records.duration: Terms vary from one to four years, depending on the recipient's time in the program. At the University of Calgary the published terms are $26,000 for master's students for up to two years and $31,000 for doctoral students for up to four years.
records.deadline: No single calendar deadline is published. The Alberta Innovates programme page gives the due date as "Continuous" and states "This program is accepting applications on a seasonal basis. Intake Open Date is specific to each individual university; please contact your university of choice for deadline information." At the University of Calgary, "The Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 of each year" and "Deadlines vary by program"; the Faculty of Graduate Studies reference deadline is February 1.
records.application_period: Continuous at the funder level, with a seasonal intake at each institution. Alberta Innovates publishes the due date as "Continuous". At the University of Calgary the Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 each year, program deadlines vary and must be confirmed with Graduate Program Staff, and results for the Alberta Innovates competition are announced September to December. Awards are paid in the following academic year, with the majority starting in September.
records.description: The Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships program funds full-time graduate students researching emerging technologies at participating Alberta post-secondary institutions, so that they can devote their full time to their academic studies. Alberta Innovates publishes funding ranging from $12,000 to $31,000 per year with terms of one to four years; at the University of Calgary the published values are $26,000 for master's students for up to two years and $31,000 for doctoral students for up to four years, plus top-ups of $18,000 where the student also holds an Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship and $12,000 where they also hold a major award of $17,500 or higher. It is a research scholarship rather than a comprehensive award: no source establishes that tuition, living costs and required expenses are all covered, so it is not fully funded.
records.best_fit: Master's or doctoral students, including international students, enrolled full time in a thesis-based research programme at the University of Alberta, University of Calgary, University of Lethbridge, Athabasca University or Concordia University of Edmonton, whose research develops an Applied Digital or Emerging Technology in natural sciences or engineering and can produce potential environmental, health, economic and social impacts for Alberta.
records.eligibility_summary: Canadian, permanent resident or international graduate students conducting full-time research in information and communications technologies or advanced materials and manufacturing technologies at one of the five named participating Alberta post-secondary institutions, whose project develops rather than merely uses an emerging technology and who can articulate its potential impact for Alberta.
eligibility: Be a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident of Canada, or an international student.

Be enrolled as a full-time graduate student conducting full-time research at one of the participating institutions: Athabasca University, Concordia University of Edmonton, the University of Alberta, the University of Calgary or the University of Lethbridge.
Be conducting research in a key emerging technology area of information and communications technologies (ICT) or advanced materials and manufacturing technologies (AMM).

Be able to clearly articulate how your research aligns with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and how your research can produce potential environmental, health, economic, social and other impacts for Alberta.
At the University of Calgary: be applying to, or enrolled in, a thesis-based graduate degree programme.
At the University of Calgary: have submitted your admissions application and received your University of Calgary student number (UCID).
Meet the eligibility requirements in the terms of reference of the award at the time the award is paid, even if you did not meet them at the time you applied.
coverage: Scholarship funding enabling full-time graduate students to devote their full time to their academic studies

requirements: Check with your institution's faculty of graduate studies for full descriptions and application details.
Submit your application to your institution; the applicant does not apply directly to Alberta Innovates.
At the University of Calgary: submit your admissions application and obtain your UCID before applying for the award.

At the University of Calgary: go to your Student Centre and click the link Apply for Graduate Funding in the Financial Aid section of your home screen, then select the Graduate Award Competition Application.
Only one application is required regardless of the number of awards you are applying for.
You may create one application per competition each year; if an application is incorrectly cancelled you must contact your graduate program to request reactivation.
Request and track your references before finalizing your application so they arrive before or by the application deadline.
New students can use their references from their admission application toward their scholarship application.

Reference letters used for admission may be used toward the scholarship competition as long as they were written within the eleven months prior to the Faculty of Graduate Studies' February 1 deadline.

application_method: Check with your institution's faculty of graduate studies for the full description and application details.
Submit your application to your institution.
Wait for your application to be reviewed by that institution.
records.selection_notes: Selection is institution-specific. Each of the participating Alberta institutions has its own scholarship application and evaluation processes for students in full-time programmes, and Alberta Innovates directs students to their faculty of graduate studies for that information. At the University of Calgary the competition is merit-based and the applicant must be able to clearly articulate alignment with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and the potential impacts of the work for Alberta. For the Killam and Open Doctoral categories a first-class average is required, which at the University of Calgary is a grade point average of 3.5 or higher in the last two years of study, though that published indicator is stated for those categories rather than for the Alberta Innovates category. Successful students may normally hold one GAC scholarship per year across the Open Doctoral and Special Awards categories and will be awarded the highest-value scholarship for which they are eligible.
records.notes: Multi-year scholarships are renewed annually after the first year upon satisfactory reporting by the student. Students who have been awarded an Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarship must complete annual and final reports through the term of their award, and post-award reports after the end of the award. No deferral rule, no return-home obligation and no clinical or practice-location restriction are published. You may create only one application per competition each year. At the University of Calgary, students in course-based and professional degree programs are NOT eligible for the Graduate Award Competition through which this award is applied for.

official_details.description: The Graduate Student Scholarships program provides funding to enable full-time graduate students to research emerging technologies at participating post-secondary institutions. The program offers funding ranging from $12,000 to $31,000 per year, and the terms vary from one to four years, depending on the recipient's time in the program. Alberta Innovates states that it is proud to support the next generation of leaders in emerging technology areas in their pursuit of academic excellence through scholarship funding that can enable the student to devote their full time to their academic studies. It is open to Canadian, permanent resident, and international graduate students conducting full-time research in key emerging technology areas of information and communications technologies (ICT) and advanced materials and manufacturing technologies (AMM).

The primary objective must be the advancement of the ET itself, rather than improvements in other products.

Thematic Areas of Focus that an ET development project may additionally support: Health, Agricultural, and Life Science Innovation; Advanced Materials, Defence, and Aerospace; Natural Resource Recovery.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are enrolled, or applying to enrol, full time at one of the five participating institutions: Athabasca University, Concordia University of Edmonton, the University of Alberta, the University of Calgary or the University of Lethbridge.
Confirm your research genuinely develops an emerging technology, rather than using one as a tool. This is the most common disqualifier.
Re-read Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas list and pick the topic you are actually developing.
Draft a plain statement of the potential environmental, health, economic and social impacts of your work for Alberta; the institution will expect you to articulate this.
Contact your faculty of graduate studies now for the institutional deadline, because the funder's continuous due date does not tell you when to submit.
At the University of Calgary, get your admissions application in and wait for your UCID before applying for the award.
Line up referees early; at the University of Calgary the Faculty of Graduate Studies reference deadline is February 1.
Check that your referees' letters will be written within eleven months of that February 1 deadline.
At the University of Calgary, use Microsoft Edge or Mozilla Firefox; the page warns Chrome users will encounter issues.
Read the terms of reference for each award you tick, not just the programme summary.
Put your reporting obligations in your calendar from day one: annual and final reports through the award term, plus post-award reports.
important_advice_for_students: Do not assume 'Continuous' means you can apply any day. Alberta Innovates states the intake open date is specific to each individual university, so the real deadline is your institution's.
Do not waste effort on projects that merely apply AI or another emerging technology to an existing product. Those are classed as use of emerging technology and are not funded.

Do not apply to only one award because you are interested in Alberta Innovates. At the University of Calgary one application covers the whole Graduate Award Competition and you tick every award you want considered.
Do not skip the references. UCalgary's own guidance is to request and track references before finalizing, because missing references remove an otherwise complete application.
Do not assume the top-ups come automatically. The $18,000 AGES top-up and the $12,000 Major Award top-up each require you to have applied for and been awarded a second award as well.
Do not treat the annual renewal as automatic forever. Multi-year scholarships are renewed annually after the first year only upon satisfactory reporting.
Do not budget this as full funding. Nothing published establishes that tuition, living costs and required expenses are all covered.
common_rejection_risks: Research that uses an emerging technology as a tool rather than developing or advancing the emerging technology itself.
Applying at an institution that is not one of the five named participating institutions.
Failing to articulate the potential impacts of the research for Alberta.
Missing the institutional deadline because the funder's due date reads as Continuous.
Applying before your admissions application is submitted or before you have your student number.
References that arrive late, or that were written more than eleven months before the February 1 Faculty of Graduate Studies deadline.

submission_workflow: Read the Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships Program Guidelines for 2026-27.
Confirm your institution is one of the five participating institutions and get its internal deadline.
Confirm your project is emerging-technology development, not emerging-technology use.
Submit your admissions application and obtain your student number where required.
Wait for the institutional competition to open (November 1 at the University of Calgary).
Access the Student Awards Application from your Student Centre under Apply for Graduate Funding.
Select the Graduate Award Competition Application and tick every award you want considered.
Read the terms of reference for each award you tick.
Request and track your references, checking they meet the eleven-month rule against the February 1 deadline.
Submit before your program's internal deadline.
Await results in the September to December window and check the results page even if you hear nothing.
Complete annual, final and post-award reports for the life of the award.
post_award_requirements: Remain enrolled full time at a participating institution for the term of the award.
Complete annual reports and a final report through the term of the award.
Complete post-award reports after the end of the award.
Multi-year awards are renewed annually after the first year only upon satisfactory reporting.
Where the host institution requires it, remain in a thesis-based graduate programme.
No return-home obligation and no clinical or practice-location restriction are published for this award.

records.name: Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung Scholarship – Förderung internationaler Studierender und Promovierender (Scholarship for Studies / PhDs for international students and doctoral candidates)
records.official_source: Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung e. V., Institut für Begabtenförderung
records.region: Germany (all applicants who are international students at a state or state-recognised German university; applications are routed through the HSS country office where one exists)
records.duration: Study scholarship: normally up to the maximum funding period under BAföG, reviewed at the end of each funding year; doctoral scholarship: initially three years, extendable by six months on justified application and in exceptional cases up to a maximum of four years
records.deadline: Application portal open 15 December 2026 to 15 January 2027 inclusive (12:00 CET) for Internationale Studierende und Promovierende (Ausländer); a further window 15 June 2027 to 15 July 2027 (12:00 CEST). Applications possible only via the HSS online application portal.
records.application_period: 15 December 2026 – 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET) and, for the same programme, 15 June 2027 – 15 July 2027 (12:00 CEST); the Institute informs applicants by email about the outcome of their application approximately four weeks after the application deadline
records.description: The Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung funds international students and doctoral candidates at state or state-recognised higher education institutions in Germany with a monthly stipend plus a study-cost flat rate, together with an ideological and networking programme. The page states that the amount is based on the income and assets of the person responsible for support and that graduates of the second educational path are funded independently of parents. The scholarship does not have to be repaid and there is no legal entitlement to the stated benefits. Double funding with BAföG or other public funds is expressly excluded.
records.best_fit: International students already enrolled in, or about to enrol in, a full-time degree programme at a state or state-recognised university in Germany, who are under 45, can prove German at B2 level or equivalent, have above-average school or study performance, are involved in voluntary work, are politically interested and endorse the foundation's aims. For doctoral candidates: admitted to a German university or research institution.
records.eligibility_summary: Under 45, proven German skills of at least B2 or comparable, above-average performance, voluntary engagement, political interest, civic-mindedness, acceptance of the foundation's aims, and a full-time course of study at a state or state-recognised higher education institution in Germany.
eligibility: I am less than 45 years old
I have proof of German language skills of at least B2 or a comparable level
I show above-average performance at school or in my studies
I am actively involved in voluntary work (politics, church, social association, sports, music, etc.)
I am politically interested
I support democracy, rule of law, and human rights
I speak German at an adequate level
I complete a full-time course of study at a state or state-recognized university in Germany
coverage: Monthly study scholarship of at most 992 €/month calculated according to BMBF guidelines, the level depending on the income and assets of the person responsible for support (page 'Finanzielle Förderung')

Study-cost flat rate of 300 €/month paid in addition to and independently of parents' income, intended for study-related expenditure that does not serve subsistence – for example learning and working materials (including books, hardware and software), language courses, relevant specialist conferences, congress visits and excursions
benefits: Where the scholarship holder is personally health-insured, a monthly supplement towards health insurance of up to 102 € and towards care insurance of 35 € may be granted
For voluntarily, statutorily or privately insured students over 30 years of age, the assessment base may be increased by up to 185 € for health insurance and up to 48 € for care insurance

Married and unmarried scholarship holders (including single parents) with at least one child under the age of 14 living in the same household receive an additional monthly childcare flat rate of 160 € per child, provided the other parent does not receive a childcare supplement

Individual advice and accompaniment by HSS staff and trust lecturers at the university location, practical seminars conveying key qualifications and intercultural competence, and integration into a network of HSS scholarship holders
requirements: Applications can be submitted only through the HSS application portal; incomplete applications cannot be submitted
Scholarship holders receive an electronic confirmation that the application has been submitted; no separate confirmation email is sent
Applicants from countries where the HSS maintains a country office must contact that office first; where no office exists, the application is submitted directly via the online application portal
Selection presupposes a preliminary screening in the Institute for Talent Promotion and, for shortlisted candidates, an invitation to a selection meeting
The applicant is informed by email about the outcome and any next steps approximately four weeks after the application deadline
application_method: Check the requirements for your programme on the 'Wen wir suchen' page and confirm every point with 'yes'
Contact the HSS country office in your home country, or, if the HSS has no office there, go directly to the application portal
Prepare all documents listed under the relevant programme section as PDF files before starting
Submit the application exclusively via the HSS application portal between 15 December 2026 and 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET)
Submit on the portal: the portal only allows submission when all mandatory fields are complete; you can save and resume an application until it is submitted
records.selection_notes: A preliminary screening is carried out in the Institute für Begabtenförderung against the criteria on the 'Wen wir suchen' page. Applicants who appear suitable are invited to a selection meeting (Auswahltagung) where they are examined by an independent selection committee. The outcome and any next steps are communicated by email about four weeks after the closing date.
records.notes: The scholarship does not have to be repaid. There is no legal entitlement to the stated benefits; the amount is individually calculated. Double funding by the Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung together with BAföG or other public funds is excluded. Study scholarship holders drop out of the study funding programme on passing their first qualifying examination, although they remain connected to HSS as former scholarship holders. Promotion funding ends in the month of the last examination or defence of the dissertation, and is initially granted for three years, with a six-month extension possible on justified application and up to a maximum of four years in exceptional cases such as illness or pregnancy. The published pages do not state a deferral rule.

official_details.description: The Hanns-Seidel-Stiftung's Institute for Talent Promotion provides ideological and financial support for students and doctoral candidates, including international students and doctoral candidates (Ausländer). The level of the scholarship depends on the income and assets of the person responsible for support; graduates of the second educational path are funded independently of parents. There is no legal entitlement to the stated benefits and the scholarship does not have to be repaid.
purpose: Support talented and engaged students and doctoral candidates through ideological and financial promotion
Promote high-quality academic successor generation in education and research
Promote students who are politically interested, voluntarily engaged, civically minded and who endorse the foundation's aims
Provide practical seminars that convey key qualifications and intercultural competence
degree_levels: First degree (Erststudium) at a state or state-recognised university in Germany
Master's programmes that follow on from a Bachelor's programme (these are not treated as a second degree)
Doctoral candidates and research stays for international doctoral candidates admitted to a German university or research institution

records.description: The Deutschlandstipendium is a German public-private scholarship that pays 300 euros a month, income-independent, to high-achieving and socially engaged students at German public and state-recognised universities. Half of the money comes from the federal government and half from private donors, and the university itself selects and pays the scholarship holders. The award is granted for at least two semesters and at most the standard period of study, and can be held in addition to BAföG.

records.selection_notes: The Deutschlandstipendium law (StipG) and the scholarship programme ordinance (StipV) set the funding criteria which the universities can shape. The intention is to support gifted and high-performing students; school and study results are an important indication, but the criteria also include awards and prizes, previous professional activity and internships, extracurricular or non-specialist engagement, and the overcoming of origin-related biographical obstacles. The application and selection procedure is intended to take the whole personality of the applicant into account. Refugee experience or experience of political persecution counts among the special social, family or personal hurdles that must be taken into account. Selection is made by the university's own selection commission; there is no central list and no right to the scholarship.
records.notes: The money does not have to be repaid. Students with a refugee background can also receive the scholarship if enrolled at a participating university. Funding ends on successful completion of the degree with the announcement of the overall grade, at the latest at the end of the second month after the last examination; otherwise it ends with the end of the month in which the student drops out, changes subject or de-registers. Funding is not continued during a leave of absence for personal or family reasons, but the award period is extended by that period; it does continue for a leave for an abroad semester or a compulsory internship, without extending the award period. The Deutschlandstipendium ends in principle with a successful first degree, including a bachelor's, and universities may set up special selection procedures to ease the transition to master's funding. Temporary suspension is possible (for example during a DAAD-funded period abroad), but the award period is not extended by this. Parallel funding: anyone who already receives a merit- and performance-dependent material grant averaging 30 euros or more a month cannot receive the Deutschlandstipendium; a DAAD full scholarship is not compatible, while a DAAD partial scholarship can run in parallel. The Deutschlandstipendium is not counted towards BAföG; counting applies only if combined scholarship income exceeds a monthly average of 300 euros. It is generally not counted towards other social benefits such as unemployment benefit II, with housing benefit (Wohngeld) as the exception, but it is taken into account in the parents' child maintenance. Tax: under the StipG it generally does not constitute taxable or contribution-liable income; exceptions are possible in certain constellations of private, state-recognised higher education institutions.

official_details.description: The Deutschlandstipendium supports talented and high-achieving students at German public and state-recognised universities. It pays 300 euros a month, income-independent, split equally between the federal government and private donors, and can be held in addition to BAföG. It has been running since the summer semester 2011. The notion of performance behind it is deliberately broad: good grades and study results count, as do the willingness to take responsibility and the successful overcoming of obstacles in one's own life and educational path.

records.name: France 2030 - PEPR GFM "Grands Fonds Marins" - Appel à projets - 2026
records.official_source: Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR), France 2030 / CNRS, Ifremer, IRD
records.region: France (all French higher education and research institutions; transnational partners allowed as unfunded partners)
records.duration: Projects must run between 36 and 54 months.
records.deadline: Limite de dépôt des projets : 17/11/2026 à 11:00 CET. The application PDF cover states: "L'appel à projets est ouvert jusqu'au 17/11/2026 à 11h00 (heure de Paris)". Section "Dates importantes" repeats: all submission elements, including the documents signed by the legal representative of each partner, must be deposited electronically before 17 Novembre 2026 à 11h00 (heure de Paris).
records.application_period: Ouverture : 21/07/2026 à 09:00 CEST. Clôture : 17/11/2026 à 11:00 CET. Single-phase call (l'appel à projets se déroule en une seule phase): full proposals are submitted and evaluated by an international committee set up by the ANR.
records.description: The PEPR GFM (Programme et Equipement Prioritaire de Recherche "Grands Fonds Marins : savoirs, usages, communs") first wave-1 call funds new interdisciplinary and/or transdisciplinary research consortia on the deep sea, defined as everything from the seafloor and its subsoil up to the water column below 200 m depth. The grant is paid as a grant (dotation) disbursed by the ANR to the coordinating French institution and can fund new activities including equipment, project-specific staff and associated running costs. It explicitly expects the recruitment of doctoral students, post-doctorants and technical staff on the projects, and the AAP text is scored on how each contractual worker's contribution advances their academic or non-academic career.
records.best_fit: A permanent staff member (enseignant-chercheur or chercheur) at a French higher education or research institution who can lead a 36-54 month consortium and needs to build a genuinely new, wide-interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary deep-sea research consortium, typically with 800 k€-3 M€ of ANR money and with doctoral students to hire on the project budget.
records.eligibility_summary: Any permanent staff member can lead, but the coordinating institution must be a French higher education or research institution, the project must last 36-54 months, request 800 k€-3 M€, sit in at least one of the five PEPR GFM challenges, and be led by an eligible French laboratory.
eligibility: The submission file must be deposited complete on the ANR submission site before the published closing date and time, and the administrative and financial document signed and stamped by each partner institution must be deposited at the date and time indicated in the AAP.
The project scientific document must imperatively follow the template published on the call website and be deposited in unprotected PDF format.
The project must have a duration of between 36 and 54 months.
The amount of aid requested must be between 0.8 M€ and 3 M€.
The coordinating institution must be a French higher education and research institution.

The beneficiaries of the aid are research organisations and higher education and research institutions; private institutions contributing to public-service missions in higher education and research under article L.732-1 of the Code de l'Education may be financed after ANR analysis, MESRE opinion and SGPI validation.
Companies and foreign institutions may be associated as partners but cannot receive funding for that participation.
The project must fit into one or several of the five PEPR GFM challenges (Défi 1 to Défi 5).
The project must require a wide interdisciplinary and/or transdisciplinary approach as defined in section 2.2 of the AAP.
coverage: A grant (dotation) of between 800 k€ and 3 M€ per project, disbursed by the ANR to the coordinating institution according to the schedule set in the aid contract.
Total envelope of about 17.5 M€ for this first PEPR GFM call.

Eligible expenditure is defined by the PEPR financial regulation (Règlement financier des PEPR); the AAP states the aid may for example finance equipment purchases and personnel expenditure specifically assigned to these projects, plus associated running costs.

Project running costs including the maturation phase, interaction with the PEPR GFM Scientific Council and Stakeholder and Citizen Forum, participation in PEPR GFM actions, the Data Management Plan, and travel connected with reducing the project's environmental footprint.

Personnel expenditure: the AAP expects the permanent staff involved to represent a substantial time commitment and explicitly anticipates recruiting post-doctorants, doctoral students (doctorants) and technical staff on the project.
benefits: Each funded project is monitored by members of the PEPR GFM Scientific Council (CS) and, where possible, of the Forum des parties prenantes et citoyennes (FPPC); this monitoring must be built into the project organisation and budgeted.
Project leaders sit on the Comité des porteurs et porteuses de projets (CPP) of the programme and significant participation in PEPR GFM events is expected.
Access to the PEPR GFM operational cell (data component) for data-management expertise and to the FAIR/CARE-compliant Data Management Plan template on DMP OPIDoR.
Projects reusing health data are pointed to the Health Data Hub platform (contact@health-data-hub.fr) instead of buying compute.
requirements: Obtain an account (login and password) on the ANR submission site in advance; the AAP recommends registering as early as possible.
Deposit the complete submission file electronically from the project manager's account before the published closing date and time.
Only the electronic version of the submission documents present on the submission site at the call closing time is taken into account for evaluation.

Define, in the scientific document, a structured maturation phase at the start of the project, with duration, budget and responsible persons, producing an operational roadmap, an ethical issues analysis, an internal ethics charter and a Data Management Plan.
Designate a person responsible for data (référent données) who drafts and updates the PGD.
Identify, from the time of submission, a person responsible for ethical issues (référent des enjeux éthiques).
Identify among the people involved in the project one person responsible for monitoring equity and inclusion (équité et inclusion).
Describe strategies for maintaining the interdisciplinary and/or transdisciplinary dialogue throughout the project and designate the person responsible for monitoring them.

Explicitly justify in the project budget the participation of project leaders in 2 in-person meetings every 18 months in metropolitan France and 3-4 travels for workpackage leaders or staff in training (doctorate or post-doctorate) every 2 years.

Projects acquiring new data or samples at sea on unprogrammed French oceanographic fleet (IR* Flotte) means must justify why non-realisation would not undermine the project and must follow the upstream operational feasibility study procedure of the IR* Flotte (FOF naval operations pole); the minutes of the ad hoc commission (CNFH or CNFC) must be supplied.
Data management must rely on the Research e-Infrastructures tools and services (Data-Terra, Huma-num, Progedo), following FAIR and, where relevant, CARE principles.
records.english_requirement: The scientific document must be written in English (rédigé en anglais), maximum 15 pages, using the published template and deposited as an unprotected PDF.
application_method: Open an account (login and password) on the ANR submission site as early as possible.
Prepare the scientific document strictly on the published template, in English, 15 pages maximum, including the three-year publication list appendix.
Collect the commitment letters of every partner institution, signed and stamped by the legal representative, and embed them in the administrative and financial document.
Complete the administrative and financial Excel document (budget between 800 k€ and 3 M€, duration between 36 and 54 months).
Upload both documents into the dedicated 'documents de dépôt' and 'documents signés' sections of the call entry on the submission site, well before the closing time.
Validate the submission electronically before 17/11/2026 at 11:00 Paris time; an electronic acknowledgement of receipt is sent to the project manager.
Wait for evaluation by the international committee convened by the ANR.
records.selection_notes: Only proposals satisfying the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are assessed by an independent international-dimension committee convened by the ANR, which may call on external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after sending questions in advance. The committee produces (1) a list of projects it recommends for funding on the published criteria and (2) a list it proposes not to fund because quality is insufficient on at least one criterion, with a written justification for each project, and may give an opinion on the amount requested. Uninvolved PEPR GFM programme directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after opinion of the CPMo and the SGPI, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (a) scientific ambition and excellence (research question going beyond the documented state of the art, discipline combination justified by the question, dialogue of conceptual frameworks, ethical questions treated as integral to ambition); (b) quality of the consortium, resources mobilised and governance (recognised complementary expertise, adequacy of staff with objectives including a precise role and career benefit for each contractual worker, structured maturation phase, mechanisms for shared appropriation of questions, inventory/acquisition/management strategy for data and samples, recurrent ethical monitoring mechanisms, explicit choices to minimise the environmental footprint, coherent sizing with an argued 0.8-3 M€ budget); (c) fit with the PEPR GFM challenges and impact (clear fit with at least one challenge and the programme's strategic priorities, described scientific/economic/environmental/societal impacts, described sharing of data and results, open-access data strategy with FAIR and CARE and Opidor PGD links, dissemination to academic and non-academic audiences).
records.notes: Aid is awarded as a one-off exceptional grant, distinct from recurrent institutional funding, intended for new actions. It is a grant to an institution, not a personal scholarship: no tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is paid to individual students, and the individuals hired on a project are salaried employees of the host institution. Consortiums without companies are not obliged to conclude and transmit a consortium agreement; where required, the coordinating institution must supply it to the ANR within a maximum of 12 months from signature of the aid contract, and its absence can lead to cessation of funding and repayment under article 6.6 of the Financial Regulation. Beneficiaries must guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, deliver a first PGD within 6 months of project start, deposit data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and must mention the France 2030 support and logos in communications. Annual indicator reporting to the State and the ANR is mandatory for ex-post evaluation. Financial aid may constitute State aid under TFEU Article 107(1) and is subject to the French research State-aid framework 2022/C 414/01, the RDI exemption regime SA.111723, the de-minimis Regulation 2023/2831 and the 2011/20/EU decision.

official_details.description: The PEPR "Grands Fonds Marins : savoirs, usages, communs" aims to produce knowledge on deep seas, defined broadly as going from the seafloor and its subsoil up to the water column below 200 m below sea level, considered as places of energy and matter exchange, habitats for marine organisms, and media linked to human activities and imaginaries. This first wave-1 call stimulates the creation of new transdisciplinary (involving non-academic stakeholders) and/or wide-interdisciplinary research consortia. The integrated approach fits within the framework of the United Nations Decade of the Oceans and aims to train a new interdisciplinary generation in all research and higher-education professions.
purpose: Produce new holistic knowledge on deep seas by creating research consortia that bring together disciplines centred on natural phenomena in which human societies are only one element among others, and disciplines centred on human societies for which those same phenomena are a relational issue.

Support projects that require a wide interdisciplinary and/or transdisciplinary approach, using all the investigation means of each discipline (empirical, formal, quantitative, qualitative and contextual) and, if the scientific question justifies it, methodological or technological developments.

Have projects fit into one or more of the five PEPR GFM challenges: Défi 1 biodiversity of deep seas and ecosystem services; Défi 2 transfers of matter and energy between solid earth, biosphere and water column; Défi 3 representations, knowledge and uses of deep seas between local/Indigenous knowledge and scientific knowledge; Défi 4 political and environmental economy of deep seas; Défi 5 multi-scale governance of deep seas.
Ensure data and samples feed national and European management, accessibility, interoperability, reuse (fairisation) and banking via research infrastructures (IR Data Terra, IR* Huma-Num, IR REGEF).
Pay particular attention to the place and valorization of data and samples, and to Overseas territories of all ocean basins, which occupy a central place in the programme.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG or sustainable-development-development goal is a formal eligibility condition. The call states the integrated approach fits within the framework of the United Nations Decade of the Oceans and mentions environmental sustainability, environmental and social justice, and intergenerational justice as ethical issues projects must address.

One eligibility criterion does impose an environmental test: projects that would cause significant harm to the environment (DNSH - Do No Significant Harm - principle under Article 17 of the EU Taxonomy Regulation) are excluded.

Lettres d'engagement des établissements partenaires, signed by the legal representative of each partner, deposited in the 'documents signés' section.
Plan de Gestion de Données (PGD): first version within 6 months of project start, using the ANR-recommended structured DMP OPIDoR template, links (Opidor) to be provided in the project.
Charte éthique interne au consortium, written during the maturation phase.
Compte rendu de la commission ad hoc (CNFH or CNFC) of the IR* Flotte, where a not-yet-programmed fleet campaign is integrated.
Annexe publication (publications annex template, .docx) and Trame du document scientifique (scientific document template, .docx) supplied by the ANR for completion.
Accord de consortium, or a copy of an existing framework contract with equivalent provisions, when required.
document_format_rules: The scientific document must imperatively follow the model published on the call website and be deposited as an unprotected PDF (PDF non protégé).
The scientific document has a maximum length of 15 pages.
The scientific document must be written in English.
The scientific document must include, in appendix, the list of scientific publications of the last three years of the proposing researchers/teams.
The administrative and financial document is supplied in Excel format (modèle) and must be signed and stamped by each partner institution.

The signature of the commitment letters integrated in the administrative and financial document certifies that partners agree to submit the project under the conditions described in that document and in the scientific document and its appendices.
No size limit, file-type list or translation rule is published beyond the unprotected-PDF and Excel-format requirements; no translation requirement is published for the submission documents.
Documents must be uploaded into the dedicated 'documents de dépôt' and 'documents signés' sections; the submission cannot be validated by the project manager until every document has been uploaded.
The ANR will disregard any file version other than the one present on the submission site at the closing time.
selection_criteria: Ambition scientifique et excellence: the structuring research question goes beyond the documented state of the art and is not a simple continuation, involving opening up disciplines and/or to non-academic stakeholders; all projects must think about their interface with society

Ambition scientifique et excellence: the combination of disciplines is justified by the scientific question, each discipline alone cannot answer the question, and the role of non-academic partners in producing knowledge is justified and not limited to dissemination
Ambition scientifique et excellence: conceptual frameworks of each discipline are put in dialogue and generate results no single discipline would have produced
Ambition scientifique et excellence: existing or newly acquired data and samples are exploited to answer new questions, using new methodologies if needed
Ambition scientifique et excellence: identifying and managing ethical issues is integral to the scientific ambition and excellence

Qualité du consortium: the project leader and co-leaders have recognised expertise in complementary fields and demonstrate capacity to coordinate an ambitious interdisciplinary consortium and/or animate transdisciplinary projects

Qualité du consortium: adequacy between staff and objectives, with the role of each academic and non-academic partner clearly defined, substantive permanent-staff involvement, and a precise role for contractual staff that demonstrates benefit to their career
Qualité du consortium: a structured maturation phase is explicitly described, with duration, budget and persons specified for its deliverables

Qualité du consortium: concrete mechanisms let all consortium members appropriate the research questions (launch seminars, shared glossaries, co-writing processes, disciplinary translation workshops), with procedures for resolving scientific disagreement and explicit strategies to overcome foreseeable limitations (fieldwork, stakeholders, data, interdisciplinarity, transdisciplinarity)

Qualité du consortium: the strategy for inventorying, acquiring and managing data and samples is described and shows what exists, what is missing and why any acquisition fills a real, non-redundant gap
Qualité du consortium: concrete and recurring mechanisms for analysing and implementing ethical follow-up
Qualité du consortium: explicit scientific and operational choices to minimise the project's environmental footprint
Qualité du consortium: sizing coherent with ambition in human resources and budget; the 0.8-3 M€ request is argued and consistent, and budget lines reflect the stated commitments
Inscription dans les défis: the project clearly addresses research issues in at least one PEPR GFM challenge and contributes to the programme's strategic priorities
Impact: expected scientific, economic, environmental and societal impacts are described and the contribution to the domains of the Stratégie nationale d'accélération is argued
Impact: modalities for sharing data and results during and after the project are described, with assured transparency of each partner's contributions
Impact: modalities of open access to scientific data are defined, the PGD strategy integrates FAIR and CARE principles and specifically addresses SHS data, and Opidor PGD links are provided
Impact: dissemination of results in academic and non-academic circles and engagement with the scientific community and the general public are described
official_details.selection_notes: Two-step gatekeeping: only proposals meeting the eligibility criteria reach the committee and can never be funded otherwise. An independent international-dimension committee convened by the ANR, possibly with external experts and possibly hearing project leaders, produces a funding-recommended list and a non-funding list with written justification per project, and may give an opinion on the requested amount. Programme directors not involved in submitted projects then propose to the SGPI the projects that could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after opinion of the CPMo and the SGPI, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by an ANR contract with the coordinating institution. Committee and external experts commit to ANR deontology and scientific-integrity rules, strict confidentiality, declaration of conflicts of interest, and a ban on using AI tools in the evaluation. The committee composition is published on the call website after selection.

important_advice_for_students: If you are a doctoral student, you cannot apply to this call yourself. It is a grant to a French institution led by a permanent researcher; your route in is to be recruited on a funded project's budget, so the practical move is to approach laboratories that are building a PEPR GFM consortium and to make your own doctoral position's role in the project explicit to them.
Do not waste time preparing a personal research proposal in the ANR portal. The portal expects a project leader depositing a two-document institutional file; individual applications are not accepted.

Read the evaluation criteria section 3.3 of the AAP before drafting - the committee scores a very specific checklist, and generic excellence statements score badly on the consortium, maturation, data-strategy and footprint criteria.
If you are an early-career researcher, the co-leadership or workpackage-lead role for post-doctorants is explicitly encouraged, but the AAP still requires the project leader to be permanent staff.

Coordinating institution outside France.
A purely disciplinary project with no genuine wide-interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary design, or where the non-academic partners only diffuse results.
No structured maturation phase with budgeted duration, persons and deliverables.
Missing data referent, ethics referent or equity/inclusion referent.
Acquisition of a new sea campaign on unprogrammed fleet means without the upstream feasibility procedure and the commission minutes.
Poorly argued budget sizing, or budget lines that do not match the commitments described (maturation phase, CS/FPPC interaction, PEPR GFM actions, PGD, environmental footprint).
A project that would cause significant environmental harm, triggering the DNSH exclusion.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The consortium's own complementary funding for everything outside the ANR grant - no other funding is mentioned for the deep-sea work itself.
Funding for companies and foreign institutions participating as partners.
Funding for the health-data reuse compute environment, unless the project budgets the Health Data Hub services.
Data processing costs on reused data must be budgeted by the project or they are simply not funded.
Publication charges and open-access fees beyond what the publication routes cover; the ANR mandates routes but does not state a dedicated APC budget line.
For recruited staff: nothing is stated about how a PhD position recruited on a PEPR GFM project compares with a state doctoral contract - confirm the contract type with the host before accepting.

records.description: The PEPR PROPSY call funds precision-psychiatry research projects in three axes: pre-clinical studies, clinical studies and mixed studies, with an indicative total envelope of about 9 600 000 € for 8 to 16 projects in 2026. The aid is paid as a grant to the coordinating institution and may finance equipment, personnel specifically assigned to the project and associated running costs, so doctoral and post-doctoral positions are recruited on project budgets rather than awarded as individual scholarships. Funded projects must target bipolar disorders, resistant and/or recurrent depressions, psychotic disorders or autism spectrum disorders, and transdiagnostic projects are assessed positively.
records.best_fit: A permanent researcher at a French research organisation, higher education and research institution, or recognised foundation of scientific cooperation, who can coordinate a 24-48 month precision-psychiatry project of 500 000 € to 2 M€ and, for the clinical and mixed axes, assemble a consortium of at least two different French research structures.
records.eligibility_summary: A permanent researcher can lead a project on one of three axes, provided the coordinating institution is French, the duration and aid amount fall inside the axis-specific bands, the project targets the four PEPR PROPSY disorders, and clinical and mixed projects involve at least two different French research structures.
eligibility: The submission file must be deposited complete on the ANR submission site before the closing date and time, and the administrative and financial document signed by each partner institution and scanned must be deposited at the date and time indicated in the call document.
The project scientific document must imperatively follow the template available on the call website and be deposited in unprotected PDF format.
Project duration must be 24-48 months for the pre-clinical axis and 36-48 months for the clinical and mixed axes.
Aid requested must be 500 000 €-800 000 € for the pre-clinical axis, 800 000 €-1 500 000 € for the clinical axis, and 800 000 €-2 000 000 € for the mixed axis.
The coordinating institution must be a French higher education and research institution, a research organisation, or a foundation of scientific cooperation.
For the clinical and mixed axes, projects are necessarily collaborative with a minimum of two different French research structures (structure identified by an RNSR number).

Beneficiaries are research organisations, higher education and research institutions, and recognised foundations of scientific cooperation described as "organismes de recherche et de diffusion des connaissances".

Private institutions contributing to public-service missions in higher education and research under article L.732-1 of the Code de l'Education may be financed after ANR analysis, MESRE opinion and SGPI validation.
Companies and foreign institutions may be associated as partners but cannot receive funding for that participation.
Pre-clinical studies may be single-team; collaborations are encouraged. Clinical and mixed projects must be collaborative.
Teams of the PROPSY "Projets Ciblés" are eligible as partners, but their coordinators are not authorised to coordinate a project in this call.
coverage: A grant (dotation) of between 500 000 € and 2 000 000 € per project depending on the axis, disbursed by the ANR to the coordinating institution according to the schedule set in the aid contract.
Indicative total envelope of about 9 600 000 € for this 2026 call, funding 8 to 16 projects; indicative per-axis envelopes of about 3 M€ (pre-clinical), 3.5 M€ (clinical) and 3.1 M€ (mixed).

Eligible expenditure is set by the PEPR financial regulation (Règlement financier des PEPR); the AAP states the aid may for example finance equipment purchases, personnel expenditure specifically assigned to the projects, and associated running costs.

Projects may build on existing national and international cohorts and databases, including the SNDS and the French Minds cohort, and the data sets mobilised must be identified and documented at submission to guarantee feasibility within the granted duration.
benefits: The existence of public and/or private co-funding, national or international, is encouraged (not mandatory) in all three axes.
Use of artificial intelligence and machine learning is explicitly encouraged for biomarker identification and validation and for new analysis methods, including in silico clinical trials.

Interdisciplinarity and the involvement of patient associations are encouraged in the mixed axis; integration of patient associations, links with industrial partners and links with other projects or programmes are assessed under the governance criterion.
Funded projects are integrated into the existing PEPR PROPSY consortium and are invited to contribute to PEPR PROPSY events.
A dedicated page will be created to make communication of the funded projects easier, with communication centralised through the PEPR PROPSY communication tools, website and social networks.
requirements: Open an account (login and password) on the ANR submission site in advance; the AAP recommends registering as early as possible.
Deposit the complete submission file electronically from the project manager's account before the published closing date and time.
Only the electronic version of the submission documents present on the submission site at the call closing time is taken into account for evaluation.
Contribute to strengthening and enhancing the capacity of French research actors, their attractiveness, their European and international influence, and their impact on the economy and society.
Produce high-quality research strengthening the acquisition of disciplinary and/or interdisciplinary scientific knowledge to address current and future precision-psychiatry issues.
Valorise the research and innovation produced, accompanying clinical implementation and/or industrialisation.
Integrate the sharing of data, results and knowledge in an open science logic.

Respect the PROPSY thematic scope: projects mainly on addictions are not eligible, except where those conditions are addressed within precision psychiatry as secondary phenomena or comorbidities of one of the four PEPR PROPSY disorders.

Integrate a humanities and social sciences dimension where relevant, for example analysis of care pathways, clinical, social or ethical acceptability of innovations, and/or the involvement of patients, affected persons or associations in the design, implementation and valorization of projects.
Signal any overlap with an already funded or submitted project and supply, where applicable, the justifications showing the absence of duplication.
Where relevant, rely on public or private co-funding, national or international: these are not mandatory but are encouraged.

For clinical studies, the data sets mobilised (cohorts, national or international databases, SNDS or existing health data warehouse data) must be identified and documented from the submission to guarantee project feasibility within the granted duration.

records.selection_notes: Only proposals meeting the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are evaluated by an independent international-dimension committee, which may use external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after transmitting questions in advance. The committee delivers to the PEPR PROPSY scientific directors a report with a list of projects recommended for funding, a list of projects it proposes not to fund for insufficient quality on at least one criterion, a written justification for every project, and possibly an opinion on the amounts requested. The PEPR PROPSY scientific directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after SGPI opinion, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (1) excellence and scientific ambition in precision psychiatry - clarity of objectives and hypotheses, innovativeness, ambition, originality, methodological or conceptual rupture against the state of the art, methodological relevance, preliminary data, project feasibility; (2) quality of the consortium, project management, resources mobilised and governance - competence, expertise and involvement of the project leader including capacity to coordinate ambitious multidisciplinary projects or consortia, academic track record, international recognition, quality and complementarity of the scientific consortium, adequacy between human and financial means and the objectives, relevance of the schedule and management of scientific risks with alternative solutions and credible milestones, relevance and efficiency of governance including patient associations and links with industrial partners or other programmes; (3) impact and outcomes - capacity to address precision-psychiatry development issues, active strategy to measure economic and/or societal impact, contribution to solutions for pathophysiological, diagnostic or therapeutic issues, dissemination and valorization strategy in itinere and ex post, adherence to FAIR and Open Science principles and promotion of scientific culture. Committee members and external experts commit to ANR deontology and integrity rules, strict confidentiality, declaration of conflicts of interest, and a ban on AI tools in the evaluation.
records.notes: Aid is a one-off exceptional allocation, distinct from recurrent institutional funding, intended for new actions, paid as a grant (dotation) to the coordinating institution. It is institutional research funding, not a personal scholarship: nothing is paid to individual students, and tuition, living costs or individual travel allowances are not covered. Consortiums without companies are not obliged to conclude and transmit a consortium agreement; where it is required (mandatory when companies are involved, otherwise when exigé), the coordinating institution must supply it to the ANR within a maximum of 12 months of contract signature, and its absence can lead to cessation of funding and repayment under article 6.6 of the Financial Regulation. Beneficiaries must guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, deliver a first PGD within 6 months of project start, deposit data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and must mention the France 2030 support with the Plan France 2030 and PEPR PROPSY logos in communications. Funded projects must send accepted publications to the PEPR PROPSY direction team for diffusion and archiving, and annual indicator reporting to the State and the ANR is required. Financial aid may constitute State aid under TFEU Article 107(1) and is subject to the French research State-aid framework 2022/C 414/01, the RDI exemption regime SA.111723, the de-minimis Regulation 2023/2831 and the 2011/20/EU decision. Projects mainly on addictions are out of scope unless addictions appear as secondary phenomena or comorbidities of one of the four targeted disorders.

official_details.description: The PEPR PROPSY "Psychiatrie de précision" is a national initiative financed under the France 2030 plan, piloted by Inserm and CNRS with the support of the Fondation FondaMental, with a budget of 80 million euros over seven years. Its aim is to transform the care of four disabling disorders: bipolar disorders, resistant and/or recurrent depressions, psychotic disorders and autism spectrum disorders. This 2026 call will finance 8 to 16 projects for a total of about 9 600 000 €, covering pre-clinical studies, clinical studies and/or mixed studies to explore physiopathological mechanisms or identify and validate biomarkers or therapeutic targets in a precision-psychiatry approach. It is one of five work packages of the PEPR, alongside the French Minds longitudinal cohort, mechanisms, new therapeutic strategies, a French biomedical industry in mental health, and training and information actions.
purpose: Refine the characterisation of psychiatric disorders and clarify their heterogeneity.
Identify new stratification, prognostic and/or treatment-response biomarkers.
Develop innovative therapeutic strategies targeted at a precise mechanism and/or a homogeneous subgroup of patients.
Structure a French biomedical sector in precision psychiatry, encouraging collaboration between public research and the pharmaceutical industry and relying on new medical and digital technologies.
Strengthen training and the attractiveness of professions related to psychiatric care and to research and innovation in precision psychiatry.
Contribute to the transformation and strengthening of French research capacity, its attractiveness, its European and international influence, and its impact on the economy and society.
Produce high-quality research and valorise the resulting research and innovation, accompanying clinical implementation and/or industrialisation.
Integrate the sharing of data, results and knowledge in an open science logic.
sdg_requirement_details: No SDG is a formal eligibility condition. The call is a health-science programme; sustainability is not among its selection criteria.

One eligibility criterion imposes an environmental test: projects that would cause significant harm to the environment (DNSH - Do No Significant Harm - principle under Article 17 of the EU Taxonomy Regulation) are excluded.

Immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit of the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, and the mandated ANR funding acknowledgement wording.
A first version of the Data Management Plan within 6 months of project start, FAIR compliant, deposited in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv with the ANR project reference.
Funded projects are integrated into the PEPR PROPSY consortium and are invited to contribute to its events.
Accepted publications must be sent to the PEPR PROPSY direction team for diffusion and archiving.
Mandatory mention of France 2030 support with the Plan France 2030 and PEPR PROPSY logos in communications and publications of results.
Annual collection of France 2030 and PEPR common indicators, and transparency and reporting obligations to the State and the ANR for ex-post evaluation.
official_details.clinical_restriction: The call is restricted to four disorders of interest: bipolar disorders, resistant and/or recurrent depressions, psychotic disorders and autism spectrum disorders. For clinical studies, included patients must present at least one of these disorders. Projects mainly on addictions are out of scope. This is a research-topic restriction, not a clinical-practice restriction on the applicant.
timeline_rules: Ouverture de l'appel : 24/06/2026 à 09:00 CEST.
Date limite de dépôt initiale : 15/10/2026 à 11h00, ensuite fixée au 10/11/2026 à 11h00 (CET) par avis publié sur la page de l'appel.
Webinaire de présentation : 26/08/2026 (présentation et FAQ publiés).
Evaluation by an independent international committee after the deposit; no publication date for results is published.
First version of the Data Management Plan within 6 months following project start.
Consortium agreement, where required, within 12 months of signature of the aid contract.

Signed and scanned administrative and financial document deposited in the 'documents signés' section at the same date and time
Consultation address for the call: https://anr.fr/PEPR-PROPSY-AAP-2026
official_details.region: France (France 2030 national programme)
coverage: Grant of 500 000 € to 2 000 000 € per project depending on the axis, for 24-48 months, paid to the coordinating institution
Project-specific personnel, equipment and associated running costs
Use of existing national and international cohorts and databases (SNDS, French Minds cohort, health data warehouses)

application_readiness_checklist: Choose the axis first (pre-clinical, clinical or mixed) and check the duration band (24-48 vs 36-48 months) and aid band (500-800 k€, 800 k€-1.5 M€, 800 k€-2 M€) - the bands are not interchangeable.
If clinical or mixed: secure at least two different French research structures (RNSR numbers) before writing, as a single-partner proposal is inadmissible.
Confirm you are not the coordinator of a PEPR PROPSY "Projet Ciblé" - those coordinators may partner but not lead this call.
Confirm the project is not mainly about addictions, and if addictions appear, frame them explicitly as secondary phenomena or comorbidities of one of the four targeted disorders.
For clinical studies, identify and document the data sets (cohorts, SNDS, health data warehouse) at submission, with the feasibility argument; the AAP makes this an explicit expectation.
Consider contacting aap@pepr-propsy.fr before drafting to confirm the thematic and structural fit - the direction team explicitly invites this.

Build the open-science, dissemination, impact-measurement and governance statements the committee scores (criterion 3 in particular: an active impact-measurement strategy is scored, not just claimed).
Prepare the three-year publication list of every proposing researcher as the scientific document appendix.
Collect signed and scanned commitment letters from all partner institutions, including the legal representative of the coordinating institution, well before the deadline.
Create the submission-site account immediately; do not wait until the last week to register.
important_advice_for_students: If you are a doctoral or post-doctoral student, you cannot apply to this call yourself; it is a grant to a French institution. Your route in is a position recruited on a funded project's budget - approach laboratories building a PROPSY consortium, and the ANR's HR indicators confirm doctoral and post-doctoral positions are expected on these projects.
Do not spend time on a personal proposal in the ANR portal; it only accepts a project leader's two-document institutional file.

If your clinical project depends on access to the French Minds cohort, check the PEPR PROPSY work-package route early, since cohort construction is a separate work package and access is not automatic.
Machine learning and AI are explicitly encouraged, not penalised - if your strength is computational, the call welcomes it, but the biomarker must be objective, quantifiable and reproducible.
common_rejection_risks: File not deposited complete before 10/11/2026 11:00 CET, or the signed and scanned partner documents missing or uploaded after the deadline.
Scientific document not on the published template, deposited as a protected PDF, longer than 15 pages, or not in English.
Aid amount or duration outside the band of the chosen axis.
Single-partner project on the clinical or mixed axis (minimum two different French research structures required).
Proposal led by a coordinator of a PEPR PROPSY "Projet Ciblé".
Project mainly about addictions, or outside the four targeted disorders.
A project that would cause significant environmental harm (DNSH exclusion).
Lack of preliminary data or a feasibility argument, particularly for clinical studies relying on external data sets that are not documented.
Weak impact and dissemination strategy, or no active impact-measurement plan (criterion 3).
Overlaps with an already funded or submitted project without a justification of non-duplication.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Funding for the international and industrial partners, who may participate but are not directly financed.
Any co-funding is encouraged but not funded by this call; the institution must source it if the budget depends on it.
Running costs beyond the grant, and any non-eligible cost under the PEPR financial regulation.
Clinical trial costs beyond what the project budgets; the AAP does not publish a separate trial-cost line.
For recruited staff: nothing is published on the contract type or salary of a PhD position recruited on a PROPSY project budget; confirm with the host.
document_audit: Scientific document: on the ANR Word template, English, unprotected PDF, maximum 15 pages, three-year publication list in the appendix.

Publications annex: completed from the ANR .docx template.

Future commitment: PGD within 6 months of start (DMP OPIDoR structured template) and, if required, the consortium agreement (mandatory with companies; otherwise within 12 months).
Where applicable: documented data-set references (cohorts, SNDS, health data warehouse) for clinical projects.

Which partner structures will be part of the consortium, and have they confirmed their commitment letters?
Do any partners include companies (which makes a consortium agreement mandatory) or foreign institutions (which cannot be funded)?
Is there an industrial or patient-association partner ready to be named, given this is scored under governance and impact?
What administrative and budget support will the project have for the Excel annex and the 15-page English template?
