records.name: Appel à projets M-ERA.NET 2026/27 - Science et ingénierie des matériaux pour l'innovation en Europe (édition 2027 pour l'ANR)
records.official_source: Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR), pour le compte du consortium M-ERA.NET
records.region: France within a transnational European and associated consortium; more than 30 national and regional funding agencies participate, and partners may come from EU member states, Horizon Europe associated countries and further participating countries listed in Annex 3 of the call text.
records.duration: Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).
records.deadline: Limite de dépôt des projets : 18/11/2026 à 12:00 CET. The two-step schedule is: "Étape 1 : 12/05/2026, 12 h 00 (CEST)" (pre-proposals, closed) and "Étape 2 : 18/11/2026, 12 h 00 (CET)" (detailed proposals). Only coordinators whose pre-proposal was recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries and who received the M-ERA.NET invitation may deposit a detailed proposal in step 2. Partners requesting ANR aid must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with the exact link and deadline communicated later by email.
records.application_period: Ouverture : 31/03/2026 à 09:00 CEST. Limite de dépôt des pré-dossiers : 12/05/2026 à 12:00 CEST (step 1, closed). Limite de dépôt des projets : 18/11/2026 à 12:00 CET (step 2, open on 2026-10-01). An information webinar was held on 18 March 2026, 12:00-14:00 CET, with presentations and the recording available on the M-ERA.NET call site.
records.description: M-ERA.NET Call 2026 (2027 edition for the ANR) is a transnational ERA-NET call co-funded by more than 30 national and regional funding agencies to fund ambitious R&D projects on advanced materials and battery technologies, supporting the European Green Deal and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The ANR funds only the eligible costs of French partners, paid directly to each partner's national or regional organisation. ANR aid ranges from a 15 000 € minimum up to 180 000 € for a non-coordinating French partner and 250 000 € for a coordinating French partner, with a 350 000 € total cap across several ANR partners, plus an optional additional 20 000 € per project for European project-preparation activities.
records.best_fit: A researcher or institution in France leading or joining a materials or battery-technology consortium of at least three funded partners from at least three different countries, whose pre-proposal was recommended in step 1 and who need French ANR co-funding for a maximum 36-month project in one of the four ANR-eligible topics.
records.eligibility_summary: A French partner may request ANR aid if the consortium has at least three funded partners from three different countries with at least two EU member states or Horizon Europe associated countries, the project matches exactly one ANR-eligible topic, the final TRL for the ANR-funded partner does not exceed 5, no single partner exceeds 60% and no single country exceeds 70% of person-months, and the aid requested stays within the ANR caps.
eligibility: The pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one (and only one) scientific collaboration theme defined in the call.
Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).

Minimum consortium composition of 3 Partners requesting funding from a funding agency listed in Annex 3 of the call text and eligible for that funding, from at least three different countries, of which at least two are EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026. Partners not requesting funding may participate if this minimum is met.
The coordinator must request funding from one of the agencies participating in M-ERA.NET Call 2026 and be eligible there.
The involvement of a single Partner must not exceed 60% of the total involvement (measured in person-months) of the proposal.
The involvement of Partners from a single country must not exceed 70% of the total involvement (measured in person-months).

If one or more Partners are not eligible (or not invited to step 2) and their total effort is equal to or greater than 15% of the total project effort (in person-months), the entire pre-proposal or detailed proposal is discarded from the selection process.
To be invited to submit a detailed proposal in step 2, the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different countries participating in the Call 2026.

A pre-proposal containing one or more Partners requesting ANR aid must clearly indicate the topic studied and the TRL levels of the tasks of each French partner in the consortium, and must be deposited on the ANR submission site in step 2, in addition to the deposit on the call site, providing all the information requested on the site.

A pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one of the ANR-eligible topics: 1. Materials for energy storage and distribution systems; 2. Materials for energy conversion; 4. Innovative functional materials with designed architectures; 6. Next-generation materials for electronics. The relevance of the proposal to the chosen topic must be clearly justified from step 1; proposals not matching these topics are rendered ineligible for ANR funding.

The final TRL of the project must not exceed 5 for an ANR-funded partner, on pain of ineligibility, and the work carried out by partners requesting ANR aid must necessarily be positioned either in the "fundamental research" segment or in the first "applied research" segment.

Partners, legal or natural persons, subject to European Union sanctions are excluded from the call; the ANR declares ineligible any partner requesting its aid who is associated within the submitted project with partners covered by a sanction measure. As of publication this concerns in particular partners from Russia and Belarus, and partners from territories of Ukraine escaping the control of the Ukrainian government. The list is non-exhaustive and may change with new EU sanctions.

A project proposal may not be similar in whole or in part to another proposal submitted to any ANR call under evaluation (all calls and all evaluation stages) or funded by the ANR. Similarity is established when the projects describe identical main objectives or result from a simple adaptation.
A researcher may request ANR aid (whether as partner, coordinator or co-coordinator) for only one proposal in the 2026/27 M-ERA.NET call.
Each project Partner must meet its own funding agency's national or regional criteria, including its TRL requirements, and must be selected by that agency to receive funding.
coverage: ANR aid of at least 15 000 € per partner, with the requested amount not exceeding 180 000 € for a non-coordinating partner and 250 000 € for a coordinating partner.
A total ANR aid cap of 350 000 € for a project with several ANR partners.

An optional additional 20 000 € per project for network-development activities, on a commitment to draft and submit, after the M-ERA.NET project, a collaborative international research proposal to calls of the next EU Framework Programme (FP10), coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner. This raises the caps to 200 000 €, 270 000 € and 370 000 € respectively.

Only the eligible costs of the Partners that have requested ANR aid are financed; the applicable funding rate and cost types are set by the ANR Financial Regulation (eligible cost sheet no. 3) and can be determined by completing the "Déclaration relative aux activités économiques des Partenaires d'un projet ANR" form.
Project duration up to 36 months.
benefits: French partners coordinating a transnational project may receive a higher ANR aid than simple partners (up to 250 000 € instead of 180 000 €).

The optional 20 000 € European project-preparation supplement, requiring a dedicated Work Package and budget under the responsibility of an ANR-funded partner and producing an extra deliverable at the end of the M-ERA.NET project.

ANR explicitly favours projects with a significant French participation and those opening and diversifying French collaboration networks, particularly with countries where France has few other opportunities than M-ERA.NET; in tie-breaks between projects of similar scientific quality within the funder group, wider and more diverse consortia may be favoured.
Access to the M-ERA.NET partner search tool (Partnersearch) and to the Materipedia database of previously funded projects and Success Stories.
requirements: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, written in English, must be deposited by the project coordinator on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site.
Use of the templates available on the M-ERA.NET site is mandatory; any unauthorised modification, in particular exceeding the page limit, may render the proposal ineligible.
The pre-proposal must be the duly completed pre-proposal form, in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions.

The detailed proposal must be the duly completed detailed-proposal form in English, complying with the mandatory layout conditions, and must include Annex 1 describing the Partner profiles together with the CVs of all consortium participants, also in English.

Partners requesting ANR aid invited to step 2 must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with information identical to the central deposit; the exact link and deadline are communicated later by email.
National and regional eligibility, selection and funding rules apply at both steps, and for some countries/regions restrictions on topics, TRL levels and the type of eligible partners apply.
The scientific and technological objectives stated in the pre-proposal cannot be modified at step 2.

It is not possible to add Partners from new countries to the consortium in step 2; only new Partners from countries already involved in the pre-proposal via a funding request to one of their funding agencies may be added.

Any change must be communicated to and accepted by the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date, with the consortium coordinator ensuring acceptance.

The scientific lead (Responsable scientifique) formally commits that their hierarchy (administrative and financial services and persons legally entitled to represent the managing institution, or their representatives) has approved the submission and that the information has been communicated to them.

French project leaders (requesting funding or not) ensure compliance with the national research professions deontology charter and the ANR deontology and scientific-integrity charter within the research activities carried out under their responsibility.

Where genetic resources are used, all participants (requesting funding or not) must respect the Nagoya Protocol obligations, and beneficiaries under the access-and-benefit-sharing regulation must provide the Due Diligence Declaration receipt by the date of the final payment.
Where relevant, take into account the sex and/or gender dimension in the research and give equitable visibility to the work produced.

Before any ANR project deposit, applicants should approach their institution's defence and security officer or PPST services to verify their project's eligibility conditions; projects with foreign public or private partners are subject to SHFDS/MESR opinion, and a negative opinion prevents selection.
records.english_requirement: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, and Annexe 1, must be written in English (rédigées en langue anglaise). The ANR also states that, on request, a translation of the evaluation criteria may be provided.
application_method: Register the intended project with the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site before the step 1 pre-proposal deadline of 12/05/2026 at 12:00 CEST (this step is closed).
Submit the pre-proposal form in English on the M-ERA.NET site, clearly stating the topic and, where ANR aid is sought, the TRL levels of each French partner's tasks.
Wait for the M-ERA.NET invitation: the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries.
Prepare the detailed proposal in English on the mandatory template, with Annexe 1 and the CVs of all consortium participants.
For ANR aid, await the email from the ANR with the exact ANR submission link and deadline, then deposit the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site.
Validate both deposits before 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET; the ANR does not require a deposit on its site at step 1.
Communicate and obtain acceptance of any change from the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date.
records.selection_notes: Evaluation and selection are centralised at M-ERA.NET level and take place in two steps: step 1 central evaluation of pre-proposals by independent international experts convened by the M-ERA.NET Call Secretariat, with invitations to step 2 issued in ranking order and taking account of the participating agencies' budget capacity; step 2 central evaluation of detailed proposals by independent international experts convened by the same secretariat. Proposals are ranked on the evaluation results and selection follows the ranking. The list of projects recommended for funding is drawn up by the group of participating funders taking account of their respective budget capacities, and the final funding decision is then taken individually by the funders concerned. Results are sent by the call secretariat to the project coordinators. Evaluation modalities and criteria are those of the call text (Guide for proposers) available on the ANR call page and the M-ERA.NET call site; the ANR adds its own horizontal objectives, which are that projects show significant French participation (in coordination or in charge of a substantial part of the work), generate significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, and are ambitious with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration. During discussions to separate projects of similar scientific quality within the funder group, projects involving a wider and/or more diverse consortium may be favoured.
records.notes: This is institutional research funding, not a personal scholarship: nothing is paid to individual students and no tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is established for individuals. The aid is paid to each partner's own national or regional organisation, not centrally. Amounts may not be increased between the two steps: increases are not authorised, and projects that do not respect the aid limits or that do not conform to any budgetary adjustments requested by the ANR are declared ineligible. The 20 000 € European-preparation supplement is conditional on adequate planning and activities within the M-ERA.NET project (a dedicated Work Package and budget under the responsibility of an ANR-funded partner), on the activities actually leading to a research proposal involving consortium members in continuity with the M-ERA.NET work, and on the follow-up proposal targeting clearly identified FP10 calls (not co-funded by the ANR) coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner; it is a subject of a final assessment and a supplementary deliverable to the ANR. Beneficiaries commit to immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit of the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, a FAIR approach to research data, a PGD within 6 months of the scientific start, deposit of data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and free-licence release and Software Heritage archiving of software. Any change affecting the whole project (extensions, consortium modifications) must be approved by all partners, their funding agencies and M-ERA.NET. Proposals may be transmitted to other administrations, control bodies and partner funders, and certain national funders are obliged to publish submitted pre-proposals/proposals, which may disclose intellectual-property or business-secret content; applicants are warned to be careful with what they include. The ANR applies the PPST protection of the scientific and technical potential of the nation to projects with foreign public or private partners, and a negative SHFDS/MESR opinion prevents selection without reasons being given.

official_details.description: More than 30 funding agencies participate in the M-ERA.NET 2026 call (2027 edition for the ANR) to finance ambitious transnational R&D projects on research and innovation in materials, supporting the European Green Deal and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. The call is structured in 6 themes, of which 4 are eligible for ANR funding. Selected projects' partners are funded directly by their respective national or regional organisations, so national and regional rules apply in addition to the call's own rules. ANR funding is paid for the eligible costs of the French partners only.
purpose: M-ERA.NET's overall aim is to offer a wide network and a powerful tool to address European and global challenges in research and innovation on advanced materials and battery technologies, supporting the European Green Deal.
Support the European Green Deal with particular attention to green energy technologies and future batteries.
Support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
Promote socio-ecological benefits in the context of responsible research and innovation (RRI).
Support the innovation chain.
Accelerate technology transfer by integrating digital tools and secure, open data management, in line with FAIR principles and a responsible and inclusive digital transformation.

Contribute to financing projects demonstrating a high level of scientific excellence and to building the European Research Area, while simplifying cooperation between researchers in participating countries.

Support projects with significant French participation, generating significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, and ambitious with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration.
sdg_requirement_details: "Soutenir les Objectifs de développement durable des Nations Unies" is one of the call's five stated horizontal objectives (with the European Green Deal, socio-ecological benefits under RRI, the innovation chain, and technology transfer with FAIR data).
"Soutenir le pacte vert pour l'Europe" is a second horizontal objective, and the supporting European Green Deal is a stated aim of M-ERA.NET.
These are published objectives of the call, and the ANR horizontal objectives add support for projects that demonstrate them; no separate SDG-compliance form is required.

document_format_rules: Pre-proposals, detailed proposals and Annexe 1 must be written in English.

Use of the templates available on the M-ERA.NET site is mandatory; any unauthorised modification may render the proposal ineligible, in particular modifications resulting in exceeding the page limit, which would breach equity between participants.
The pre-proposal must be the duly completed pre-proposal form complying with the mandatory layout conditions.
The detailed proposal must be the duly completed detailed-proposal form complying with the mandatory layout conditions, with Annexe 1 attached.
Annexe 1 must be written in English and include the CVs of all consortium participants.
The ANR parallel deposit must provide all the information requested on the ANR site and the information provided on the two deposits must be identical.
No deposit or modification of a document is accepted after the step closing date and time, for either step.
No file-size limit or additional accepted-file-type list is published in the ANR annex; the mandatory M-ERA.NET templates govern format.
The scientific and technological objectives stated in the pre-proposal cannot be modified at step 2.
selection_criteria: The evaluation modalities and criteria are those described in the call text (Guide for proposers) on the ANR call page and the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 site; a translation of the criteria can be provided by the ANR on request.

ANR horizontal objective: significant French participation within the consortia, whether in coordination or in charge of a substantial part of the research work, with a higher aid for the transnational project coordinator.
ANR horizontal objective: significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, mainly with countries where French partners have few opportunities other than M-ERA.NET.
ANR horizontal objective: ambitious projects with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration, for example in the form of other European projects.

Call horizontal objectives: support the European Green Deal, with attention to green energy technologies and future batteries; support the UN Sustainable Development Goals; promote socio-ecological benefits under responsible research and innovation; support the innovation chain; accelerate technology transfer by integrating digital tools and secure, open FAIR data management.
Projects must be designed around an effective scientific collaboration and must not amount to national projects continuing in parallel.
Tie-breaking within the funder group on similar scientific quality may favour projects with a wider and/or more diverse consortium.
official_details.selection_notes: Centralised two-step evaluation by independent international experts convened by the M-ERA.NET Call Secretariat: step 1 evaluates pre-proposals, and invitations to step 2 follow the ranking order, taking account of the participating agencies' budget capacity; step 2 evaluates detailed proposals by the same type of panel. Proposals are ranked on the evaluation results and selection is based on that ranking. The list of projects recommended for funding is established by the group of participating funders taking account of their respective budget capacities, and the final funding decision is then taken individually by the funders concerned. Results are sent by the call secretariat to the project coordinators. At ANR level, proposals that fail the ANR-specific eligibility criteria are rendered ineligible, and requested aid is assessed against the published ranges; a translation of the evaluation criteria is available from the ANR on request.
application_method: Register the project on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site and submit the pre-proposal in English on the mandatory template before 12/05/2026 12:00 CEST (step 1, closed).
For ANR aid, state the topic and the TRL levels of each French partner's tasks in the pre-proposal.
Obtain the M-ERA.NET invitation: the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries.

Prepare the detailed proposal in English on the mandatory template, describing the project as a whole and each Partner's contributions, without modifying the pre-proposal's scientific and technological objectives.
Attach Annexe 1 with Partner profiles and the CVs of all consortium participants, in English.
Await the ANR email with the ANR submission link and deadline, then deposit the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site with all required information.
Validate both deposits before 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET; no ANR deposit is required at step 1.
If any change is needed, communicate it to the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat and obtain acceptance at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date.
application_steps: 1. Set up the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission and register the consortium (step 1).
2. Write and submit the pre-proposal in English on the mandatory template, with the topic and French partners' TRL levels, before 12/05/2026 (closed step).
3. Wait for the step 1 evaluation and the M-ERA.NET invitation, which requires a recommendation by at least three funding agencies from at least three countries.
4. Assemble Annexe 1 with the Partner profiles and the CVs of all consortium participants.
5. Write the detailed proposal in English on the mandatory template, keeping the pre-proposal's scientific and technological objectives unchanged and respecting the 60% and 70% person-month caps.
6. Set the ANR aid request within the published ranges and, if applicable, plan the 20 000 € European-preparation Work Package and budget.
7. On receipt of the ANR email, deposit the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site.
8. Validate both deposits before 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET and keep the confirmations.
9. If a change is needed, obtain acceptance from the funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date.

Immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit of the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL with the mandated ANR acknowledgement, FAIR data approach, a PGD within 6 months of the scientific start, deposit of data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and free-licence software with Software Heritage archiving.

Annual or periodic reporting to both the ANR (via aap.agencerecherche.fr/) and M-ERA.NET (via the central platform or monitoring@m-era.net), with intermediate and final reports on the deadlines set in the call text and/or the aid award decision.

application_readiness_checklist: First check whether you submitted a pre-proposal by 12/05/2026 and were recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries. If not, this call is closed to you: the 18/11/2026 date accepts only invited coordinators.

Confirm the work sits in one of the four ANR-eligible topics (materials for energy storage and distribution; materials for energy conversion; innovative functional materials with designed architectures; next-generation materials for electronics). Topics 3 (surfaces, coatings and interfaces) and 5 (materials for environmental challenges) are explicitly ineligible for ANR aid.
Verify the final TRL for the ANR-funded partner stays at or below 5 and that the work is positioned in the fundamental research segment or the first applied research segment.

Check the consortium math: at least 3 funded partners from 3 different countries with at least 2 EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries; no single partner above 60% and no single country above 70% of person-months; ineligible or non-invited partners below 15% of total effort.

Set the ANR aid request within 15 000 €-180 000 € (non-coordinating) or up to 250 000 € (coordinating), total 350 000 € max; if you want the 20 000 € European-preparation supplement, plan a dedicated Work Package and budget under an ANR-funded partner now, because the supplement is assessed on that planning.
Do not change the pre-proposal's scientific and technological objectives at step 2, and do not try to add partners from new countries.
Use the mandatory M-ERA.NET templates exactly; exceeding the page limit is the most common avoidable disqualification.
Prepare Annexe 1 with the Partner profiles and the CVs of every consortium participant, in English.
Watch for the ANR email with the ANR submission link and deadline for the parallel deposit, and make sure the two deposits carry identical information.

Get your institution's approval in writing: the scientific lead formally commits that their hierarchy approved the submission, and the ANR may send the list of its deposits to laboratory directors and the institution's administrative managers.
Contact your institution's defence and security officer about PPST before depositing, since the consortium includes foreign partners and a negative SHFDS/MESR opinion blocks selection.
important_advice_for_students: Individuals cannot apply. The applicant is an institution and the money goes to a French partner's managing institution; there is no individual scholarship, tuition waiver or stipend created by this call.

If you are a doctoral student working on battery or advanced-materials R&D, your realistic route is employment on a funded partner's budget inside a consortium that has already passed step 1. Use Partnersearch and the Success Stories pages to identify active M-ERA.NET projects, then approach the French coordinator.
Do not invest time in drafting a proposal if your group did not submit a pre-proposal by 12 May 2026; watch the 2027 edition of this ERA-NET instead.

If your institution is new to EU project preparation, the 20 000 € supplement is the cheapest route to an FP10 proposal, and it is easier to obtain when the Work Package and budget are written into the step 2 proposal rather than added later.

Final TRL above 5 for the ANR-funded partner, or work outside the fundamental/first applied research segments.
A single partner above 60% or a single country above 70% of person-months.
Ineligible or non-invited partners accounting for 15% or more of total effort, which discards the whole proposal.
Exceeding the page limit or otherwise modifying the mandatory M-ERA.NET templates.
Adding partners from new countries at step 2, or modifying the pre-proposal's scientific and technological objectives.
A similar proposal already under ANR evaluation or ANR-funded, or a second ANR request by the same researcher in this call.
Requested aid outside the ranges, or an increase between the two steps.
Partners subject to EU sanctions (Russia, Belarus, certain Ukrainian territories), or a negative SHFDS/MESR PPST opinion.
Missing the parallel ANR deposit at step 2, or information differing between the M-ERA.NET and ANR deposits.

French partners working on the two non-eligible topics, who may only participate on their own funds.
Work above TRL 5 or outside the fundamental and first applied research segments, which is outside ANR scope.
The difference between the requested aid and the amount actually granted, which depends on the ANR funding rate and the individual partner's economic-activity categorisation.
Any co-funding from the institution: the ANR aid is capped and does not cover the full budget of a large consortium.

Decide on the 20 000 € European-preparation supplement now; it needs a dedicated Work Package and budget under an ANR-funded partner, and it is judged on the adequacy of that planning.
Talk to your institution's defence and security officer about PPST: with foreign partners in the consortium, a negative SHFDS/MESR opinion prevents selection.

submission_workflow: Verify step 1 eligibility and invitation status.
Write the detailed proposal in English on the mandatory M-ERA.NET template, keeping the pre-proposal's objectives unchanged and respecting the 60% and 70% person-month caps and the TRL 5 limit.
Assemble Annexe 1 with Partner profiles and all CVs, in English.
Set the ANR aid request within the published ranges and, if applicable, plan the 20 000 € European-preparation Work Package and budget.
On receipt of the ANR email, deposit the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site.
Validate both deposits before 18/11/2026 12:00 CET and keep the confirmations.
If a change is required, obtain written acceptance from the funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date.
post_award_requirements: Deliver a Data Management Plan within 6 months of the scientific start of the project.

Guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY and deposit the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL with the mandated ANR acknowledgement sentence and the ANR project reference with a Crossref DOI.

Adopt a FAIR approach to research data, deposit data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv citing the ANR project reference, and release software under a free licence with archiving in Software Heritage.
Submit intermediate and final progress reports to the ANR via aap.agencerecherche.fr and to the M-ERA.NET follow-up team via the central platform or monitoring@m-era.net.
Conclude and transmit the consortium agreement where required under ANR Financial Regulation sheet no. 4.
Obtain approval from all partners, their funding agencies and M-ERA.NET for any change affecting the whole project, such as extensions or consortium modifications.
For the 20 000 € supplement, deliver the additional deliverable showing the FP10 proposal drafted and submitted, coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner.
Ensure compliance with the Nagoya Protocol where genetic resources are used and provide the Due Diligence Declaration receipt by the final payment date where applicable.
Take into account the sex and/or gender dimension in the research where relevant and give equitable visibility to the work produced.
questions_to_ask_host: Did we submit a pre-proposal by 12/05/2026, and do we have the written recommendation from at least three agencies in at least three countries?
Are we the coordinating partner or a simple partner, and does the institution's economic-activity categorisation change the applicable funding rate or cost types?
Do we have the institution's formal approval for the submission, and who is the person legally entitled to represent the managing institution?
Has the institution run the PPST check with its defence and security officer for a consortium with foreign partners?
What is our person-month share, and does it stay below 60% (partner) and does the country's total stay below 70%?
Do we want the 20 000 € European-preparation supplement, and who will own the dedicated Work Package and budget?
Which national or regional agency funds our partner, and does it require a parallel national application beyond the M-ERA.NET and ANR deposits?
Who will prepare Annexe 1 and collect the CVs of every consortium participant?

records.name: Bourse d'excellence WBI IN (WBI Excellence Scholarship for international researchers — Wallonia/Brussels postdoctoral stay)
records.official_source: Wallonie-Bruxelles International (WBI), Service des bourses internationales
records.region: Belgium (host: Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles institutions in Wallonia and Brussels; applicants: researchers from all countries, WBI states 'WBI accueille des chercheurs du monde entier')
records.duration: Long duration: postdoctoral level, minimum 1 year, renewable once. Short duration: postdoctoral level, 1 to 3 months, renewable provided the 3-year interval between two stays is respected.
records.deadline: Long duration: 'Au plus tard le 1er février (UTC/GMT +1) précédant l'année académique durant laquelle le séjour est souhaité' with departure at the latest 1 October. Short duration: 'Au plus tard le 1er octobre (UTC/GMT +2) précédant les séjours prévus entre mars et juillet' and 'Au plus tard le 1er avril (UTC/GMT +2) précédant les séjours prévus entre septembre et février'.
records.application_period: Continuous annual cycle with three separate cut-offs. Short-duration stay of March–July 2027: file due 1 October 2026 (this is the cycle open on 2026-10-01). Long-duration stay for academic year 2027-2028: file due 1 February 2027. Short-duration stay of September 2027–February 2028: file due 1 April 2027.
records.description: WBI funds researchers from any country who hold a doctorate awarded by a foreign institution to carry out a postdoctoral research programme at a higher-education institution organised or subsidised by the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. The support is a net monthly grant of 2,120 EUR paid for the duration of the research programme, plus return international economy-class travel and health, civil-liability and repatriation insurance. WBI states explicitly that this is a monthly grant and not a salary, and that it is awarded as a mobility allowance. Priority research themes are the Marshall Plan 4.0 competitiveness clusters, though any field including humanities, fundamental or applied sciences will be considered.
records.best_fit: Researchers of any nationality who completed a doctorate outside Belgium and want a postdoctoral research stay in Wallonia or Brussels, at a maximum of 12 months spent in Belgium during the three years before applying.
records.eligibility_summary: Any researcher from any country holding a doctorate from a foreign higher-education institution who plans a postdoctoral research programme at a Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles higher-education institution, with no more than 12 months spent in Belgium in the preceding three years.
eligibility: Researchers from all countries are accepted: 'WBI accueille des chercheurs du monde entier'.

Must hold a doctorate (diplôme de l'enseignement supérieur de docteur) delivered by a foreign institution, or be a doctoral candidate still awaiting the degree (proof of success must be supplied by the published dates).
The postdoctoral programme must take place at a higher-education institution organised or subsidised by the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles.
IN candidates may have spent at most 12 months in Belgium during the three years preceding their application.
coverage: Net monthly grant of 2,120 EUR for the duration of the research programme (mobility allowance, not a salary)
Return international travel in economy class from home to the place of assignment, based on a simulation established by WBI
Health care insurance
Civil liability insurance
Repatriation insurance
benefits: Three insurances (health care, civil liability, repatriation) are taken in charge and are named separately from the grant and travel support
Travel and other non-grant costs are reimbursed, but only against a claim declaration accompanied by the supporting documents
The grant is paid monthly
Long-duration grants may be renewed once; short-duration grants may be renewed subject to the 3-year gap between stays
requirements: Application file must be complete, signed and dated
Research project written in a maximum of 4 pages
At least 2 recommendation letters on the mandatory template, sent by the referees directly to WBI
Invitation letter or agreement from the host university and the supervising research promoter
Proof that the doctorate was obtained abroad (mandatory for IN candidates)
If the project does not fit a Marshall Plan 4.0 competitiveness cluster, the applicant must comment on the possible societal impact of the project for Wallonia and the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles
Excellence IN grants may not be combined with an F.R.S.-FNRS grant or mandate
application_method: Prepare the complete file: application form, Annexes 1 to 6 and the research project, as a single and unique PDF excluding the recommendation letters
Send the complete file by email to the International Scholarships Department at bourses@wbi.be; if the annexes are too voluminous, add an online sharing link (Google Drive, WeTransfer, Dropbox, etc.)
Ensure that the file is complete, signed and dated before sending it
Have at least 2 referees email their recommendation letters, written on the mandatory template, directly to WBI

If still a doctoral candidate, supply proof of successful defence by the published date (15 July for long-duration grants of a September–August stay; 1 December for short-duration stays of March–July; 1 July for short-duration stays of September–February)
Respond to WBI within 7 calendar days of the result to accept or decline the grant
Once selected, follow the practical guide for scholarship holders sent with the grant decision
records.selection_notes: Five-stage process: administrative verification of admissibility; admissible files passed to the selection jury; jury ranking sent to WBI; WBI allocates the grants according to available budget; WBI communicates results. The jury is composed of members of the Fonds de la Recherche Scientifique (F.R.S.-FNRS), the Direction générale opérationnel 'Economie, emploi et recherche' (DGO6) of the Walloon public service, and WBI. Files are ranked in three categories A–B–C; only files rated A (with sub-categories A- and A+) by at least one jury member can be selected. Selection is based on: link to Marshall Plan 4.0 competitiveness clusters; recommendation letters; academic records; interest of the field for Walloon universities and research centres; scientific publications; added value of the intended mobility; professional career path. Results are normally issued in early June for long-duration grants, early January for short-duration stays of March–July, and early July for short-duration stays of September–February.
records.notes: The grant is explicitly NOT a salary ('ne constitue aucunement un salaire') and is awarded as a mobility allowance. Long-duration grants may be renewed once; short-duration grants are renewable only while the 3-year interval between two stays is respected. No return-home obligation is published. Award holders must acknowledge WBI support with the wording 'Avec le soutien de Wallonie-Bruxelles International' and the WBI logo on any public document, and must submit periodic reports, a final mission report and an ALUMNI form. There is no clinical or field restriction published for this programme.

official_details.selection_notes: Five stages: (1) administrative verification of admissibility; (2) admissible files transmitted to the selection jury; (3) the jury sends its ranking to WBI; (4) WBI allocates the grants according to available budgetary resources; (5) WBI communicates the results. records.name: Estonian Scholarship Programme for international students, researchers and academic staff — Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia
records.official_source: Estonian Education and Youth Board (Haridus- ja Noorteamet) and Estonian Ministry of Education and Research
records.region: Estonia (citizens of 38 listed countries)
records.duration: One academic year (2026/2027); scholarships are paid for undergraduate students for 12 months of the academic year, except for the final nominal year when the scholarship is paid for 10 months
records.deadline: 2026 application period will be open from 1st of October 2026 until October 31st 2026 (23:59, Estonian time)
records.application_period: Applications accepted 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026 (23:59 Estonian time); results announced personally by email
records.description: A monthly stipend for foreign students who already hold an admission confirmation from an Estonian higher education institution for the 2026/2027 academic year. The rate is EUR 350 per month for first-cycle (BA) and master's studies and EUR 660 per month for doctoral studies. The Board pays the scholarship to the host university, which then disburses it. The scheme is funded under bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreements and is run through the Estonian Scholarship Programme.
records.best_fit: Students from the 38 listed countries who already have an Estonian university admission letter for 2026/2027 and can fund the rest of their costs from other sources
records.eligibility_summary: Citizens of 38 listed countries admitted to an Estonian higher education institution for 2026/2027, with master's and PhD studies supported in all fields and BA only in Estonian language and culture.
eligibility: The scholarship can be applied for by foreign students who wish to study at a higher education institution in Estonia during the 2026/2027 academic year at formal studies or as an exchange student

Applications will be accepted only from students from countries whose citizenship is in the listed countries: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czech Republic, Cyprus, Egypt, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Israel, Italy, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Mexico, Moldova, People's Republic of China, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Korea, Slovenia, Spain, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Tunisia, Turkey, Ukraine, United States of America
The scholarship supports master's and PhD studies in all fields
In the first stage of higher education (BA), the scholarship can only be applied for in fields that are related to Estonian language and culture
The application should include a confirmation letter concerning the student's admission to an Estonian higher education institution with reference to 2026/27 academic year
Degree studies scholarship applicant from 2nd year upwards has to be enrolled in full time studies
coverage: Monthly scholarship of EUR 350 at first-cycle (BA) level and at master's level
Monthly doctoral scholarship of EUR 660
For exchange students, the scholarship is paid during the period of studying in Estonia, but not more than ten (10) calendar months a year, and only for exchange studies lasting more than one month
The scholarship is paid from the first day of studies until the last day of studies according to the dates approved by the host higher education institution
requirements: Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia (the strand applied for here)
The scholarship decision does not guarantee admission to the desired higher education institution — the applicant must separately meet the institution's own admission requirements
The final scholarship decision will be made after confirmation of admission
If the applicant does not start or continue studying in Estonia, they shall lose the right to the scholarship
Applications that are incomplete, drafted offhand, include false information, omit relevant information or have been submitted after the deadline will not be considered for assessment
records.english_requirement: The application is submitted in English. All submitted documents must be in English or Estonian; documents in other languages must be provided with translations into either English or Estonian.
application_method: Secure an admission confirmation letter from the Estonian higher education institution that names degree or exchange student status for 2026/27, level of study, curriculum, and start and end date of study
Complete the Education and Youth Board's 'Degree_exhange study APPLCIATION FORM 2026' Word document (the form cannot be changed)
Prepare a copy of your passport or ID card
Send one email with all required annexes attached to the Education and Youth Board address entitled "Scholarship for degree and exchange study in Estonia"
The submission email is for complete applications only
records.selection_notes: Applications shall be evaluated and the proposal for awarding the scholarship shall be made by the scholarship committee, based on the provisions of the directive and the committee's rules of procedure. Applications shall be evaluated based on the applicant's motivation (based on the letter of motivation) and the overall quality of the application — these two criteria carry equal weight. The scholarship recipients shall be approved by a directive of the Director General of the Board. The page warns the programme is highly competitive: historically only about 10% of applicants receive the scholarship, and in the 2026 application round 15 scholarships will be awarded.
records.notes: Scholarship is assigned for one academic year. Modification of scholarship periods after confirmation of the results is possible only with the written consent of the Education and Youth Board and provided that the total amount of the scholarship does not increase. Payment of the scholarship does not guarantee admission to the institution of interest. The Board has the right to check the conformity of the submitted documents with the originals. No deferrable, renewable or return-home conditions are published for this strand.

official_details.description: The Estonian Ministry of Education and Research and the Education and Youth Board offer scholarships to foreign nationals pursuant to bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreements concluded with other countries. Starting from the year 2016 the scholarships based on the international agreements are offered in the framework of the Estonian Scholarship Programme for international students, researchers and academic staff.
purpose: Offer scholarships to foreign nationals under bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreements concluded with other countries
Support foreign students studying at Estonian higher education institutions for the 2026/2027 academic year at formal studies or as exchange students
Support master's and PhD studies in all fields, and first-cycle (BA) studies only in fields related to Estonian language and culture

records.name: UC Doctoral Scholarship (UCDS)
records.official_source: Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury, Scholarships Office
records.region: New Zealand (applicants from any country, including international students)
records.duration: Up to a total of 360 points of thesis-only doctoral enrolment (three years of full-time study)
records.deadline: Applications for the October round close 15 October 2026. The round opened 20 August 2026 and is for students who intend to start their doctoral studies before 1 July 2027.
records.application_period: Two rounds a year. October round: opens 20 August 2026, closes 15 October 2026, for doctoral study starting before 1 July 2027. May round: opens 20 March, closes 15 May, for students starting in the second half of 2027. UC states applications generally open approximately eight weeks before the closing date.
records.description: The UC Doctoral Scholarship is a centrally funded Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury award that supports study towards a first research doctoral degree in any discipline at UC. Its published value is financial assistance of $32,650 per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points. The same round can add recognition-only or top-up Prestige awards, but applicants who hold one of the Core scholarships are also automatically considered for Prestige awards with no separate application, and the Prestige value is added on top of the Core value (for example a $32,650 p.a. stipend becomes $37,650 p.a. with a $5,000 top-up). It is not a New Zealand Government scholarship; it is a university award and subject to funding availability and annual review.
records.best_fit: International and domestic applicants who intend to enter their first research doctoral degree at the University of Canterbury, can start before 1 July 2027, and hold academic results equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0 over the last two years of relevant academic study.
records.funding_period: per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, up to a total of 360 points
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be entering their first research doctoral degree at UC in any discipline, with a GPA over the last two years of relevant academic study equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0, and international students may apply unless a scholarship's regulations restrict it to NZ citizens or residence class visa holders.
eligibility: You intend to study at UC towards your first research doctoral degree.
Your GPA over the last two years of relevant academic study is equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0.
The award is available in any discipline at UC.
International students can apply for any UC scholarship unless the regulations specifically restrict the scholarship to NZ citizens or holders of NZ residence class visas.
Most scholarships require that you have admission to the University, so you must also meet the criteria for admission to your research doctoral programme.

You must have also submitted your separate application for admission into your research doctoral degree programme at UC before the closing date for scholarship applications (point 2.2 of the Regulations); this is done in your myUC account.
You need to have created a myUC account prior to applying for a scholarship.
coverage: Financial assistance to a value of $32,650 per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points.
Tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points, as stated in the published value of the award.

Automatic consideration for Prestige top-up awards if awarded one of the Core scholarships, with no separate application; for example the Brownlie Scholarship and Ngata Centenary Doctoral Scholarship each add $5,000 per 120 points to the Core value, and the Roper Scholarship in Science is $30,000 per 120 points of thesis enrolment.
benefits: Recognition-only award with no extra money: the Canterbury Scholarship, which recognises high-ranked domestic recipients of a centrally funded Core UC Doctoral Scholarship.

Prestige awards that add value on top of the Core award: Brownlie Scholarship ($5,000 per 120 points top-up), Ngata Centenary Doctoral Scholarship ($5,000 per 120 points top-up), William & Ina Cartwright Scholarship (Faculty of Education, $24,500 per 120 points of thesis enrolment), Doctoral Graduate Women Canterbury (Inc.) Trust Board Scholarship ($24,500 per 120 points, Arts, Education or Health), Rātā Foundation Scholarship ($24,500 per 120 points).

The UC Commitments Doctoral Scholarship adds an additional $5,000 for research expenses across the duration of the degree, and UC Connect Doctoral Scholarships are co-funded with external agencies, but both are separate applications with their own project lists and their own closing dates (UC Commitments closes 27 October; UC Connect closes 15 September).

The UC Matariki Doctoral Scholarship and UC Pacific Doctoral Scholarship and the UC Doctoral Scholarship for Students with Disabilities are separate awards in the same round, the last running for up to 480 points rather than 360.
requirements: Applications for the following doctoral scholarships are now open and will close 15 October: UC Doctoral Scholarship (UCDS), UCDS for Students with Disabilities, UC Pacific Doctoral Scholarship and UC Matariki Doctoral Scholarship.
This application round is for students who intend to start their doctoral studies before the 1 July 2027.

With the exception of the UC Doctoral Scholarship for Students with Disabilities and the UC Connect Doctoral Scholarships, students can apply for all other Core UC Doctoral Scholarships on the single 'UC Doctoral Scholarship' application form.
You must also have submitted your separate application for admission into your research doctoral degree programme at UC before the closing date for scholarship applications.
These scholarships are subject to funding availability and are reviewed each year.

Most UC scholarships are selected on the basis of the written application and referees' reports; some require an interview with the selection panel, and the Scholarships Office will notify you if one is required.
UC states that late applications are not accepted and that the closing date is not flexible.
application_method: Search the UC scholarships database and read the scholarship's Regulations to confirm you meet every eligibility criterion.
Check the closing date for your round; UC states late applications are not accepted and scholarship applications are generally open approximately eight weeks before closing.
Create a myUC account if you do not already have one; UC states you need a myUC account before you can apply for any scholarship.
Submit your separate admission application for the research doctoral degree programme at UC in your myUC account, before the scholarship closing date (point 2.2 of the Regulations).
In your myUC account, click the 'Apply for a Scholarship' link and use the 'Search' function to find the scholarship.
Click 'Apply here' on the scholarship, which brings the application into your myUC account under 'My Applications'.
Complete the application. You can save and return to it. Attach every requested document and sign and date the privacy provisions.

Nominate your referees and make sure they know which scholarships you are applying for, the closing date, and what they must include; UC says it is your responsibility to ensure referees' reports arrive by the due date and the Scholarships Office will not follow up missing referee reports.

Submit the application before the closing date, then check that the status in 'My Applications' has changed to 'Submitted' and that you received an email confirming receipt. 'Request Pending' means the application was submitted but at least one reference is outstanding.
Await the outcome; UC states the selection process typically takes six to eight weeks but may take longer, and you will receive notification of the outcome in writing once the selection is final.
records.selection_notes: UC states that most scholarships are selected on the basis of the written application and referees' reports, that some require an interview with the selection panel, and that selection committees vary according to the scholarship. It states the selection process typically takes six to eight weeks but may take longer, and the outcome is notified in writing once selection is final. The scholarship's own selection criteria sit in the Regulations document, which is not published on the pages read here. Prestige awards are awarded from the applicants who applied for a Core scholarship in a given academic year, with no separate application, and are awarded at the end of each academic year.
records.notes: Not deferrable, not renewable, and no must-return-home or clinical restrictions are published on the pages read; treat all four as unconfirmed rather than as published terms. It is a university award, not an Australian or New Zealand Government scholarship, and UC states these scholarships are subject to funding availability and are reviewed each year. The published value is $32,650 per 120 points plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment up to 360 points; UC does not publish on these pages a statement that living costs, travel, or compulsory course fees outside thesis-only enrolment are covered, so this must not be budgeted as full funding. If you intend to start your doctoral study on or after 1 July 2027 you are in the wrong round and must apply in the next round, which opens 20 March and closes 15 May.

official_details.description: The UC Doctoral Scholarship is a centrally funded University of Canterbury award that supports study towards a first research doctoral degree in any discipline at UC. Its published value is financial assistance of $32,650 per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points.
purpose: To support students for study towards a research doctoral degree in any discipline at UC.
The UC Doctoral Scholarships collection is made up of three categories: Core, Prestige (awarded from Core applicants, value added to the Core value), and Recognition (no additional monetary value).
study_type: Research doctoral degree (thesis-only enrolment)
Full-time or part-time study load is not specified on the pages read
official_details.degree_award: A full research doctoral degree; the scholarship funds study towards the degree rather than a short-term award.
official_details.duration: Up to a total of 360 points of thesis-only enrolment. The UC Doctoral Scholarship for Students with Disabilities runs for up to 480 points.
official_details.application_cycle: Two Core UC Doctoral Scholarship rounds a year. October round: opens 20 August 2026, closes 15 October 2026, for doctoral study starting before 1 July 2027. May round: opens 20 March, closes 15 May, for students starting in the second half of 2027.
official_details.deadline_central_display: Applications for the following doctoral scholarships are now open and will close 15 October. For students who intend to start after this date, please wait and apply in the next application round (applications opening 20 March, and close 15 May).
official_details.deadline_institutional: Separate rounds inside the same page: UC Connect Doctoral Scholarships close 15 September; Core UC Doctoral Scholarships close 15 October; UC Commitments Doctoral Scholarships close 27 October. Time and day of week are not published on the page.
official_details.deadline_note: UC publishes the closing day only, with no closing time or time zone. UC separately states that late applications are not accepted and that applications generally open approximately eight weeks before the closing date. Because the October round closes 15 October 2026 and the award is for study starting before 1 July 2027, a successful applicant applies into the 2027 cohort.

official_details.home_tuition_rule: Not applicable and not published: this is a New Zealand university award for study at UC, not an award payable to an overseas institution.
official_details.host_institution_fee: The published value includes tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment only. UC publishes no separate statement on student services fees, compulsory course costs or other required expenses for the UC Doctoral Scholarship, so these remain unconfirmed.

not_covered_or_excluded: No published statement that living costs are met in full; the $32,650 per 120 points is published as 'financial assistance', not as a cost-of-living allowance.

benefits: Prestige top-up awards available from the same Core application, no separate application required: Brownlie Scholarship ($5,000 per 120 points top-up), Ngata Centenary Doctoral Scholarship ($5,000 per 120 points top-up).

important_advice_for_students: Budget from the published value only: $32,650 per 120 points plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment. UC does not publish a living-cost, travel, visa or relocation component on these pages, so do not treat this as fully funded.
Do not submit the scholarship form and hope the admission application follows; the admission application must already be in before the scholarship deadline.

records.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)
records.official_source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan - administered in-country through Japanese embassies/consulates
records.region: Japan (applicants from countries served by Japanese embassies/consulates; field and type of application vary by country)
records.duration: Embassy Recommendation: irregular course within 2 years; regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added)
records.deadline: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.
records.application_period: Applications for the 2027 cycle are handled at embassy/consulate level. MEXT lists the 2027 Embassy Recommendation Research Student recruitment under "募集中のプログラム" (programmes currently being recruited). No central opening or closing date is published; embassies set and publish their own deadlines and sit their own qualifying examinations.
records.description: The MEXT Scholarship research-student route funds postgraduate research study at a Japanese graduate school: it exempts tuition, pays a monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000, and provides round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Recipients are selected by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country after sitting that mission's Japanese and English qualifying examinations, and are then placed at a graduate school. This record covers the Embassy Recommendation route for the 2027 cohort; the separate University Recommendation route is administered by individual Japanese universities.
records.best_fit: Applicants who already hold (or are close to) a bachelor's degree and can enter a Japanese graduate school's master's or doctoral programme, who are under 35, who sit the embassy/consulate's Japanese and English examinations, and whose country runs the Research Student track.
records.eligibility_summary: Research students must be under 35 years of age and be eligible for admission to a master's programme or a doctoral programme (first or second stage) at a Japanese graduate school.
eligibility: Research students: You must be under 35 years of age and be eligible for admission to a master's program or a doctoral program (first or second stage) at a Japanese graduate school.
Embassy Recommendation: scholarship recipients are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy (or consulate general, depending on the country).

The type and field of application may vary from country to country. Please check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission in your country to see if there are any openings in the type and field you wish to apply for.
All required documents and interviews will be conducted by the Japanese embassy or other diplomatic mission abroad in your country.
coverage: Tuition exempted
Monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000 per month for research students
Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided
Preliminary training of Japanese etc.: 6 months (only those who need this training)
benefits: Preliminary training of Japanese etc. of 6 months for those who need this training, where offered by the institution
Placement into a Japanese graduate school at no application cost
requirements: Application must be made through a Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's own country (Embassy Recommendation route).
Applicants must take the embassy/consulate's qualifying examinations, which for research students are Japanese and English.
The applicant must submit a 'Configuration Preference for University of Placement' (配置希望大学申請書) as part of the application forms.

official_details.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship supports foreign students who study in higher education institutions, selected on the recommendation of Japanese Embassy/Consulate General, University, or Authority. This record covers the 2027 Research Student track under Embassy Recommendation. The Study in Japan types table gives research students: level of studies 'Graduate school level'; duration '[Embassy Recommendation] Irregular course: within 2 years; Regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added)'; preliminary training of Japanese etc. '6 months (Only those who need this training)'; field of study 'Major in field of specialty at a graduate school etc.'; scholarship '¥143,000~¥145,000 per month'; tuition 'Exempted'; travel allowance 'Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided'.
purpose: The national scholarship system exists to accept excellent students from overseas, thereby promoting international exchange and friendship, contributing to the development of human resources in foreign countries, advancing the internationalisation of universities and other institutions in Japan, improving educational and research capacity, and contributing to the internationalisation and vitalisation of society as a whole and to the development of Japan and the world.
For Embassy Recommendation, scholarship recipients are recruited and initially screened by a Japanese embassy (or consulate general, depending on the country).

Regular course or irregular course (regular course may include 6 months preliminary Japanese training where necessary)

Paying a third party claiming to process a MEXT application; MEXT warns that such organisations are unrelated to the Japanese Government.

records.name: JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan - Short-term (FY2027, 2nd Recruitment)
records.official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) - applied for by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution
records.region: Japan (candidates must be citizens or permanent residents of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan)
records.duration: 14 to 60 days
records.deadline: FY2027 2nd Recruitment (Short-term): Application deadline (from host institution to JSPS) April 23, 2027 (by 5 p.m. (JST)). The first FY2027 recruitment deadline was August 28, 2026. Note that host institutions set their own internal deadlines, which 'depending on the institution, it may have its own deadline more than one month before the application deadline set by JSPS'.
records.application_period: FY2027 2nd recruitment: host-institution submissions to JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027; selection results published in early August 2027; periods for arrival in Japan 1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028. The JSPS Electronic Application System becomes available approximately two months before each JSPS deadline.
records.description: The JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan invite mid-career and senior overseas researchers to Japan for lectures, discussions and exchange activities hosted by a Japanese researcher. The short-term option runs 14 to 60 days and covers a round-trip economy air ticket, a maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day, overseas travel insurance and a host-applied research support allowance of up to JPY 150,000. The candidate does not apply directly: a host researcher in Japan submits the application through the head of their institution.
records.best_fit: Established overseas researchers holding a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor (or researchers more than six years past a doctorate who have continuously conducted research), who already have an agreed collaboration plan with a Japanese host researcher and can spend 14 to 60 days in Japan.
records.eligibility_summary: The candidate must be a citizen or permanent resident of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan (Taiwan and Palestine treated likewise) and must hold a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor at a foreign university or research institution.
eligibility: Candidate eligibility (both conditions must be satisfied at the time of application, at the time of selection, and during the fellowship period): (1) Be a citizen or permanent resident of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan. (Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner.) Persons of Japanese nationality are eligible to apply if they have resided at the time of application in a foreign country for 10 years or longer and are judged at a host research institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community. (2) Be a full-time researcher or person with full-time researcher status at a university or research institution in a foreign country and have a position equivalent to a professor, associate professor or assistant professor in Japan (including positions such as professor emeritus). Researchers of other status may apply if it has been six years or longer since they obtained their doctoral degree and the host research institution judges them to have continuously conducted research at a foreign university or research institution.

Host researcher (applicant) eligibility: be affiliated with a research institution specified in Article 2 of the Procedure for the Handling of Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) issued by MEXT, be eligible to apply for a KAKENHI grant, and wish to host an overseas researcher.

Host researcher eligibility: be a full-time researcher. However, researchers who are not employed full time may be eligible if the host institution judges them able to execute their responsibility to carrying out the program uninterruptedly throughout the Fellow's tenure including providing them a suitable research environment (e.g. laboratory, space, facilities and personnel) in the same way that a full-time researcher would be able to do.
Selection policy requires that the applicant (host researcher) and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan.
coverage: Round-trip air ticket (economy-class), based on JSPS's regulations
Maintenance allowance of JPY 18,000 per day (Short-term)
Overseas travel insurance
Research support allowance: up to JPY 150,000, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
benefits: JSPS provides fellows with useful information on living in Japan, opportunities to foster interactions among researchers, and avenues for conducting outreach activities.
JSPS supports the Science Dialogue Program, enabling fellows to give lectures in English on their research work at high schools in the vicinity of their Japanese host institutes.
Access to the JSPS Fellows Plaza network and alumni follow-up activities after the fellowship.
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution.
The host researcher must choose the review section in which the application will be screened from the FY2027 Review Section Table, referring to the FY2027 Review Section Set.

The host institution's application must be sent to the president of JSPS by the application deadline for the programme, verified as approved by the head of the institution and confirmed that the stated requirements will be carried out if approved.
Before sending the application, the institution must check the 'List of Applications' on the JSPS Electronic Application System to verify that the registered information is correct.
A Research Proposal Document (S-2) must be completed jointly by the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate.
A Fellow's Curriculum Vitae (S-3) must be completed by the candidate.
application_method: Agree a concrete activity plan with the prospective host researcher in Japan; JSPS requires that the two 'have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan'.
The host researcher selects the appropriate category from the FY2027 Review Section Table, checking the FY2027 Review Section Set for the paired reviewers.
The host researcher obtains approval from the head of their institution and collects the candidate's S-3 Curriculum Vitae, then completes S-2 jointly with the candidate.
The host researcher submits the application through the JSPS Electronic Application System by the host institution's internal deadline, which may be more than one month before the JSPS deadline.
The host institution transmits the application to the president of JSPS by the JSPS deadline (5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027 for the FY2027 2nd recruitment).
JSPS conducts a document review by three examiners, then a panel review; results are published in early August 2027 for the 2nd recruitment.
The fellow arrives in Japan within the published arrival period (1 October 2027 - 31 March 2028 for the 2nd recruitment).
records.selection_notes: Selection of the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Reviewers with a potential conflict of interest are removed, and all Review Committee Members must comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners per application, using a graduated 1-5 scale (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor), taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged document-review score is the primary screening criterion for panel review. Two selection judgements are made: Selected and Not-selected.

official_details.description: The programs provide excellent researchers from other countries an opportunity to conduct collaborative research, discussions, and opinion exchanges with researchers in Japan. These programs are intended to help advance the overseas researchers' research activities while advancing science and promoting internationalization in Japan. JSPS Invitational Fellowships for Research in Japan consists of two options of Long-term, and Short-term. Grantees are selected by going through the selection process following the submission of applications by a host researcher in Japan who wishes to invite a researcher from overseas via the head of their university or institution. The recruitment and selection for the Long-term program is announced and conducted once a year, and twice a year for the Short-term.

selection_criteria: Short-term selection policy item 1: That the collaboration will contribute to advancing science in Japan and other countries.
Short-term selection policy item 2: That the collaboration can be expected to advance research in the subject field. Evaluation should place emphasis on researchers invited from other countries.
Short-term selection policy item 3: That the applicant (host researcher) and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete activity plan.
Short-term selection policy item 4: That the host institution has adequately prepared a system for receiving the candidate.
Short-term selection policy item 5: That the plan can be carried out within the period of the candidate's fellowship tenure.

Short-term selection policy item 6: That the plan has as its objective lectures, discussions or other exchange activities held not only in the host institution but also in some other institutions. That the plan also includes instructive opportunities to foster young researchers.
Short-term selection policy item 7: That, as much as possible, unbalance should avoided in the selectees' nationalities, host institutions and areas of specialization.
Short-term selection policy item 8: That not only the score of the document review but also the examiners' reasons and comments are to be given adequate consideration.
Short-term selection policy item 9: That the number of selectees with Japanese nationality be no more than about 3% of all the selectees under one recruitment for an application deadline.
Short-term selection policy item 10: That two selection judgements be made: (1) Selected and (2) Not-selected.
official_details.selection_notes: Selection of applicants (host researcher) and candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Any reviewer with a potential conflict of interest is removed from the Review Committee for the relevant review, and all Members are obliged to comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners for each application, using a graduated scoring system on a scale 1 to 5 (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor). Marks are made on a comprehensive basis taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity, and future potential of the research. The averaged score in the document review is used as the primary screening criterion in the panel review, through which a specified number of applicants are selected in each of the panel review sections.

Confirm you hold a position equivalent to Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor, or that it is six or more years since your doctorate and your host institution judges you to have continuously conducted research.
