records.description: The Young Leaders' Program is a Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarship that brings young government officials from designated countries to Japan for a one-year Master's course in public policy at GRIPS, awarding the Master of Public Policy degree. Funding covers a monthly scholarship of ¥242,000, full tuition exemption and round-trip airfare, and the programme requires the fellows to return to their home administration after graduation.

official_details.description: Young Leaders Program (YLP) was introduced by the Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology in 2001. GRIPS runs two courses: School of Government, introduced in 2001, and School of Local Governance, started in 2009. The programme awards a Master of Public Policy degree, is taught in English, runs for one year with October enrolment and September graduation, and the scholarship for international students is the Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarship. In the Study in Japan types table, YLP students are shown with: level of studies 'Master course at a graduate school', duration '1 year', preliminary training of Japanese etc. 'None', field of study 'Master course at a graduate school', scholarship '¥242,000 per month', tuition 'Exempted', travel allowance 'Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided'. YLP is the one MEXT scholarship type available only by recommendation from official overseas recommending organizations - neither embassy recommendation nor university recommendation is shown for it.
purpose: Foster future national leaders in designated countries.
Build up comprehensive human networks among the leaders of nations.
Establish friendly relationships among the countries involved, including Japan.
Improve the quality of policy making in the participating countries.
Expand students' comparative as well as historical knowledge of international/regional politics and economics while providing them with an in-depth understanding of Japanese politics and economy.

On GRIPS's own statement: 'The Young Leaders Program (YLP) is a scholarship program launched by MEXT in 2001. YLP contributes to the cultivation of future national leaders in Asian and other countries, to building human networks among the leaders of each country, and to promoting friendship among the countries involved, including Japan.'

application_readiness_checklist: Find your country on GRIPS's published list of recommending authorities and identify the specific ministry or agency for the School of Government and/or the School of Local Governance.
Be under 40 years of age (in principle) and already hold a university or college degree.
Build at least three years of public-administration work experience in your home country; GRIPS states this is a prerequisite in principle.
Start the process early: the application window is historically July to October, and nomination by your authority will take time.
Contact your Japanese embassy or consulate general as well, since MEXT routes all scholarship procedures through embassies/consulates or Japanese institutions.
Never pay an application fee or deposit; MEXT states the application is free and that anyone charging fees or deposits has no relation with the Japanese Government.

Prepare to articulate, in your application, your potential to become a future leader at home, your role in your country's development, and your capacity to sustain friendship and trust with Japan and other countries - these are GRIPS's published admission appraisal criteria.
Note the timeline: October enrolment, September graduation, results announced the following April.
important_advice_for_students: You cannot apply to GRIPS directly for this scholarship - YLP is available only through official overseas recommending organizations, and the Study in Japan table marks both embassy and university recommendation as 'No' for this type.

Read the published YLP Brochure for 2027-2028 rather than assuming prior-year requirements; the brochure is the cycle-specific document.
Plan for the Japanese-language component: the programme runs in English but the MEXT table describes the track as including Japanese language education.
Budget separately for anything not listed as covered, including accommodation; the pages read do not establish that rent is covered.
Both School of Government and School of Local Governance run; check which one your nominating authority is listed for, since the authority lists differ by country and course.
common_rejection_risks: Being 40 or older at the point of application.
Applying directly to GRIPS or MEXT instead of going through a nominating authority - the track is closed to direct applications.
Coming from a country with no listed recommending authority, or from a ministry not listed for the course being applied to.
Insufficient public-administration work experience; GRIPS states a minimum of three years in the field in the applicant's home country is a prerequisite in principle.
Missing your nominating authority's internal timetable, since no central deadline is published and the window is short.
Not being able to demonstrate the published appraisal criteria: leadership potential, contribution to national development, and sustaining friendship and trust with Japan.
Paying a third party claiming to process a MEXT application.

records.description: The Korean government-invited scholarship degree programme that funds a year of Korean language training followed by an associate degree (2-3 years) or bachelor's degree (4-6 years) at a designated GKS university in Korea. The published benefits list is airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition and monthly allowances. Selection runs through two routes: an Embassy Track that applies through the Korean embassy/consulate, and a University Track in which the student applies directly to a GKS-designated university (UIC specialisation and Associate Degree).
records.best_fit: Non-Korean nationals under 25 who hold a high-school diploma (bachelor's track) or are entering an associate degree programme, and who meet the published academic-performance threshold; also international students from R-GKS partner countries applying through the Embassy Track.

records.description: KAIST's own scholarship for international graduate students, selected as part of the admission application rather than as a separate scholarship application. It covers full tuition fees plus national health insurance and a monthly stipend, and 94% of KAIST's international student body receive it. Two higher tiers are awarded automatically to those selected: the KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship (KRW 1,000,000 per month for 4 regular semesters) and the KAIST Prestige Scholarship for International Ph.D. Students (KRW 300,000 per month for 8 regular semesters). The published cost-of-study table shows the student still carries on-campus housing, food, books, travel and telecommunications costs.
records.best_fit: Non-Korean nationals applying to KAIST master's, Master's-Ph.D. integrated or Ph.D. programmes who meet KAIST's English proficiency requirement (or a published exemption) and can satisfy a doctoral or master's-level qualification by the start of the course.
records.eligibility_summary: Open to international applicants for KAIST graduate programmes who are citizens of countries other than Korea, hold a bachelor's degree (master's/Master's-Ph.D.) or a master's degree (Ph.D.) by the start of the course, and provide a qualifying English proficiency test score unless a published exemption applies.

records.english_requirement: KAIST's official language of communication and instruction for international students is English. All applicants must provide at least one English proficiency test score, and the scores must be valid as of the online application deadline. Published minimums: TOEFL iBT 83 (taken before 21 Jan 2026) or 4.5 (taken on or after 21 Jan 2026); IELTS Academic 6.5 band; TOEIC 720 (Listening & Reading, TOEIC Public Testing Program); TEPS 326. TOEFL institutional code 0195, department code 99; Home Edition accepted; iBT MyBest Scores are NOT accepted; IELTS Online is accepted but IELTS One Skill Retake is NOT accepted; test scores from Institutional Testing Program (ITP) are NOT accepted. Exemption: no EPT score is required if you hold citizenship of, or have physically studied and completed a bachelor's-equivalent or higher qualification at an institution physically located in, Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Malta, New Zealand, St Kitts, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad and Tobago, the U.K. or the U.S.A. A further exemption applies if you hold citizenship of one of a listed group of countries AND have physically studied and completed a qualification equivalent to a bachelor's degree or higher in English as the medium of instruction at an institution physically located in one of those countries, in which case a certificate from the school attended indicating English as the medium of instruction (e.g. English Lecture Certificate) must additionally be provided. Applicants expecting to graduate from regular KAIST degree programmes in the semester before the intended course also do not need to provide a score. Programs that do not require an EPT score: GDI-ITTP track, KINS-KAIST.
application_method: Check the published admission window for your entry term (Spring: mid August - early September; Fall Early: early December - late December; Fall Regular: early March - late March)
Create an ApplyWeb account and complete the KAIST International Graduate online application
Select the KAIST scholarship option as your financial resource in the application
Request your recommendation letter through the KAIST online Letter of Recommendation system during the designated submission period
Submit the application before the online application deadline (the EPT score must be valid as of that deadline)
If selected, you are automatically considered for the KGPS and/or KPS; no separate scholarship application is needed
Respond to the offer, register for school, prepare the certificate of admission and apply for a student visa
records.selection_notes: Scholarship status is decided inside the admission process: applicants who select the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource in the application are automatically considered for the KAIST Scholarship and, where the degree programme matches, for the KGPS or the KPS. For the KGPS, no separate application is made and only highly competitive applicants will be recommended by the department head. For the KPS, applicants demonstrating outstanding academic and research achievements receive recommendations from the department head, with final selection by the college dean. KAIST states that 94 percent of its international students benefit from the scholarship and that the scholarship rate may vary by student.
records.notes: Not a standalone scholarship application: the award is attached to admission. The monthly stipend of the base KAIST Scholarship is stated to be dependent on research involvement, and no base stipend figure is published; KAIST also states the stipend amount may vary depending on individual colleges, with the College of Engineering publishing its own stipend terms separately. The KPS stipend for Master's-Ph.D. integrated entrants begins at the start of the Ph.D. programme, not on entry. The published Cost of Studying at KAIST figures are for the 2023 academic year. The Global Technology Innovation Program (GDI-GTIP Track) is excluded from KAIST Scholarship applications.

official_details.description: KAIST offers a simple yet generous scholarship program specifically designed for international students. The KAIST Scholarship covers full tuition fees and provides stipends, benefiting 94% of our international student body. This support is often complemented by research opportunities, enabling most students to achieve financial self-sufficiency and minimize their dependence on external funding. International applicants who select the KAIST scholarship as their financial resource during the admission application process will be automatically considered for the following scholarship programs, based on their chosen degree program or major.

records.description: KAIST awards its scholarship automatically to every admitted international undergraduate student, with no separate application: the applicant simply ticks "KAIST scholarship" on the Statement of Financial Resources section of the admission application. The award pays tuition exemption for 8 semesters, a living allowance of 350,000 KRW per month, and medical health insurance. It is not full funding: KAIST's own cost table shows the scholarship offsets 11,738,360 KRW of a 14,885,680 KRW essential annual budget, leaving roughly 3,359,000 KRW per year for housing, food and books.

records.name: ICSSR Participation in International Seminar Abroad (Travel Grant Scheme)
records.degree_levels: Doctoral, Postdoctoral, Research (faculty and doctoral/postdoctoral scholars)
records.official_source: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education, Government of India
records.region: India (Indian social science scholars; conferences held outside India)
records.duration: Period of stay abroad not exceeding the actual days of the conference plus travel dates
records.deadline: Applications can be submitted online throughout the year. The applications should be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference.
records.application_period: Rolling - applications are submitted online throughout the year, and must be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference.
records.description: This scheme gives partial financial assistance to Indian social science scholars who have been formally invited to present a paper at an international conference abroad. Assistance covers air travel, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance, maintenance for the stay, and registration fee up to US$200. Regular faculty receive up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit, while SC/ST faculty, persons with benchmark disability, and postgraduate/doctoral/postdoctoral researchers without salary protection may be considered for the full cost of the visit.
records.best_fit: Indian social science scholars (faculty, PhD scholars, postdocs, and some independent senior professionals) with a formally accepted oral paper at a high-value international conference outside India, who need help with the cost of attending.
records.eligibility_summary: Indian social science scholars in regular service at a UGC-recognized university/deemed university/college, an Institute of National Importance, or an ICSSR research or recognised institute, holding a PhD, or post-graduate/PhD/post-doctoral scholars at an advanced stage of study, or certain independent senior professionals.
eligibility: Faculties with regular service in public funded Universities/Deemed-to-be-Universities/Colleges, Institutes of National Importance as defined by MoE / UGC, and ICSSR Research Institutes/Recognized Institutes having a PhD degree are eligible to apply.
Post-Graduate (Regular)/PhD/PDF scholars in Social Science disciplines who are in the advanced stage of their studies/research are eligible to apply.

Independent scholars having served as Civil servants, officers from Defence services, and other professionals with a social science perspective having not less than 20 years of regular service and demonstrable research experience through publications of books/research papers/reports/policy documents, etc. may also apply.
coverage: Air travel (economy class, purchased through the three government approved travel agencies)
Visa fee
Travel insurance
Local conveyance
Maintenance costs for the period of stay abroad (not exceeding the actual days of the conference plus travel dates)
Registration fee up to US$200

Up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit for regular faculty; the full cost of the visit may be considered for SC/ST faculty, persons with benchmark disability and PG/doctoral/postdoctoral researchers without salary protection, and for faculties from ICSSR Research Institutes/Recognised Institutes
benefits: Preference is given to younger scholars, scholars attending a conference or seminar for the first time, and scholars from remote and backward areas.

Invitations from global subject associations, reputed international organisations, universities or institutions are given preference, and due consideration is given to the peer review process used by the conference organisers.
requirements: The application will be considered only when the paper for oral presentation has been accepted by the organiser of the Conference through a formal invite. A formal invitation letter should be submitted along with the application. A simple email will not be considered as a formal invite.
The submission of the full length paper to be presented is mandatory and it should be either in English or Hindi.

Applications should be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference; the application will not be entertained or considered in any case after participation and presentation of the paper in the Conference.
If the paper is co-authored, priority will be given to the first author, but a No Objection Certificate(s) from the second author(s) may be procured and attached with the application.
Air tickets (economy class) must be purchased only from M/s Ashoka Travels and Tours (ATT), M/s Balmer Lawrie & Company Ltd (BLCL), or Indian Railways Catering & Tourism Corporation Ltd (IRCTC).
Application for the second time will be considered only after a gap of three years, and a scholar can avail of the award only twice in his/her lifetime.
It is mandatory to buy tickets through the three government approved travel agencies; it is the scholar's own responsibility to arrange travel, visa and accommodation.
records.english_requirement: The full length paper to be presented is mandatory and should be either in English or Hindi.
application_method: Obtain a formal written invitation to present an oral paper at the international conference.
Submit the online application at https://app.icssr.org/ at least three months before the Conference due date.
Send the hard copy of the application along with all documents to the In-charge, ICG Division, ICSSR, Aruna Asaf Ali Marg, JNU Institutional Area, New Delhi 110067.
Applications are screened by the ICSSR Secretariat, then reviewed by an Expert Committee.
Expert Committee recommendations are placed before the Research Committee/Council for final approval.

After the visit, submit the original boarding pass, attendance certificate, statement of expenditure and a participation report duly forwarded by the Supervisor/Head of the Department/Centre, for reimbursement.
records.selection_notes: Applications are initially scrutinised by the ICSSR Secretariat; an Expert Committee then reviews the applicant's research background, the quality of the paper to be presented and the academic credentials of the organising institution; recommendations go to the Research Committee/Council for final approval. The Council reserves the right to reject any application without assigning any reason and is not responsible for postal delays or loss.
records.notes: Not deferrable: the application will not be entertained or considered in any case after participation and presentation of the paper in the Conference. Not renewable in the sense that a scholar can avail of the award only twice in his/her lifetime, and a second application is considered only after a gap of three years. No must-return-home rule is published because this is a travel grant, not a degree award. Post-award: expenditure is reimbursed on submission of the original boarding pass, attendance certificate, statement of expenditure and a report on participation; ICSSR may ask for a copy of the tickets booked and the visa obtained before departure. Publication is expected in high valued journals/edited books/impactful reports with due acknowledgement of ICSSR, and the paper presentation should clearly display the ICSSR logo and its support. A second time application is not considered for poster presentations, session chairs, conveners, rapporteurs, or workshop/training/refresher/summer/winter course attendance.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your paper has been formally accepted for ORAL presentation, and obtain a formal invitation letter - an emailed acceptance that the ICSSR does not accept as a formal invite is the single most common disqualifier.

Make sure you are not applying for a poster presentation, to chair a session, as a convener or rapporteur, or to attend a workshop, training, refresher, summer or winter course - all of these are expressly ineligible.
Work backwards from the Conference due date: the online application must be uploaded at least three months before it.
Write or finalise your full-length paper in English or Hindi - submission of the full paper is mandatory.
If the paper is co-authored, you are most likely first author; obtain No Objection Certificates from the other author(s) and attach them.

Do not buy air tickets yourself before you know the award position, and when you do, use only Ashoka Travels and Tours, Balmer Lawrie & Company, or IRCTC - economy class.
Do not skip the hard copy. The online submission is not sufficient; the printed application with all documents must reach ICSSR, and ICSSR is not responsible for postal delay or loss.
Remember the lifetime cap: you can take this award at most twice, and a second application is only considered after a three-year gap.

A No Objection Certificate is to be procured and attached where the paper is co-authored; priority is given to the first author.

alerts.trigger: As soon as your paper is accepted for oral presentation
alerts.message: Start the ICSSR online application immediately - you must upload it at least three months before the Conference due date, and the hard copy must still reach New Delhi.

alerts.trigger: Three months before the Conference due date
alerts.message: Hard stop. After this point the online application can no longer be considered.
Submit the original boarding pass, attendance certificate, statement of expenditure and forwarded participation report to claim reimbursement - applications are never considered after presentation.

alerts.trigger: If you won this award before
alerts.message: Check the three-year gap and the two-in-a-lifetime limit before applying.

submission_workflow: Secure formal written acceptance for an oral presentation from the conference organiser.
Finalise the full-length paper in English or Hindi.
Register on and submit the online application at https://app.icssr.org/ at least three months before the Conference due date.
Upload the invitation letter, the paper and any co-author No Objection Certificates.
Obtain institutional forwarding/signature from the Head of Department or supervisor.
Post the printed application with all enclosures to ICG Division, ICSSR, New Delhi 110067.
After award, book economy-class air tickets through ATT, BLCL or IRCTC.
Attend, present with the ICSSR logo displayed, and publish the paper with ICSSR acknowledgement.
post_award_requirements: Book and use only government approved travel agencies for air tickets.
Display the ICSSR logo and its support on the paper presentation and acknowledge ICSSR in any resulting publication.
Submit a detailed participation report plus copies of air ticket, visa, visa payment receipt, registration fee receipt, original boarding pass and certificate of participation.
Retain the original boarding pass - the grant is reimbursed, not paid in advance.
Be ready to produce booked ticket copies and visa proof if ICSSR asks before departure.
Expect ICSSR to reserve the right to publish the presented paper if required.
questions_to_ask_host: Is my invitation a formal invite that ICSSR will accept, and will they issue it in writing to me?
Is my presentation confirmed for oral delivery rather than a poster?
What are the conference due date and the actual dates of the conference, so I can work back three months?
Is the conference organised by an Indian organisation? If so, this scheme does not apply.
What is the total registration fee, given the US$200 cap?
Is the peer review process of the conference one that ICSSR would give due consideration to?
What travel agency arrangements does the conference recommend, so I can stay within the three government approved agencies?

records.name: University of Sharjah Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) Scholarship for Master's Students
records.official_source: University of Sharjah
records.region: United Arab Emirates (open to UAE nationals and non-nationals, with a separate CGPA threshold published for each)
records.duration: Tied to enrolment in a full master's degree programme; continuation is subject to the bylaws and regulations of the University of Sharjah. No scholarship duration is published.
records.deadline: Applications for Master's programs will be open from 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026.
records.application_period: Master's applications are open 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026 for the published 2026/2027 intake. The University publishes no separate RA/TA scholarship application window; it states that meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee a scholarship and that selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability and approval.
records.description: The University of Sharjah offers work-based Research Assistant and Teaching Assistant scholarships to eligible master's students, who must commit 20 hours per week at the University and may not be employed elsewhere during the scholarship period. The award is awarded by the concerned academic department based on its academic and research needs and available opportunities. The official page read does not publish the benefit amount, whether tuition is waived, or any list of expenses the scholarship covers, so this record is deliberately left unquantified rather than assumed to be full funding.
records.best_fit: Master's applicants with a very high undergraduate CGPA — 3.60 out of 4.00 for non-nationals, 3.20 for UAE nationals — who can commit 20 hours a week and are not employed elsewhere, and who can apply to a programme that is not on the published exclusion list.
records.eligibility_summary: Master's students holding a bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.60 out of 4.00 for non-nationals or 3.20 for UAE nationals, committed to 20 hours of work per week at the University and not employed outside it.
eligibility: Hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.20 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for UAE national students, and 3.60 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for non-national students.
Be committed to working 20 hours per week at the University as part of the scholarship requirements.
Not be employed outside the University during the scholarship period.
Meet any additional requirements established by the concerned academic department and the University.

Regular master's admission also requires a bachelor's degree or equivalent from a university recognized by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MoHESR), a minimum CGPA of 3.00 out of 4.00, and a bachelor's degree in a field relevant to the intended master's program.
coverage: No coverage list is published on the official page read. The page states only that the University offers Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) scholarships to eligible Master's students, subject to the University's applicable bylaws, regulations, and available opportunities.
requirements: Scholarship eligibility and continuation are subject to the bylaws and regulations of the University of Sharjah.
Remedial courses are not covered by the scholarship.
Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee the award of a scholarship; selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability, and approval.
The concerned academic department reserves the right to select eligible candidates based on its academic and research needs and the applicable selection criteria.
Applicants to Master's programs taught in English must obtain TOEFL iBT 79, TOEFL PBT 550, or IELTS Academic 6.0.
The University does not accept Home Edition or other online home-based English language proficiency examinations.
AED 500 non-refundable application fee.

Applicants nominated for admission must reserve their seat by paying AED 10,000 within the specified deadline; the amount paid is applied toward tuition fees upon enrollment, and on withdrawal or non-enrollment AED 5,000 is non-refundable.
records.english_requirement: Applicants to Master's programs taught in English must obtain one of the following minimum scores: TOEFL iBT 79; TOEFL PBT 550; IELTS Academic 6.0. Applicants to the Master of Applied Sociology, Master in Private Law, Master in Public Law, Master in Conservation Management of Cultural Heritage, and Master of Arts in Applied Criminology and Criminal Justice must either obtain a minimum TOEFL ITP score of 450, or its equivalent, or a minimum IELTS Academic score of 4.5, or successfully complete the prescribed English language course (ESL - 0 credit hours) during the first semester; students who do not satisfy the requirement by the end of the first semester will not be permitted to continue in the program. For Master's programs taught in Arabic, English language proficiency is not required unless specifically required by the selected program. English language proficiency test results are valid for two years from the date of the examination. The University does not accept Home Edition or other online home-based English language proficiency examinations.
application_method: Discover your program and select a college to view the master's programs and specializations offered.
Check your eligibility against the regular and conditional master's admission requirements.
Complete the required English language test, or provide official proof the bachelor's degree was taught in English.
Get your documents ready (passport, certified bachelor's certificate and transcript, photograph, Emirates ID, recommendation letters, MoHESR equivalence where applicable).
Explore scholarships and benefits, including RA/TA scholarship eligibility and the programme exclusion list.

Submit the online application through the University of Sharjah Online Admission Portal, upload all required documents, and pay the AED 500 non-refundable application fee between 5 October 2026 and 12 November 2026.
If nominated for admission, reserve the seat by paying AED 10,000 within the specified deadline.
records.selection_notes: The concerned academic department reserves the right to select eligible candidates based on its academic and research needs and the applicable selection criteria. Selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability, and approval; meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee the award of a scholarship.
records.notes: The scholarship carries a 20 hours-per-week work commitment at the University, and the holder must not be employed outside the University during the scholarship period. Remedial courses are not covered. Nine master's programmes are barred from RA/TA eligibility (all five Master of Dental Surgery programmes, Master of Science in Leadership in Health Professions Education, Master of Leadership in Higher Education, Executive Master in Business Administration, Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD)), and the Master of Science in Molecular Medicine and Translational Research is eligible for Research Assistant scholarship only. No deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction terms are published. No tuition, housing, insurance or travel coverage is stated on the official page read, and the AED 500 application fee and AED 10,000 seat reservation are not described as scholarship-covered.

official_details.description: Work-based Research Assistant and Teaching Assistant scholarships offered by the University of Sharjah to eligible master's students, in exchange for 20 hours per week of work at the University. Awarded by the concerned academic department under the University's bylaws, regulations and available opportunities.
purpose: The University of Sharjah states that it offers Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) scholarships to eligible Master's students, subject to the University's applicable bylaws, regulations, and available opportunities.
The stated purpose is academic: the scholarships support master's study while students contribute 20 hours per week of research or teaching work to the University.
The University states that meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee the award; selection is driven by departmental academic and research needs.
study_type: Master's degree programmes; the University lists master's programmes as Full Time and/or Part Time and publishes no mode restriction for RA/TA scholarships.
official_details.degree_award: Full degree - the award is attached to enrolment in a master's degree programme, not a short-term award.
official_details.application_cycle: Master's admission for the 2026/2027 intake is open 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026. The University publishes no separate RA/TA scholarship cycle; the scholarship is tied to master's admission.
official_details.deadline_central_display: Applications for Master's programs will be open from 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026.
official_details.deadline_note: No separate RA/TA scholarship deadline is published. The master's admission closing date (12 November 2026) is the only published date, so it is used as the central deadline; this is an admission window, not a separately announced scholarship closing date.
official_details.funding_label: Research Assistant (RA) / Teaching Assistant (TA) Scholarship
official_details.tuition_rule: Not published on the official page read. The page states the University 'offers Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) scholarships to eligible Master's students, subject to the University's applicable bylaws, regulations, and available opportunities', and that 'Scholarship eligibility and continuation are subject to the bylaws and regulations of the University of Sharjah.' No tuition waiver, tuition reduction or tuition obligation is stated.
official_details.host_institution_fee: AED 500 non-refundable application fee is payable to the University with the master's application, and nominated applicants must pay AED 10,000 to reserve a seat (AED 5,000 non-refundable on withdrawal or non-enrollment). The page does not state that either amount is scholarship-covered.
covered_expenses: Not itemised on the official page read. The award is described as a Research Assistant / Teaching Assistant scholarship requiring 20 hours per week of work at the University; no expense list, stipend figure or tuition treatment is published.
not_covered_or_excluded: Remedial courses are not covered by the scholarship.

Programmes not eligible for RA/TA scholarships: Master of Dental Surgery in Orthodontics; Master of Dental Surgery in Oral Surgery; Master of Dental Surgery in Endodontics; Master of Dental Surgery in Periodontology; Master of Dental Surgery in Prosthodontics; Master of Science in Leadership in Health Professions Education; Master of Leadership in Higher Education; Executive Master in Business Administration; Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD).
The Master of Science in Molecular Medicine and Translational Research is eligible for a Research Assistant scholarship only and not for a Teaching Assistant scholarship.

No tuition, housing, health insurance or travel coverage is stated for the scholarship; the AED 500 application fee and the AED 10,000 seat-reservation deposit are not described as scholarship-covered.
Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee an award - the department may decline even eligible candidates.
eligibility: Hold a Bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.20 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for UAE national students, and 3.60 out of 4.00 (or equivalent) for non-national students.
Be committed to working 20 hours per week at the University as part of the scholarship requirements.
Not be employed outside the University during the scholarship period.
Meet any additional requirements established by the concerned academic department and the University.
general_eligibility: Hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification from a university recognized by the UAE Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MoHESR).
Have a minimum CGPA of 3.00 out of 4.00, or its equivalent, for regular admission.
Hold a Bachelor's degree in a field relevant to the intended Master's program.

Conditional admission is available at CGPA 2.50-2.99 (max 6 credit hours in the first semester, minimum CGPA 3.00 and no grade below C+) and for applicants whose bachelor's degree is in a different field (prerequisite or remedial courses of up to 24 credit hours, minimum grade C, completed within two consecutive semesters).
Applicants must meet the English language proficiency requirements of the selected program, where applicable.
ineligibility_conditions: Enrolment in any of the nine master's programmes excluded from RA/TA scholarship eligibility (all Master of Dental Surgery specialisms, Master of Science in Leadership in Health Professions Education, Master of Leadership in Higher Education, Executive Master in Business Administration, Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD)).
Teaching Assistant scholarship is not available to students in the Master of Science in Molecular Medicine and Translational Research (Research Assistant only).
Employment outside the University during the scholarship period disqualifies the holder.
A bachelor's CGPA below 3.60 out of 4.00 for non-national students, or below 3.20 for UAE national students, does not meet the published scholarship threshold.
Home Edition and other online home-based English language proficiency examinations are not accepted.

For the five programmes with a lower English threshold, failure to submit a qualifying score or complete the prescribed ESL course by the end of the first semester means the student will not be permitted to continue in the program.

official_details.international_eligibility: Non-UAE national master's applicants are eligible to apply; the published minimum CGPA for non-national students is 3.60 out of 4.00 (or equivalent). records.description: The Programa Portugal-Berkeley is an FCT call, run with FLAD and UC Berkeley, that supports doctoral students to spend a research stay as Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley for up to six months. FCT launches the call to promote the internationalisation of Portuguese science and to foster research exchange between Portuguese universities and UC Berkeley in areas of mutual scientific interest. The selected candidate's home institution (CPS) is responsible for the administrative procedures to acquire the Visiting Student Researcher status and pays the University Services Fee, the DS-2019 visa processing fee and the Institute of European Studies administrative fees at UC Berkeley. The selected candidate must arrange and financially cover their own travel, accommodation and health insurance, and the call publishes no direct stipend or award figure.

Applications are grouped by submission date into quarterly assessment windows; each window produces a positive or negative opinion with a weighted final classification
records.selection_notes: Assessment is carried out by an academic committee appointed by FCT and FLAD. Criterion A: candidate's curriculum, considering academic grades, track record and scientific achievements including peer-reviewed publications, scholarships, prizes, conferences and project participation (40%). Criterion B: scientific quality, innovative character of the work plan and feasibility of the research activities to be developed (30%). Criterion C: motivation letter explaining the relevance of the stay and the work to be developed for the scientific ambition of the doctoral work plan, and the expected impact of the stay on the candidate's career (30%). Selection is based on the analysis of these criteria, producing a positive or negative opinion, with final classification CF = 0.4 A + 0.3 B + 0.3 C.
records.notes: Applications are open on a rolling basis and are assessed in quarterly windows, so an application can be submitted at any time before closing; the call closes early if the annual quota is reached. Selected candidates must finance their own travel, accommodation and health insurance. Arrival at UC Berkeley cannot occur earlier than six months after selection for the programme. The call is governed by the published Expression of Interest Call (Chamada de Manifestação de Interesse) and the accompanying documents (Memorandum of Understanding Portugal_Berkeley_Program, FCT-CPS-Berkeley Protocol, model letter, Research Scholarships Regulation, Table of Scholarship-related Subsidies (2025), and the assessors' college).

records.deadline: Application period: 1 November to 1 February & 1 June to 10 August. First application cycle opens on 1 November and closes on 1 February of the following year; second application cycle opens on 1 June and closes on 10 August of the following year.
records.application_period: Two cycles a year: 1 November to 1 February (outcomes from mid-April) and 1 June to 10 August (outcomes from mid-November). A*GA may consider off-cycle applications on a case-by-case basis.
records.description: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS) funds up to four years of PhD or EngD study at an autonomous university in Singapore, jointly supervised by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member, with research conducted at an A*STAR Research Institute. Support published for up to 4 years comprises full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment. Monthly allowance is a published matrix by track and residency status: AGS (STEM) $4,500 for Singapore Citizens, $4,100 for Singapore Permanent Residents and $3,600 for International Students; AGS (Specialised Tracks: Semiconductor, Quantum, Computing) $6,200, $5,600 and $5,000 respectively.
records.best_fit: Final-semester undergraduates and Master's students at, or on track to graduate from, a Singapore autonomous university, and mid-PhD students already enrolled in a Singapore autonomous university, who want to do a research-intensive PhD at an A*STAR Research Institute. International students without Singapore Permanent Residence should be comfortable with a 3-year service commitment in a Singapore-based company.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants of all nationalities may apply, but international students must have completed or be on track to obtain a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a Singapore autonomous university, hold at least a Second-Class (Upper) Honours degree or equivalent, be in the last semester of final studies (full-term) or minimally one semester into a Singapore AU programme (mid-term), and satisfy PhD admission criteria at an autonomous university.

records.selection_notes: Referees can be academic referees from universities or supervisors/PIs whom you have worked with. There will be at least 2 rounds of interviews involving the senior management of the Biomedical Research Council or Science & Engineering Research Council, and researchers from A*STAR's Research Entities. The nomination of supervisor(s) has to be approved by A*STAR; in most cases the main and co-supervisors should hold at least the designation of Principal Investigator or Principal Scientist at an A*STAR RI. Final approval of the PhD supervisor(s), research project and university for successful applicants is subject to A*STAR's approval. A*STAR makes a holistic assessment of each application and takes into consideration factors such as achievements in science/maths related competitions and CCAs; prior research experience helps but is not mandatory. The application process typically takes about 5 months from submission of a complete application to notification of results.
records.notes: Bond-free for Singapore citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents. Foreigners who are non-SPRs must serve a 3-year service commitment in Singapore-based companies, without commitment to any specific organisation; Singapore-based companies refer to local companies and international companies that have a base in Singapore and which is registered with the Accounting & Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA). The area of work should preferably be in Biomedical Sciences, Physical Sciences, Engineering or Computing and Information Sciences. Not deferrable within the 4-year funding period without approval: if you need more time to complete your PhD you will have to seek approval from A*STAR's management for your PhD extension. A*STAR does not pay for consumables or research fees; fees involved in the lab should be borne by the university. All scholars need to seek A*STAR's written permission before changing your course of study/research project. Mid-term applicants receive the same terms of support as full-term AGS awardees from the point of the award, with retrospective payment for all tuition fees and/or any compulsory fees from Year 1 of study onward. All rates/allowances are subject to adjustments by A*STAR from time to time. A pre-application Master's degree is not required.

official_details.description: Whether you're looking to explore broad scientific fields or dive deep into a specialised area, AGS offers full funding, access to world-class research labs, and the chance to take on a 12-month overseas attachment during your PhD. Begin your research journey at an A*STAR Research Institute, and shape the future of science, technology, and innovation.
purpose: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (STEM): enabling aspiring researchers to pursue PhD studies in biomedical sciences, chemistry, physics, engineering, and related fields. Scholars gain research experience at A*STAR and contribute to impactful work.

A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (Semiconductor): supporting students in chip design, materials science, and semiconductor technologies. Scholars gain hands-on experience and help Singapore grow as a global hub for semiconductor talent and innovation.

A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (Quantum): advancing talents in quantum computing, communications, and sensing. Scholars drive cutting-edge research and discoveries that strengthen Singapore's position in quantum technologies.

A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (Computing): nurturing leaders in AI, cybersecurity, software engineering, and data science. Scholars tackle real-world digital challenges and build expertise to power Singapore's growth as a tech-driven nation.
AGS is a collaboration between A*STAR and local Autonomous Universities (AUs). Scholars will be jointly supervised by both the A*STAR and University supervisors.
The research proposal should align with your research interests and contribute to Singapore's Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) ecosystem.

records.description: The Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships place three Fellows per year for 12 months in the executive offices of the African Development Bank (Abidjan), the UN Economic Commission for Africa (Addis Ababa) or the International Trade Centre (Geneva). Fellows work on research and policy design and receive direct mentorship from the head of the host organisation. The Mo Ibrahim Foundation funds the position; the Foundation's own programme page states a stipend of $100,000. This is a professional work placement, not a degree-granting scholarship, so no tuition is paid.
records.best_fit: African nationals with a master's degree and at least seven years of relevant work experience who want senior-level policy exposure in a continental or multilateral institution.

records.selection_notes: The host's Human Resources department vets applications to draw up a shortlist of ten files, which the Foundation then reviews; a shortlist of three candidates is put to the head of the host (for the AfDB route, the President of the Bank or a designate) for final selection. Only applicants who fully meet the requirements and are considered for interview are contacted.
records.notes: This is a work placement, not a degree programme: the contract is for one (1) year and is not renewable, and the Fellow is not a regular employee of the host and gains no right to employment. For the AfDB route the Fellow is barred from applying for a staff position at the Bank for one year from the end of the Fellowship. records.official_source: The Mandela Rhodes Foundation
records.region: South Africa (study must be in South Africa) - for citizens of any African country
records.duration: Maximum two years of funding; one year for an Honours degree, one or two years for a Masters
records.deadline: Applications for 2028 will open 9 March 2027. Applications close by the end of Wednesday, 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2.
records.application_period: The applications timeline runs from March to November of each year for the following year's intake. For the Class of 2028: applications open Tuesday 9 March 2027 and close 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2.
records.description: The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship funds a one-year Honours degree or a two-year Masters degree in any field at a recognised South African institution of higher education, and pairs it with a compulsory Leadership Development Programme of residential workshops and regional pods. The Foundation states it offers comprehensive funding for the core costs of study: tuition and registration fees, a study materials allowance, research and conferencing grants on request, a medical aid allowance, accommodation and meal allowances, a personal allowance, and economy-class flights between the scholar's home country and their South African institution at the start and end of the degree. The Foundation does not pay university application fees, SAQA accreditation of existing degrees, or visa application costs. Specific allowance amounts are set by the Foundation and no figures are published.
records.program_type: Foundation postgraduate scholarship with leadership development programme
records.best_fit: African citizens aged 19 to 29 in the year of applying, with an undergraduate degree above 70% or an upper-second class Honours, who intend to study an Honours or Masters degree in South Africa and can commit to the compulsory leadership programme.
records.eligibility_summary: Citizen of an African country, aged 19 to 29 in the year of applying, with an undergraduate degree completed by 1 January 2028 with above 70% or upper-second class results, and able to study at postgraduate level in English.

I aspire to be an ethical leader and I am committed to using my talents to advance equality, freedom and human dignity in Africa
I admire Nelson Mandela's ability to bridge divides and bring people together around our common humanity
I am prepared to reflect deeply on my own leadership and undergo a process of personal change and growth

records.selection_notes: The Foundation looks for young leaders who aspire to leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship, and who demonstrate the combination of intellect and character. Applicants are screened in rounds: a notification by mid-July indicates whether the applicant reached Round Two, by end of July for Round Three, and by end of August whether they are invited to a Final Round interview. Final Round interviews are conducted in South Africa in October, and final-round applicants based outside South Africa are flown in for an in-person interview with the selection committee. Selected scholars are notified by the end of October.
records.notes: The scholarship cannot be deferred: you must accept it for the year it is offered. Attendance at the residential workshops and regional pods is mandatory and a condition of the scholarship, and the Foundation will not accept travel outside South Africa, even for research purposes, as a reason for absence. You may not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities and may not do paid work for more than 12 hours a week. The award is conditional on you being offered a place at a South African institution, and the Foundation does not apply to universities for you. If you are not accepted by a South African institution in time, you cannot accept the scholarship. The Foundation does not pay visa application costs, and states that a delayed visa may mean you cannot start on time and could lose the scholarship. Applicants from outside South Africa may need SAQA verification, which the Foundation states can take 4-8 weeks and is not covered by the award. Any amount you owe prior to becoming a Scholar is your sole responsibility. The Foundation does not fund MBAs, block courses, or courses delivered predominantly online, and distance learning is not allowed.

records.deadline: Every year, the application portal for our flagship TEF Entrepreneurship Programme opens on the 1st of January till midnight on the 1st of March at Midnight, on our digital platform, www.TEFConnect.com.
records.application_period: The application window opens on 1 January and closes at midnight on 1 March each year, for that year's cohort. The next published window after 2026-10-01 is 1 January 2027 to midnight 1 March 2027.
records.description: The TEF Entrepreneurship Programme is the Tony Elumelu Foundation's flagship annual programme for African entrepreneurs, combining business management training, mentorship, coaching and a USD 5,000 non-refundable seed capital award. The application is completed on the TEFConnect digital platform and the business assessment test score determines eligibility. Selected participants complete training modules on TEFConnect, submit a business plan, financial projection and pitch video, and then provide business registration, tax and banking documents before the seed capital is paid into their business account. This is a business grant and training programme, not a scholarship, so no tuition or living costs are paid.

records.selection_notes: Independent third-party experts review eligible applications. A minimum score in the business assessment test is required or the applicant is notified as ineligible and encouraged to reapply the following year. Eligible applicants undergo LSEG World-Check global compliance screening and a physical verification exercise by authorised enumerators, which may be in person or virtual. Shortlisting is evaluated on business feasibility, market opportunity, financial understanding, scalability, and leadership and entrepreneurial skills. In the investment readiness phase an independent audit consulting firm reviews the business plan, financial projection and pitch video and ranks participants for investment readiness. Shortlisted participants are notified of participation on the 22nd of March each year.
records.notes: The seed capital is non-refundable and is not a scholarship: it does not pay tuition or living costs, and applicants must fund their own living expenses throughout the cycle. The portal is only open for two months a year, 1 January to midnight 1 March; there is no rolling intake, so missing the window means waiting a full year. You cannot have previously benefited from any TEF programme, and you cannot reapply within the same application window of the same year, which the Foundation states explicitly. Programme participants whose documents are found inauthentic, contain discrepancies, or match the document details of past TEF Entrepreneurship Programme beneficiaries are immediately disqualified. Seed capital payment requires signing the seed capital undertaking and is processed into the business account you provide.

The application is completed on the TEFConnect digital platform and the business assessment test score determines eligibility. Selected participants complete training modules on TEFConnect, submit a business plan, financial projection and pitch video, and then provide business registration, tax and banking documents before the seed capital is paid into their business account. records.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program enables highly talented, service-oriented young people to pursue higher education and is delivered through partner universities and non-governmental organisations rather than through a single central application. Financial support includes tuition fees, accommodation, books and other academic materials, mentoring, counselling, leadership development, and a return air ticket to the Scholar's country of origin if necessary, alongside psychosocial and academic support. records.name: The Inlaks Fellowship for Social Engagement
records.degree_levels: Not a degree programme (open to Indian bachelor's-degree holders and early to mid-career professionals)
records.official_source: The Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation
records.region: India (applicant country: India)
records.duration: Two years, with a six-month probation period and quarterly and annual review of the Fellow's work
records.deadline: Applications for the fellowship can be submitted latest by 15th November 2026 by 11.59 PM IST; both the Mentor and Referee letters must also be submitted by 15th November 2026, 11:59pm
records.application_period: Applications open for the 2027 cohort (opening date not published on the page); closing 15 November 2026, 11:59pm IST. Shortlisted candidates announced by the last week of February 2027, final interview within a fortnight, final fellows announced by the last week of March, fellows expected to begin work from 1 May 2027
records.description: The Inlaks Fellowship for Social Engagement is a two-year, non-degree award from the Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation that lets young Indians pursue self-directed work on an issue of public importance under a mentor of their choice. It pays a monthly stipend that varies by cost-of-living category: INR 45,000 in an 'X' category area, INR 35,000 in a 'Y' category area and INR 25,000 in a 'Z' category area, with the final amount at the Foundation's discretion. It supports individual learning only, not organisational work, and fellows must attend three Foundation-hosted workshops at regular intervals.
records.best_fit: Indian citizens residing in India, born on or after 1 January 1991, who hold a bachelor's degree from a recognised Indian institution (or have at least three years of relevant work experience) and want two years to do self-directed research, cause lawyering, grassroots journalism, community-rights, public-health or ecological work.
records.eligibility_summary: Indian citizens residing in India, born on or after 1 January 1991, who are graduates of a recognised Indian institution or have at least three years of relevant work experience, and who are not enrolled in academic study or a PhD for the fellowship period.
eligibility: The applicant must be an Indian citizen currently residing in India.
The applicant must be born on or after 1st January 1991.
The applicant must be a graduate (hold a Bachelor's degree) from a recognised institute/university in India.
In the absence of a Bachelor's degree, they must carry at least three years of relevant work experience.
Those enrolled in academic studies/PhD for the duration of the fellowship are NOT eligible to apply.
Applicants proposing to work on art installations, photo books etc. are not eligible to apply for this fellowship.
coverage: Monthly fellowship stipend for two years, at INR 45,000 / 35,000 / 25,000 per month depending on whether the fellow is living and working in an 'X', 'Y' or 'Z' category area (final amount at the Foundation's discretion)
No tuition, travel, health insurance or equipment costs are listed as covered by the award on the published pages
benefits: Attendance at three workshops hosted by the Foundation at regular intervals during the fellowship
Support to pursue the fellowship project under a mentor of the applicant's own choice
requirements: Complete all questions in the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS)
Enter name, address and latest contact information correctly
For the 'Topic of your project' field, describe the fellowship activity in a few lines so that it correctly represents the nature of the project
Statement of purpose and work plan must be completed in the Foundation's own format and uploaded as PDF only
Your Statement of purpose and work plan must not exceed 1000 words each
The statement of purpose must outline the applicant's personal and professional trajectory very briefly, and the motivation for taking up the project and how it contributes to social change

The work plan must include a title of the proposed work with a concise description of the work or research planned during the fellowship, the expected outcomes, and in detail the manner in which the project will be undertaken with a clear timeline for 2 years
Two letters are required: a Mentor endorsement letter and a Recommendation letter

The Mentor endorsement letter must include a brief description of the mentor's work experience, the mentor's contact details (email and official address), a statement of why the mentor endorses the applicant's work plan, a statement that the mentor agrees to supervise the applicant's work during the fellowship, willingness to review and comment on quarterly and annual progress reports, and willingness to hold periodic meetings with the Foundation so it can assess the fellow's progress

The Letter of Recommendation must elaborate the nature of engagement with the applicant (in what capacity they engaged with the applicant) and the reason why the referee would like to recommend the applicant and the work plan

records.application_period: Cycle-based: applicants apply directly to a listed EPOS postgraduate course for the published intake year (the current DAAD programme list is headed 'List of Application Deadlines for Intake 2027/2028'); the course's own committee then nominates candidates, who are invited to upload to the DAAD portal for the final selection.
records.description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Scholarships are awarded subject to funding being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
records.best_fit: Graduates from DAC-listed developing and newly industrialised countries who hold a Bachelor (normally a four-year course) with above-average results (upper third), have at least two years of professional experience after that degree, and can prove a development-related motivation tied to their work in a public authority or company.
records.eligibility_summary: Graduates with at least two years' professional experience from DAAD-listed developing and newly industrialised countries, who hold a relevant Bachelor degree with far above average results and whose degree is normally not more than six years old.

application_method: Step 1: Send your complete application directly to the postgraduate course you have chosen.

Step 4: The selection process is finalised and the suggested candidates are informed accordingly.
records.selection_notes: Selection is by independent, voluntary selection committees. Candidates must fulfil the academic requirements and be expected to complete the study programme successfully (above-average first academic exam, top performance in the third, language skills), hold a relevant Bachelor degree, have at least two years' professional experience, and prove a development-related motivation. Special circumstances such as a disability may be taken into account.
records.notes: The scholarship call is made subject to the provision of funds by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), so funding is not guaranteed by the DAAD itself. Applications sent to the DAAD are not forwarded and will not be considered - the course must be applied to directly. Applicants resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline are excluded. Degrees should normally not be more than six years old. Some courses require additional documents. DAAD scholarships do not have to be paid back.

records.description: MOPGA is a French Government visiting fellowship that pays a monthly allowance to early-career foreign researchers to carry out a 12-month research project in a French host laboratory on climate and environmental themes. Each fellowship covers a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, and health, civil liability and repatriation coverage. Host laboratories receive no funding under the programme; the money is intended solely to cover the invited researcher's living expenses, and international travel costs are not covered.

records.selection_notes: Selection takes place in two stages: scientific experts appointed by the French Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space in the relevant fields assess the applications received, then a scientific committee makes the final selection. Innovative approaches involving advanced technologies within the eligible research areas are given particular consideration during the selection process.
records.notes: The fellowship is not renewable and lasts exactly 12 months. International travel costs to France are not covered by the programme; the host laboratory may be able to help but is not funded to do so. The award cannot be combined with a French employment contract (research contract or postdoctoral contract) or any other individual funding from a French government entity. A PhD defended after December 2026 is not eligible. If the doctoral degree certificate has not yet been issued, an official certificate confirming the defence, proof of thesis submission, or another official institutional document is accepted. For researchers who obtained their PhD more than five years ago, the eligibility window may be extended by 18 months per child, or by the actual duration of maternity leave, on submission of supporting documents noted in the application file. Only projects with a genuine integrated 'One Health' approach qualify under the human, animal and environmental health theme; projects focused solely on medicine or human health are not eligible.

records.name: AAPG - Appel à projets générique 2027 (ANR Generic Call for Proposals 2027)
records.official_source: Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR)
records.region: France (project applicants in the French research system, with international bilateral collaborations via the PRCI instrument)
records.duration: Project duration set by the applicant; grants are awarded annually across the project period
records.deadline: Clôture du dépôt et enregistrement Etape I : 13/10/2026 à 17:00 CEST
records.application_period: Call opened 16 July 2026 at 09:00 CEST. Step 1 submission and registration closes 13 October 2026 at 17:00 Paris time. Step 1 results are notified mid-February 2027; step 2 runs from end February 2027 (template and IRIS opening) with submission closing end March 2027; selected projects are announced July 2027.
records.description: The AAPG is the ANR's main competitive call and it funds project-based research in every scientific field, including recruitment of doctoral students (contrats doctoraux) and young researchers on successful projects. It runs through five funding instruments: JCJC (young researcher), PRME (single-team project), PRC (collaborative project), PRCE (socio-economic partnership project) and PRCI (bilateral international collaboration project). This is a research-team funding instrument, not an individual scholarship: a doctoral contract is only available to a student recruited onto a project that has been selected for funding.
records.best_fit: Principal investigators and research teams based in a French institution who can submit a project through the IRIS portal by the step 1 deadline and who intend to recruit doctoral students as part of the funded project.
records.eligibility_summary: All scientific communities and all public or private actors involved in French research may apply through one of five funding instruments, choosing one of 57 research axes.
eligibility: Open to all scientific communities and to all public or private actors involved in French research
Covers all scientific fields and all disciplines, including fundamental, exploratory and finalised research

Structured into 57 research axes, each corresponding to a scientific evaluation committee (CES) of the same name: 38 axes within 7 disciplinary domains and 19 axes on cross-cutting trans- or interdisciplinary issues
Coordinators choose the funding instrument (JCJC, PRME, PRC, PRCE, PRCI) when submitting or registering the project; this choice cannot be changed during the selection process
For the PRCE instrument in step 1, no scientific document is required: only the online project characterisation form and the CVs of coordinators and partner scientific leads must be completed

For PRCI collaborations, only the PRCI annexes confirm whether the collaboration is open and under which submission modality; mandatory step 1 registration applies in ANR Lead Agency and non-Lead Agency modalities
coverage: Project-based research funding awarded through the JCJC, PRME, PRC, PRCE and PRCI instruments, which can include recruitment of doctoral contracts
benefits: Additional funding opportunities exist for JCJC and PRCI projects selected in previous editions (Percée JCJC and Jeton MRSEI respectively) to help teams move towards European funding
Projects on the AAPG 2026 complementary list that are resubmitted in AAPG 2027 step 1 are automatically invited to step 2 without scientific committee assessment, subject to eligibility
requirements: Step 1 submission and registration must be completed on the IRIS portal before 13 October 2026 at 17:00 CEST

The ANR-FRQ (Franco-Quebec) PRCI collaboration is suspended for the 2027 edition

records.selection_notes: Coordinators choose the research axis and thus the scientific evaluation committee at submission; the choice cannot be changed during the selection process. PRCE step 1 registrations that meet the step 1 eligibility criteria receive an automatic invitation to step 2 without assessment of the scientific value of the registration by the scientific evaluation committees. Step 1 results are notified to coordinators mid-February 2027; a right of reply to reviews opens on IRIS in week 20 of May 2027; the list of projects selected for funding is published in July 2027. PRCI selection requires joint agreement of both funding agencies, each of which ultimately funds the teams of its own country.
records.notes: This is a research-project funding call, not an individual scholarship: there is no personal application route and no scholarship awarded directly to a student. A doctoral contract arises only when a selected project recruits a doctoral student. Funding amounts per instrument are not stated on the call page and must be read in the AAPG 2027 call text (anr-aapg-2027.pdf) and the ANR financial regulations; they are deliberately left unstated here. Projects ranked on the AAPG 2026 complementary list may have to change their partnership to meet the new PRC criteria for the 2027 edition. Applicants selected for funding at the 2026 edition must cancel their AAPG 2027 PRCI registration or JCJC/PRME/PRC submission or PRCE registration by email to aapg.science@anr.fr.

records.official_source: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), Overseas Fellowship Division, International Program Department
records.region: Japan (applicants: citizens of any country that has diplomatic relations with Japan, plus Taiwan and Palestine)
records.duration: 12 to 24 months
records.deadline: FY2027 2nd recruitment: April 23, 2027, 5 p.m. JST, submission from the Japanese host institution to JSPS. FY2027 1st recruitment closed on August 28, 2026.
records.application_period: Two open calls per year. FY2027 1st: application deadline August 28, 2026 (5 p.m. JST), results late December 2026, arrival windows April 1 - September 30, 2027, 120 fellowships. FY2027 2nd: application deadline April 23, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results early August 2027, arrival windows September 1 - November 30, 2027, 120 fellowships.
records.description: JSPS funds postdoctoral researchers from overseas to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher at a university or other eligible research institution. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000, and overseas travel insurance. A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows can also be applied for through the host institution to cover cooperative research-related expenses. Because this is a research appointment rather than a degree programme, there is no tuition to pay and the award is not presented as tuition funding.
records.best_fit: Researchers who received a PhD within the past six years (maternity and parental leave time is subtracted) and who can secure a host researcher and host institution in Japan before applying.

records.duration: 1 to 12 months
records.deadline: FY2027 2nd recruitment: January 8, 2027, 5 p.m. JST, submission from the Japanese host institution to JSPS. FY2027 3rd recruitment: June 4, 2027, 5 p.m. JST. The FY2027 1st recruitment closed on September 25, 2026.
records.application_period: Three open calls per year. FY2027 2nd: application deadline January 8, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results mid-May 2027, arrival August 1, 2027 - March 31, 2028, 20 fellowships. FY2027 3rd: application deadline June 4, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results late September 2027, arrival December 1, 2027 - March 31, 2028, 20 fellowships. The JSPS Electronic Application System opens approximately two months before each period.
records.description: This programme brings PhD students and PhD researchers from North America and Europe to Japan to conduct collaborative research under the guidance of a Japanese host for between one and twelve months. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month for PhD holders or JPY200,000 per month for non-PhD holders at the start of the research in Japan, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000 for fellows with three or more months of tenure, and overseas travel insurance. A research support allowance for cooperative research-related expenses is applied for by the host researcher. The award is a research fellowship, not a degree scholarship, so no tuition is funded.
records.best_fit: PhD candidates and PhD researchers based in the US, Canada, EU countries, the UK, Switzerland, Norway or Russia who have not previously done research at a Japanese university and can arrange a Japanese host.
records.eligibility_summary: Candidates resident in an eligible North American or European country who obtained a doctoral degree within the past six years as of April 1 of the fiscal year, or who are enrolled in a doctoral course and expect a PhD within two years of the fellowship start date.
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an eligible country, or have been engaged in research continuously for at least three years at a university or research institution in an eligible country (eligible countries: US, Canada, EU countries, UK, Switzerland, Norway and Russia); Taiwan and Palestine are also treated as eligible

Have obtained a doctoral degree from a foreign graduate school and, as of April 1 of the fiscal year, be within six years of having obtained that degree, or be currently enrolled in a doctoral course at a foreign graduate school and expect to receive a Ph.D. within two years from the start date of the fellowship period
Whether or not the candidate is employed in a full-time position is not considered

Researchers who have continuously carried out research for three or more years, or obtained their PhD within six years, minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave (every four weeks counted as one month)
A person who has never engaged in research at universities etc. in Japan would be most preferable

Those who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard (P), Short-term (PE), Short-term (PA), or Pathway to University positions in Japan (PU)) are not eligible
Those who have resident cards with mailing addresses in Japan at the application deadline set by JSPS are not eligible
A Japanese citizen who is also a permanent resident of an eligible country is not eligible
A selected fellow needs to submit an original copy of the doctoral degree certificate or diploma, or the prospect certificate if the degree is not yet obtained, before the fellowship starting date
The host researcher must be a full-time researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution and may submit up to three applications

records.description: The POSCO TJ Park Foundation awards a scholarship to international students admitted to a master's or doctoral programme at a designated Korean graduate school and recommended by that institution. Benefits published are full tuition, living expenses of KRW 1,000,000 per month, a one-time settlement fee of KRW 1,000,000, National Health Insurance premium, Korean language education support, and cultural programmes. Master's students receive full tuition for 4 semesters and living expenses for 22 months; doctoral and integrated master's and doctoral students receive full tuition for 6 semesters and living expenses for 36 months. Twenty students are selected per year, subject to change.
records.best_fit: Non-Korean nationals from the published eligible-country list who apply to and are admitted by a designated Korean graduate school, and who can obtain that university's recommendation.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold or expect to hold a bachelor's degree, hold non-Korean nationality, be admitted to a master's or doctoral programme at a designated Korean graduate school, and be recommended by that institution.

Eligible universities are listed as tentative: KDI School of Public Policy and Management, Korea University, POSTECH, Seoul National University, The Academy of Korean Studies, Yonsei University
Applicants may apply for majors in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences/engineering

records.official_source: Secretaría de Ciencia, Humanidades, Tecnología e Innovación (Secihti) and Organización de los Estados Americanos (OAS)
records.region: Mexico (beneficiaries must be nationals of OAS Member States other than Mexico)
