records.application_period: Publicación de la convocatoria: 28 de agosto de 2026. Secihti sends the compliant list to the OAS on 28 August 2026; award committee deliberates 3 September 2026; direct notification 4-10 September 2026; formalisation 7-18 September 2026; process closes 30 November 2026.
records.description: A complementary support awarded jointly by the OAS and Mexico's Secihti to students who already hold a Secihti National Scholarship for a full-time postgraduate programme in Mexico. The OAS contribution is a single payment of USD 1,200 for settling-in expenses in Mexico, paid in Mexican pesos at the official exchange rate on the day OAS deposits it, and the number of supports depends on OAS funds. Secihti adds its monthly support under the Secihti 2026 National Scholarship Scale plus ISSSTE medical service. records.description: The GS/OAS and the Universidad del Desarrollo in Chile fund USD 3,400 of the USD 3,800 total course fee for a 4-month online certificate in Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship (dLab Global 2026), focused on SDG 13 climate action. The selected candidate remains responsible for USD 400 of the course fee, plus study materials or equipment, internet access, and any additional fees not included in the offer. Living costs, travel and insurance are not addressed at all in the announcement, so this is not full funding and there is no stipend to live on.
records.best_fit: Young professionals from OAS Member States other than Chile who have a business management background, a strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship, and can commit about 4.5 hours a week in English to a fully online course.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of an active OAS Member State other than Chile, be proficient in English, have a strong business management background, and commit to paying the remaining USD 400 course fee.
eligibility: Be a citizen or permanent resident of an OAS member state, except Chile.
Have a strong interest in innovation and entrepreneurship.
Innovative resilience building business concepts closely linked to climate or environmental resilience is especially encouraged, or one that addresses a need in the market.
Can 'think outside the box,' exhibit critical thinking skills, and have a quest for discovery or investigative learning.
Demonstrate the ability to lead and inspire others.
Be a young professional who has an idea to develop, or is in the process of developing a small or medium enterprise in an active OAS member state.
Have a strong background in business management.
Be proficient in English.
Commit to at least 4.5 hours a week to the course over a one-semester period consisting of synchronous (live) and asynchronous content.
Have access to a computer with a reliable Internet connection, with appropriate video and audio functions.
Commit to covering the remaining course fee of USD 400 to the UDD.
coverage: USD 3,400 of the total course fee, contributed jointly by the GS/OAS and the University, out of a total cost of USD 3,800.
Access to the 100% online course delivered through UDD's Canvas platform.
A formal certificate issued by the Universidad del Desarrollo on successful completion of the program.
benefits: Experts in innovation are invited to speak about their projects during the course.

requirements: Submit a complete application through the online application link, including all supporting documents.
Cover the remaining USD 400 course fee to the UDD.
The scholarship will be formally awarded only after selected recipients sign an OAS Acceptance Form agreeing to its terms and conditions.

Comply with all academic guidelines requested by UDD and submit updates to those guidelines and requirements made by UDD's academic authorities.
records.english_requirement: Applicants whose native language is not English must submit an official transcript confirming completion of studies at an English-speaking university or college within the past five years; or TOEFL 570+ (paper), 230+ (computer), or 79+ (internet-based/IBT); or IELTS 6.5 or equivalent.
application_method: Prepare all supporting documents combined into one single PDF file not exceeding 5 MB, in English or with an official English translation.
Complete the OAS online scholarship application, noting that the system permits only one document upload.

If pre-selected, respond to the email contact and take part in an interview with the scholarship selection committee in English, if necessary.
If finally selected, sign the formal OAS acceptance form after being contacted by email with the scholarship offer and acceptance instructions.
records.selection_notes: A specialized OAS and UDD committee selects the recipients. Elements considered in awarding the scholarships are geographic distribution of the candidates, the applicant's profile including education and project outline and recommendation, the applicant's potential impact on completion of the course, and gender distribution. A selection committee pre-selects participants on that profile; pre-selected participants may be interviewed in English. Results are published at www.oas.org/scholarships by February 2027, and unsuccessful applicants are not contacted.
records.notes: This is a fee-reduction award, not a living stipend: the scholarship covers USD 3,400 of a USD 3,800 course fee and the recipient must find USD 400 plus study materials, equipment and internet access themselves. No living cost, travel or health insurance funding is published, so applicants must not budget this as full funding. Not eligible: current OAS scholarship recipients, GS/OAS staff and their immediate family, GS/OAS consultants, and permanent OAS staff and their immediate family. The recipient may decline the scholarship before the program start date without financial penalty, but declining after that date without proof of force majeure may require repayment of all funds awarded. The GS/OAS reserves the right to cancel this scholarship announcement at any time during the process.

records.description: The SG/OAS awards tuition discounts for online postgraduate study with UNIR (Spain), the Escuela de Posgrado Peruana de NEWMAN (Peru) and UNIR Mexico. benefits: Up to 885 places available across the three institutions for the 2026 academic course.

Pay the admission fee (cuota de admision) required by the institution in order to be admitted to the study programme.
Before starting the programme, demonstrate financial capacity to cover the programme costs not covered by the scholarship within the established period.

application_method: Step 1: Follow the admission process for the chosen programme directly with the institution, submitting all documentation the institution requires, and pay the admission fee.

Step 2: Once admitted and in receipt of the institution's application letter (carta de aplicacion), the applicant is automatically considered a candidate for the OAS-UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico scholarship; there is no separate scholarship application form.
Step 3: UNIR, EP NEWMAN, UNIR Mexico and the OAS form a specialised committee to select the scholarship holders.
Step 4: Await publication of results at www.oea.org/becas, announced from November 2026 for the 2a convocatoria.

Step 5: Only selected candidates are contacted by email by UNIR, EP NEWMAN and UNIR Mexico with the scholarship offer and acceptance instructions; after accepting, the scholarship holder starts the corresponding payment procedures with the chosen institution.
records.selection_notes: A specialised committee of UNIR, EP NEWMAN, UNIR Mexico and the OAS selects the scholarship holders, considering the geographic distribution of candidates according to the needs of Member States as reflected in the UNDP Human Development Index, the academic profile and merit and academic credentials, the applicant's potential impact on completing the programme, and gender distribution.
records.notes: This is a tuition discount only and it does not cover the whole fee, so applicants must not treat it as full funding. The 2a convocatoria deadlines fall between 19 and 30 October 2026, so the UNIR and EP NEWMAN lines close first on 19 October 2026. Excluded from eligibility: SG/OAS officials, persons under contract by results with the SG/OAS, Permanent Mission staff, and relatives of all of the above. Nicaraguan nationals and permanent legal residents are excluded. Applicants cannot study in their own country of origin. The call states programme costs shown in the document are orientative and may be lower in some countries, and it repeatedly warns that neither the OAS nor the institutions take responsibility for recognition, legalisation, homologation or convalidacion of the resulting title in the applicant's country of country of origin. The scholarship is conditional on academic performance, and it applies only to the value of the study programme. The SG/OAS reserves the right to cancel this announcement at any point in the process. The document's benefits section refers to a 'Responsabilidades del Becario' section on page 27, but the official PDF available at this URL contains only 10 pages, so that section could not be read.

records.official_source: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
records.region: Saudi Arabia (international applicants, 120+ nationalities on campus)
records.duration: M.S. is a 36-credit program expected to be completed in three semesters and one summer session; the M.S./Ph.D. pathway typically takes five to six years
records.deadline: Fall 2027 Round 2 application deadline 3 January 2027 (Round 2 opened 28 September 2026); decisions released 14 February 2027
records.application_period: Fall 2027 Round 2 applications open 28 September 2026 and close 3 January 2027; Spring 2027 entry (PhD only) had a Round 1 deadline of 27 September 2026 with decisions on 8 November 2026
records.description: The KAUST Fellowship is awarded automatically to admitted graduate students at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. The published package covers full tuition and bench fees (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year), a monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 per year for Ph.D. students depending on qualifications and academic progress), base on-campus accommodation, health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus, and relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs. KAUST states the total value of the Fellowship at between $70k and $80k per year depending on the student's situation.
records.best_fit: Graduate students in science, engineering, mathematics and related fields who hold a relevant bachelor's (Master's entry) or relevant master's (Ph.D. entry) degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0 and clear research interests.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants need a bachelor's degree in a relevant subject for Master's entry or a relevant master's degree for Ph.D. entry, be at least 18 years old on entry, hold a minimum 3.0/4.0 GPA, and demonstrate English proficiency.

Masters degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Ph.D. programs; Professional Master's degrees are not regarded as directly equivalent and must be declared
At least 18 years of age on entry

Evidence of proficiency in the English language
coverage: Full tuition and bench fee coverage (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year)
Monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 for Ph.D. students)
Base accommodation (shared accommodation for single students; 2-bed accommodation for married students)
Health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus
Relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs
benefits: Eligible students can request a housing upgrade, which will be subject to an additional fee
Relocation assistance covers each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation

requirements: Submit an application through the KAUST online application portal before the published round deadline
Provide contact details of 3 referees with academic or professional email addresses; personal email addresses are not accepted
Provide an official English language test score if available
Provide a clear, unobscured copy of the passport page showing picture and personal details (Saudi applicants may provide a national ID card)
All supporting documents, including academic transcripts, must be in English
If your official transcript is not in English, upload both the original transcript in the native language and a certified English translation
A statement of purpose of approximately 750 words
GRE or PGAT scores may be submitted but are not a compulsory requirement
records.english_requirement: IELTS 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in all individual sections (IELTS Online accepted), or TOEFL iBT 5.0 overall with at least 4.5 in all individual sections (KAUST Admissions code 4107; TOEFL Home Edition accepted), or PTE Academic 71 overall with at least 67 in all individual sections, or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 185 overall with at least 176 in all individual sections. Scores valid for two years from the test date.
application_method: Log into the KAUST application portal and submit the application before the published round deadline
Upload transcripts, CV, statement of purpose, English test score and passport page as part of the online application
Enter 3 referees' contact details, which sends reference requests to them automatically
Respond to any invitation for an online interview with KAUST faculty from your subject area
Await the decision notification by email within the published notification window for the round
records.selection_notes: Five-stage process: submission, Admissions team document review, faculty review committee evaluation and ranking against other applicants with shortlisting for interviews, academic interview and/or test, then decision. Admission review is holistic, considering academic achievements and personal qualities such as motivation and potential impact in the scientific community. All admission decisions are final and will not be reconsidered, and KAUST states it cannot provide individual feedback on specific applications.
records.notes: Relocation assistance is only for each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation. Some students with external sponsorship or funding may not be eligible for the KAUST Fellowship. Eligible students who request a housing upgrade pay an additional fee. An English proficiency score is not required if the applicant's degree was completed by in-person study at an accredited institution in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand, or if the applicant previously completed a degree taken at KAUST's campus in Thuwal; distance learning, satellite campuses, joint programs and branch institutions outside those countries do not qualify for the exemption. Applicants may submit without an English score but must meet the minimum before enrolment. Saudi nationals and PhD students scoring IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 4.5 / PTE 64 / Cambridge 176 may be admitted on condition of taking the Academic English Language Communication Course in their first year. KAUST does not accept Medium of Instruction certificates, the Duolingo English Test (except for Visiting Student applicants), TOEFL MyBest superscores, or IELTS One Skill Retake results. If accepted, there is a limited time to respond to secure the place or the decision may be withdrawn.

records.official_source: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI)
records.region: United Arab Emirates (international students and UAE nationals)
records.deadline: Final application deadline 15 December 2026, 5p.m. GST for all graduate programs except the Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence (28 February 2027 for MAAI); decision notification 31 March 2027; offer response deadline 15 April 2027
records.application_period: Application portal opened 7 September 2026, 8a.m. GST for all graduate programs except M.Sc. and Ph.D. Computational Biology, which opened 30 September 2026, 8a.m. GST. Portal closes 15 December 2026, 5p.m. GST (MAAI: 28 February 2027).
records.description: MBZUAI's graduate funding is not a single named scholarship but a University-and-faculty funding model under which funded M.Sc. and Ph.D. students receive free tuition fees, a monthly stipend, one return airfare each year to their home country, health insurance for the approved funding period, and a University-sponsored UAE residence visa and Emirates ID where eligible. Ph.D. Year 1 funding is centrally funded by the University while the student is matched with a faculty advisor, and funding moves to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2. M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is secured through a faculty advisor-sponsored research or teaching assistantship, or an approved government scholarship for UAE nationals, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence is a fee-based programme and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding.
records.best_fit: Graduate applicants to MBZUAI's M.Sc. or Ph.D. programmes in computer science, electrical or computer engineering, mathematics, physics or another relevant science or engineering major who hold a STEM degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.0 or 3.5 on a 4.0 scale depending on the programme.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a degree in a STEM field such as computer science, electrical engineering, computer engineering, mathematics, physics or another relevant science or engineering major from an accredited university or college recognized by the UAE Ministry of Education, with a minimum CGPA of 3.0 or 3.5 on a 4.0 scale depending on the program.

records.selection_notes: Applicants are evaluated on academic excellence, technical preparation, research potential, and alignment with their chosen program. Admission to MBZUAI is highly competitive with limited places available in each incoming cohort; MBZUAI states that forty-three percent of its incoming graduate students for the 2026-2027 academic year came from the world's top computer science universities. Funding decisions for M.Sc. students depend on whether a faculty advisor sponsors a research or teaching assistantship or, for UAE nationals, an approved government scholarship, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process.
records.notes: M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is NOT guaranteed for all admitted students; students without a funding source are classified as fee-paying. Ph.D. funding is subject to a confirmed advisor match and satisfactory progress, and transitions to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2. Funded students are expected to maintain an in-person presence on campus throughout their funded period and to obtain approval before being away. Students receiving external scholarships or fellowships must disclose this funding to the University; external funding normally replaces the University stipend rather than being paid in addition to it. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence (MAAI) is fee-based at AED 5,000 per credit, 34 credit hours, total tuition AED 170,000 (approx. USD 46,291), and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding. Cost of Attendance figures for Fall 2027 for unfunded M.Sc. students are currently being finalized and were not published on the page at the time of verification. An English language waiver exists and is described on the MBZUAI admissions FAQ, but the minimum score thresholds are published only on programme-specific pages, so no score is recorded here.

records.official_source: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU), a member of Qatar Foundation for Education, Science, and Community Development
records.region: Qatar (Qatari, resident and international graduate applicants)
records.duration: Stipend duration of 45 months for PhD programmes and 21 months for Master's programmes
records.deadline: Online graduate admission application opens to the public 1 October 2026; admission application deadline for international graduate applicants 1 February 2027; admission application deadline for Qatari and resident applicants who wish to apply for funding 15 March 2027
records.application_period: Online applications open to the public on 1 October 2026 and close on 1 February 2027 for international graduate applicants. Qatari and resident applicants who wish to apply for funding have a later deadline of 15 March 2027. No separate scholarship application is needed; candidates are considered during the admissions process.
records.description: HBKU graduate scholarships may include a tuition waiver applied to reduce tuition costs and a stipend paid directly to the student, and HBKU states that graduate students receiving a stipend would generally also be provided with a tuition waiver. Tuition waivers are standardised across HBKU and range from 100% for PhD STEM and PhD SHAPE and S.J.D. programmes down to 0% for LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes. Stipends are awarded to selected graduate students, with published monthly and annual rates for Qatari, international and local PhD and Master's students, over durations of 45 months for PhD and 21 months for Master's. Awards depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are made on a merit or need basis only.
records.best_fit: Graduate applicants to HBKU colleges (College of Science and Engineering, College of Health and Life Sciences, College of Islamic Studies, College of Humanities and Social Sciences, College of Law, College of Public Policy and the School of Economics and Management) who are seeking a tuition waiver and stipend, including international students who can serve as research assistants.
records.eligibility_summary: Tuition waivers and stipend awards at HBKU depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are awarded only on a merit or need basis; stipends are awarded to full-time graduate students serving as research assistants and/or teaching assistants.

records.selection_notes: There is a preliminary application review by the HBKU admissions team for completeness and eligibility, followed by assessment by the relevant college. Scholarships are not awarded automatically to admitted students: HBKU states they are offered based on merit or financial need and available funds, and they are reviewed annually depending on academic progress and available funds.
records.notes: Students are responsible for covering the cost of their housing, whether in Qatar Foundation dormitory facilities or external accommodation; this expense is paid from the monthly stipend or personal funds, and HBKU does not provide direct payment for student housing. Meal plans are not separately included; the stipend is a fixed amount meant to cover general living expenses including meals. Stipend awards do not depend on the student's marital status or the number of family dependents. Stipends for local students are limited. Stipends funded from external sources, including research grants, are excluded from the published rates. Self-sponsored graduate students are only eligible for a discounted tuition rate of 2,000 QAR per credit hour based on financial need, and these scholarship guidelines do not apply to students funded by external sources. Receipt of external funding may affect eligibility. Deferral of admission may affect scholarship eligibility. LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes carry a 0% tuition waiver.

records.name: MOFA Scholarship Program
records.official_source: United Arab Emirates Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA)
records.region: United Arab Emirates (Emirati nationals only; study takes place at approved universities abroad)
records.deadline: No application deadline is published on the program page; applications are registered through the online service and the review and final approval process typically takes between 3 to 5 months, with updates communicated by email or SMS
records.application_period: No published opening or closing dates. Applicants register through the MOFA scholarship service form and are notified of results by email or SMS; amendments after submission are handled through the call centre at +971 80044444.
records.description: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs runs a scholarship programme for Emirati students to study a Bachelor's degree at one of the world's top universities approved by MOFA, specialising in fields that meet the needs of the UAE diplomatic corps. MOFA states in its FAQ that the programme covers all tuition costs in accordance with the programme's policies, and the applicant must already hold an unconditional direct academic acceptance from an approved university indicating the programme start and end dates and the total cost. The programme is not a general study-abroad scholarship: it carries a service obligation, requiring the holder to join the MOFA diplomatic corps for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship and to join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy upon graduation.
records.best_fit: Emirati nationals aged 17 to 21 (up to 22 at the time of application) with a high school diploma meeting the published percentage thresholds, an IELTS Academic score of 6.5 or equivalent, and an unconditional offer from a MOFA-approved university, who are willing to enter the UAE diplomatic corps.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be UAE nationals holding a UAE passport and family book, aged between 17 and 21 with legal guardian approval, hold a high school diploma meeting the published percentage thresholds, have an IELTS Academic score of 6.5 or equivalent, and hold an acceptance letter from a MOFA-approved university.
eligibility: Must be UAE nationals (holders of UAE passports and family book)

Must be between 17 and 21 years old and have legal guardian approval; the FAQ states previous-year high school graduates may apply provided the applicant is between 17 and 22 years old at the time of application
Must provide a certificate of Good Conduct and Behavior from the relevant official authorities in the UAE

British System / IGCSE: completion of five IGCSE/GCSE subjects with a grade of B or higher and two AS/A Level subjects with a grade of C or higher
International Baccalaureate (IB): completion of the IB Diploma with a minimum average of 30 points or higher
School transcript listing all related instructional subjects

Applicants must hold an acceptance letter from an approved university listed and approved by MOFA
Applicants must agree to study a third language, if required
Male applicants must provide a certificate of exemption or completion of national service
Applicants must agree to join the UAE diplomatic corps at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship
Applicants must agree to join Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy (AGDA) upon graduation
Applicants must provide parental consent to join the scholarship program

coverage: All tuition costs, in accordance with the program's policies
benefits: Place in the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy's Post-Graduate Diploma in UAE Diplomacy and International Relations after the Bachelor's degree
Subsequent appointment to the diplomatic corps at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs after fulfilling graduation requirements

records.english_requirement: IELTS (Academic Module) 6.5 or above, or equivalent. The FAQ states applicants must achieve a minimum score of 6.5 in Academic IELTS or an equivalent score in TOEFL.
application_method: Obtain an unconditional direct academic acceptance from a MOFA-approved university for a specific specialty, institution and country, showing programme start and end dates and the total cost
Prepare the required documents in PDF format
Register through the MOFA scholarship service form at https://www.mofa.gov.ae/services/forms/scholarship
Upload the required documents with the registration

If already submitted and an amendment is needed, call +971 80044444 so the existing application can be removed and a new, updated application submitted
records.selection_notes: The admission procedure includes a number of tests, interviews and additional conditions. The interview is a mandatory part of the admission process and applicants must successfully pass it to complete the scholarship requirements. The review and final approval process typically takes between 3 to 5 months, with applicants notified of updates by email or SMS.
records.notes: This is a service-obligation scholarship, not free money to study anywhere: applicants must agree to join the UAE diplomatic corps at MOFA for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship, and must agree to join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy upon graduation. Only UAE nationals may apply, and only MOFA-approved universities are eligible, so an applicant who already has an offer from an unlisted institution cannot use this programme. Male applicants must have completed or been exempt from national service. Applicants who defer or want to change their major or country of study must inform the relevant programme officer at the Ministry and notify the cultural attaché in the country of study. The published page states that MOFA covers all tuition costs but does not publish any statement on living costs, accommodation, airfare or a stipend.

records.name: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
records.official_source: Study in NL (Nuffic) — financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and Dutch higher education institutions
records.region: Netherlands (applicants from outside the European Economic Area)
records.deadline: The application for the academic year 2026-2027 opened on 1 November 2025. Please check the website of the institution you want to apply to for the specific deadline(s).
records.application_period: Annual cycle: applications for an academic year open on 1 November of the preceding calendar year and close on institution-specific dates earlier in the year. The central page published the 2026-2027 opening date of 1 November 2025 and had not yet published a 2027-2028 opening date when checked.
records.description: The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national scholarship programme for bachelor and master students from outside the European Economic Area. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. Study in NL states the scholarship amounts to € 5,000 and is paid in the first year of studies, and explicitly notes that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Institutions set their own application deadlines and their own amount tiers, so the value and the deadline both depend on the institution you apply to.
records.best_fit: Non-EEA nationals applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the listed participating Dutch research universities or universities of applied sciences who can fund the remainder of tuition and living costs themselves.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be of non-EEA nationality, be applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch institution, meet that institution's own requirements, and not hold a degree from a Dutch education institution.
eligibility: Your nationality is non-EEA.
You are applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the participating Dutch higher education institutions.
You meet the specific requirements of the institution of your choice. You can find these on the website of the institution.
You do not have a degree from an education institution in the Netherlands.
Radboud University: You must not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons.

Radboud University: You must have (will obtain) a Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands, have no degrees achieved in the Netherlands and did not receive any previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes excluded, provided that they are part of the Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands).
Radboud University: You must meet the English language proficiency requirement for the Master's programme of your choice.
Radboud University: You must be able to comply with the conditions for obtaining a visa for the Netherlands.
Utrecht University: You must not be eligible for statutory tuition fees.

Utrecht University: You must never have been enrolled at an educational institution in the Netherlands (if you only took part in an exchange programme in the Netherlands, this does not make you ineligible).
coverage: A one-off grant of € 5,000 paid in the first year of studies (Study in NL and Radboud University figures).
Nothing else. Study in NL states it is not a full-tuition scholarship; Radboud University states the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered.
benefits: At Radboud University the NL Scholarship is always combined with the Radboud Scholarship Programme (RSP): applicants must also apply for the RSP, and can be awarded both or just the RSP, never the NLS alone.
Utrecht University publishes three award tiers rather than one: €5,000, €10,000 and €15,000, all paid in the first year of studies even for a two-year programme.
Nuffic states the programme is made available jointly with 47 Dutch higher education institutions, which will grant scholarships to 2,112 students per academic year.
requirements: Apply for an NL Scholarship-eligible programme at a participating institution and meet that institution's admission and scholarship requirements.
Utrecht University: your application must be submitted before 1 February, 23:59 CET; the application portal closes at that time and selection only starts after the deadline.
Utrecht University: results are aimed to be published by mid-April.

Utrecht University: you must demonstrate you can cover the remaining costs by completing the Statement of Financial Resources, showing a realistic plan covering the full nominal duration of the Master's programme.

Radboud University: your OSIRIS application must be submitted by 31 January 2027, 23:59 CET at the latest, and must be complete by 14 February 2027, 23:59 CET at the latest; incomplete applications will not be considered for scholarship selection.
Radboud University: proof of English proficiency should be handed in before the 14 February 2027 deadline.
Radboud University: the decision is communicated around mid-April 2027 (date subject to change).
Nuffic operates an integrity Code of Conduct; the programme may not be involved in financial misconduct, tax or social security default, money laundering, terrorist financing or related conduct.
application_method: Choose a participating Dutch institution and an NL Scholarship-eligible programme (not every programme participates).
Apply for admission to that programme through the institution's own application system.
Radboud University: indicate during the OSIRIS application procedure for a Master's programme that you wish to apply for an NL Scholarship.

Utrecht University: submit the application for an NL Scholarship-eligible MA programme, log in to your OSIRIS Online Application account, locate 'NL Scholarship' under your dashboard, click 'View/Edit' for the scholarship linked to your chosen programme, open the application form, answer all required questions and submit.
Meet your institution's published deadline and completeness deadline.
Upload all required documents, including the institutional financial-plans form where required.
Await the selection outcome, published by the institution after its deadline.
records.selection_notes: Utrecht University assesses applications on the academic background shown in the master's programme application, the motivation explaining the relevance of the time in the Netherlands and at Utrecht University to future goals, and the quality and feasibility of the financial plan. Radboud University assesses on academic excellence (outstanding study results, relevance of the previous degree to the programme, ranking of the university where previous degrees were obtained) and ambition (quality and relevance of the motivation letter, promise shown by achievements, life experience and extracurricular activities such as internships or volunteering), with each faculty considering its own applicants individually. Admission to the programme and selection for the scholarship are two separate processes.
records.notes: This is not full funding and should never be budgeted as such: Study in NL states it is not a full-tuition scholarship and Radboud University states explicitly that the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered. At Radboud University the award is limited to one year and can only be received once. The programme was renamed from Holland Scholarship to NL Scholarship in June 2023, so older material under the old name may be out of date. Selection for the scholarship is separate from admission to the programme — an admission offer does not imply a scholarship. Utrecht University requires applicants to prove they can cover the full remaining cost of the programme.

official_details.description: The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national scholarship programme for bachelor and master students from outside the European Economic Area. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. Study in NL states the scholarship amounts to € 5,000 and is paid in the first year of studies, and explicitly notes that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Institutions set their own application deadlines and their own amount tiers, so the value and the deadline both depend on the institution you apply to.

records.description: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships support internationally mobile postdoctoral researchers for up to two years in the life sciences. EMBO provides grants to host institutions in EMBC Member States to issue employment contracts to EMBO Fellows, with the grant intended to cover the cost of that employment contract (employer and awardee social contributions, taxes, and the net salary). Fellows working in countries other than EMBC Member States receive a stipend instead, which is solely intended to cover the cost of living in the host country. The fellowship does not cover bench fees, overheads, consumables or any other financial benefits to the host supervisor or institute.
records.best_fit: Postdoctoral researchers in the life sciences who completed a doctorate within the two years before application and must move country to take up the position.
records.eligibility_summary: Doctoral (or equivalent) degree held at the start of the fellowship, obtained within the two years prior to application, with at least one first-author paper and a required country change.
eligibility: Applicants must hold a doctorate or equivalent at the start of the fellowship.
Applicants who already hold a PhD at the time of application are eligible to apply only if they obtained it during the two years prior to the date the application is submitted.
Applicants must have at least one first author publication (research paper) accepted in or published in an international peer reviewed journal at the time of application.

A first author preprint with public in-depth peer reviews is also sufficient for eligibility provided the reviews were verifiably obtained from an independent peer review service; informal comments, highlights and reviews posted by individuals are excluded.
All applications must involve movement between countries.
Applications to go to the country in which the PhD was obtained will not be considered.
Applications to return to a laboratory where the candidate has worked in the past for more than six months, either in one or in several visits, will not be considered.

Applications for an EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowship to be held in the laboratory, institute or department in which the candidate worked to obtain the PhD, or to work again with the candidate's supervisor, no matter where the latter is located, will not be considered.
Candidates who have already started working in the host laboratory can apply only if they have been living in the host country for less than six months at the time the application is submitted.
Candidates can only submit one application for one project at one host laboratory at each round of selection.

Reapplication is permissible only once. Effective from the Autumn 2027 selection round (i.e. for all applications submitted after January 22, 2027, 14:00 CET), re-applications will no longer be permitted.
Projects that are a direct continuation of the PhD work are not eligible.
Effective from the Autumn 2026 Selection Round, a host laboratory may support a maximum of one candidate per selection round.

Exceptions to the eligibility rules are made for applicants with extraordinary personal circumstances, such as parental leave, severe illness, or military service; no exceptions for voluntary career breaks.
coverage: For EMBC Member State host institutions: the cost of an employment contract issued by the host institution to the awardee, including employer's social contributions, awardee's social contributions, taxes as required by national and local laws and regulations, and the net salary of the awardee
For non-EMBC host countries: a stipend solely intended to cover the cost of living in the host country
Travel and relocation allowance paid as a lump sum to eligible fellows, ideally before the start date of the fellowship
Child daycare allowance for non-EMBC fellows: up to 2,500 euros per fellowship year and per child for children under the age of six (prorated by fraction of year)
benefits: Dependent child allowance for non-EMBC Member State fellows, value depending on the country visited

Parental leave: three months paid parental leave for non-EMBC fellows, plus a fellowship extension for an equivalent period; EMBC fellows whose parental leave is covered by the host country's welfare system or host institute may request a no-cost extension
Part-time work at 50% or 75% of full time may be requested at no cost for EMBO; maximum fellowship duration (full-time plus part-time) must not exceed 36 months

Free attendance at an EMBO Laboratory Leadership Course (currently online only), subject to limited waivers, granted first come first served, within three years of award and only if the fellowship is held for at least six months
Invitation to join the EMBO Fellows' Network and to the EMBO Fellows' Meeting for fellows awarded three and four years earlier
requirements: Submit the application through the EMBO online application system by the published cutoff date
Submit a first author publication record meeting the eligibility requirement at the time of application

records.description: The Royal Society Career Development Fellowship is a four-year postdoctoral research fellowship supporting early career scientists from underrepresented backgrounds to establish research in a UK institution. Applicants can apply for up to £703,800 over four years, covering a contribution to the Research Fellow's salary and associated on-costs (at 80%), directly allocated costs (at 80%), and research expenses (at 100%). Relocation and visa costs for the applicant and dependants can be requested in addition to the grant cap. records.deadline: Rolling in three calls per year, each opening approximately eight months before the selection meeting and closing when 800 applications are received. The next call opens on 15 November 2026 for the July 2027 selection meeting, with the earliest possible fellowship start in September 2027. The current call has reached the maximum of 800 applications and no new applications can be created.

Each call closes automatically once 800 applications are received.
records.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe to conduct their own research at a German host institution. For postdocs the monthly fellowship amount is €3,000 and for experienced researchers €3,600, plus additional benefits. On top of the fellowship amount the Foundation provides family benefits for children and partners, subsidies for private full health insurance, and travel expense allowances, as well as personal support throughout the sponsorship. The host institute generally receives an allowance for research costs of €800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, or €500 for humanities and social sciences.
records.best_fit: Non-German postdoctoral researchers who completed their doctorate within the last four years (or experienced researchers within twelve years) and need a 6-24 month research stay in Germany.
records.eligibility_summary: Non-German national with a doctorate completed within the last four years (postdoc track) or twelve years (experienced researcher track), no more than 90 days in Germany in the 18 months before applying, with a German host providing a mentoring agreement and a confirmation of research facilities.
eligibility: Postdocs: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last four years?
Experienced researchers: did you complete your doctorate - or equivalent academic qualification - during the last twelve years?
Postdocs: have you been published in academic journals and by publishing houses that are reviewed according to international standards?

Experienced researchers: is your academic profile substantiated by an extensive list of publications including important papers in which you acted as thematic lead, and do you hold a leadership role commensurate with your career level (for example assistant professor, lecturer, head of an independent research group or higher)?

If a doctorate in your field or country of origin is not possible or uncommon, you can still apply up to 16 years after completing your master's or other postgraduate degree provided you have a publication record commensurate with your career level.

You are not a German national. If you are a German national, or if you obtained your university entrance qualification and university degree, or your university degree and your doctorate, in Germany, you can apply if you have lived and worked abroad for more than ten years and intend to continue doing so long-term. Have you lived and worked abroad for more than five years? You can still apply if there is a strong connection to your current country of residence (permanent employment, additional citizenship etc.).
For your application to be successful, you may not have lived in Germany for longer than a total of 90 days within the 18-month period prior to submitting your application.

A researcher from an academic institution of your choice in Germany will provide you with a mentoring agreement and written confirmation that research facilities are available, and will compile a detailed review for you.

You can provide two expert reviews. For postdocs: your doctoral supervisor and one other researcher - outside of your institute, if possible. For experienced researchers: important collaborative partners and/or researchers at your own institute as well as other institutes - outside your country of origin, if possible.

Natural sciences and engineering: you must have a good knowledge of German or English. Humanities, social sciences and medicine: you must have a good knowledge of German if this is necessary for conducting your research successfully; otherwise good knowledge of English will suffice.
You may not apply for the Humboldt Research Fellowship if you have already received sponsorship directly from the Humboldt Foundation (research fellowship or award).

No language certificate is required if English or German is your native language. An English language certificate is not required if you have worked in an English-speaking country for several years.

records.selection_notes: The decision to award research fellowships is taken by a selection committee consisting of 60-70 researchers from various fields. Applications are academically evaluated by a peer review process based on: academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of the key publications named in the application; originality and innovative potential of your proposed research; your future potential; and your independent research profile (for experienced researchers). The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility. The Foundation expects 20-25% of the applications received to be approved.
records.notes: The current call has reached the maximum of 800 applications, so no new applications can be created at present; the next call opens on 15 November 2026. Applicants who have already started an application can save and continue working on it but cannot submit until the next application round opens. Applications are forwarded to the Foundation only after the host has uploaded their documents, so the host's speed determines your effective submission. Applicant who has already worked in Germany for 12 months or more should look for a new academic environment; applications involving returning to the doctoral supervisor or mentor of a longer postdoctoral stay are generally rejected. Individuals with whom you are in a close personal or familial relationship cannot be selected as hosts. In the case of unanimously rejected applications you must wait a minimum of 18 months before re-applying. Decisions cannot be appealed.

records.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award funds early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and lead their own independent research programme. The award provides the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire grant period, determined by the administering organisation, plus up to £400,000 for research expenses. Certain costs sit outside the £400,000 limit, including overheads, overseas allowances, adjustment support, and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques. Staff salaries are funded up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post, and no studentships are provided on this award.
records.best_fit: Researchers with a completed PhD (or equivalent) and no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, from any discipline, based at an eligible UK, Republic of Ireland or eligible LMIC organisation, whose work has potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
records.funding_period: up to, over the award duration (usually 5 years)
records.eligibility_summary: Early-career researcher with a passed PhD viva or at least four years' equivalent research experience, no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, at least 80% of research time on the project, based at an eligible administering organisation.
eligibility: You should be able to demonstrate the ability to conduct independent, original research that makes a meaningful contribution to knowledge, achieved through completion of a PhD or equivalent higher research degree (you must have passed your thesis defence by the date you submit your application), or through at least four years' research experience equivalent to a PhD.

Any periods of research undertaken during an undergraduate or Master's degree are not counted as equivalent research experience, and you must not have started a PhD or equivalent higher research degree if relying on the experience route.

You may have some postdoctoral experience in your proposed field of study, but no more than three years at the date of submission unless you can demonstrate how other factors have impacted on your research career.

You must be able to contribute at least 80% of your research time in support of the project proposed in the award, and should not spend more than 20% of your time on non-research related activities; if you are in a clinical craft speciality you may spend up to 40% of your time on clinical duties.

If you are a health professional and want to continue with clinical activities, you must be registered with, and be licensed by, the relevant professional regulator in the country you intend to work in.

Your administering organisation must be in the UK, the Republic of Ireland, or a low- or middle-income country apart from India and mainland China; the organisation must be not-for-profit and can be a higher education institution, research institute or healthcare organisation.

Your sponsor must be an individual at your administering organisation holding an established post (or an honorary academic appointment) for the duration of the award, and must guarantee the space and resources you will need from the start date to the end date of the award.
You should also identify a mentor for the period of your award with a track record in training and mentorship; your sponsor can also be your mentor. Sponsors and mentors are not paid for their input.
Coapplicants are not accepted.
You may only have one application under consideration as a lead applicant at any one time for the Early Career Award, Career Development Award and Discovery Award schemes.

Your research must fit within what Wellcome supports in Discovery Research and have the potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing; it can be in any discipline including STEM, experimental medicine, humanities and social science, clinical/allied health sciences and public health.
coverage: Total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire period of the grant, determined by the administering organisation, including basic salary, employer contributions, pension scheme costs, incremental salary progression and locally recognised allowances
Up to £400,000 for research expenses
Overheads, which do not count towards the £400,000 limit; total overhead cost should not be more than 20% of direct research costs
Overseas allowances and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques, which do not count towards the £400,000 limit
Adjustment support including assistive technology and support staff, which does not count towards the £400,000 limit
Visa and work permit costs for the grantholder, their partner and dependent children, plus Immigration Health Surcharge costs if in the UK six months or more
Relocation allowance of up to £1,000 to cover personal removal costs
Staff salaries up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post
Conference attendance contributions: £2,000 a year for the grantholder and £1,000 each a year for research and technical staff, plus accredited carbon credits to mitigate emissions
Caring responsibility costs at conferences up to £1,000 per person per conference, subject to the stated conditions

Continuing professional development and professional skills training up to £500 a year per person, and research skills training, for staff in posts of 12 months or more working on the grant at 50% FTE or more
Materials and consumables, animals, equipment purchase and maintenance, computer equipment, and access charges for shared equipment, facilities or services
benefits: If, after two or more years from the activation date, your organisation awards you a permanent, open-ended or long-term rolling contract that includes your salary, you can keep the salary element of the award to use towards your remaining research costs
Award holders who need a visa to work in the UK may be eligible for a Global Talent Visa
The award may be held on a part-time basis, with the duration extended to reflect this; the application must still be costed at 1.0 (100%) full-time equivalent
Access to Wellcome's global talent, mentoring and community networks

records.selection_notes: Applications are assessed through Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups and then peer review. The same project may be submitted for consideration a maximum of two times across all Wellcome funding schemes and themed funding calls, and resubmissions must include significant changes demonstrating clear development of the original proposal. If your application scores in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting you will not be permitted to resubmit. If unsuccessful with an Early-Career Award, you may submit one further application for the same project to any Wellcome scheme, provided you still meet the eligibility criteria.
records.notes: Location eligibility is changing on 29 October 2026: from that date Wellcome will only accept applications from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia, so an application submitted in October 2026 from a Republic of Ireland or a Latin American organisation would not be accepted under the new rule. You can only hold one of these awards and Wellcome does not offer renewals. No studentships are provided on this award. You cannot apply if you hold or have accepted an equivalent award at this career stage, or if you have an existing tenured salaried post for the duration of the award (unless based in a low- or middle-income country). You cannot apply if you intend to carry out activities that involve the transfer of grant funds into mainland China. Total resubmission of the same project is capped at two times across all Wellcome schemes. Overheads are not paid to UK research organisations that already receive core funding for overheads.

official_details.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award provides funding for early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity. Through innovative projects they will deliver shifts in understanding related to human life, health and wellbeing, and by the end of the award they will be ready to lead their own independent research programme. The award funds the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire period of the grant plus up to £400,000 for research expenses, with certain costs outside the £400,000 limit.

No more than three years of postdoctoral experience at the date of submission, unless other factors have impacted on the research career; part-time work, career breaks and time outside research are allowed for.

referee_tracking.instructions: An individual at your administering organisation holding an established post or honorary academic appointment for the duration of the award. They must guarantee space and resources from the start date to the end date, confirm the research environment will support the project, and confirm workload expectations (no more than 20% of your time on non-research activities, up to 40% clinical duties in a clinical craft speciality). Sponsors are not paid for their input.

Should have a track record in training and mentorship and support you to manage your application, develop your research career, progress your personal development, and manage processes and regulations at the administering organisation. Does not need to be based at the administering organisation and is not paid. Your sponsor can also be your mentor.

If you plan to work for more than three months outside your administering organisation, you must also have an additional sponsor at that location who must guarantee the space and resources you will need during your visit.

Collaborators support delivery but do not lead a component, do not have to meet eligibility requirements, cannot receive a salary or compensation, and are not required to give a minimum research time commitment.

records.application_period: Two application rounds per cycle, organised to match the academic calendars of the participating programmes. For the 2027 cycle: Application Window #1 January 18 - February 26, 2027; Application Window #2 March 29 - May 21, 2027. Each participating university sets its own admission deadlines, which fall before the JJ/WBGSP window closes.
records.description: The JJ/WBGSP is a fully funded master's scholarship for mid-career professionals from listed World Bank developing countries who are already admitted to one of a fixed set of participating development-related master's programmes. For the 2027 cycle the World Bank states that a scholarship provides tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, basic medical insurance obtained through the university, and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies depending on the host country and is not published on the programme page. The Government of Japan solely funds the scholarship on an annual basis, and scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.
records.best_fit: Nationals of listed developing countries who hold a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline, have at least three years of paid development-related work experience acquired within the past six years, and can first secure unconditional admission (except funding) to one of only 44 participating master's programmes outside their country of citizenship and residence.
records.funding_period: per trip (published travel allowance only; the monthly subsistence allowance amount is not published)
records.eligibility_summary: National of a listed World Bank developing country with a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the application deadline, at least three years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past six years, and unconditional admission (except funding) to a JJ/WBGSP participating master's programme outside their country of citizenship and residence.
eligibility: Be a national of a World Bank member developing country on the published 2027 eligible list
Not hold dual citizenship of any developed country
Be in good health
Hold a bachelor's (or equivalent) degree earned at least 3 years prior to the Application Deadline date

Be employed in development-related work in a paid full-time position at the time of submitting the scholarship application, with at least 3 years of paid development-related employment since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past 6 years from the date of the application deadline

On or before the scholarship application deadline date, be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) for the upcoming academic year to at least one of the JJ/WBGSP participating master's programs located outside of the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence listed at the time the call for scholarship applications opens; the letter of admission must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application

Not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment of the World Bank Group, and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)
Individuals who have previously been offered a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but declined it, or who previously received a JJ/WBGSP scholarship but did not graduate, are not eligible to apply again
Exception: applicants from a country on the list of Fragile and Conflict States in Annex 3 of the Application Guidelines may have their limited employment opportunities taken into consideration
coverage: Tuition for the graduate program
Cost of basic medical insurance obtained through the university

Monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus during the scholarship period (accommodations, food, books); amount varies by host country and is not published on the programme page
Economy class air travel between the home country and the host university at the start of the study program and immediately after the scholarship period
US$600 travel allowance for each trip
benefits: The scholarship covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
Participation in the JJ/WBGSP alumni community of more than 7,000 mid-career professionals from 160 developing countries and Japan
requirements: Must already hold an unconditional admission letter (except for funding) from a JJ/WBGSP participating master's program, located outside the applicant's country of citizenship and country of residence as listed when the call opened
The letter of admission must be uploaded before submitting the scholarship application

The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates who are admitted unconditionally (except for finance) to a participating master's program and shortlisted as eligible JJ/WBGSP applicants by the participating university
All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to with no exceptions; they will not change during an open call for applications
application_method: Choose a target from the published list of participating master's programs for the relevant application window
Apply directly to that university and satisfy its own admission requirements and internal deadlines
Be admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to the participating master's program
Ask the university whether you meet both conditions: unconditional admission and shortlisting as an eligible JJ/WBGSP applicant
Once the university shortlists you, it communicates the link to the JJ/WBGSP application form
Upload the admission letter and submit the JJ/WBGSP application within the application window
records.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30% weight), quality of professional recommendations (30% weight), quality of commitment to the applicant's home country (30% weight), and quality of education background (10% weight). The Secretariat uses the average of the two assessors plus a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, a reasonable distribution across gender, unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to applicants who otherwise have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists go to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
records.notes: Not eligible if admitted to a non-participating programme: the World Bank states explicitly that if you are not admitted to one of the participating master's programs you are not eligible to apply for a JJ/WBGSP scholarship in 2027. The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you hold another award you must send those documents to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat. Scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree. Declining an earlier offer, or receiving the scholarship and failing to graduate, permanently bars reapplication. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 developing-country-national cycle is live.

official_details.description: The JJ/WBGSP is open to citizens of certain developing countries with relevant professional experience and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts who are applying to a master's degree program in a development-related topic. Subject to available funding, JJ/WBGSP offers scholarships for 44 Participating Master's Programs in 24 universities in the U.S., Europe, Africa, Oceania and Japan in key areas of development, including economic policy management, tax policy, and infrastructure management. A JJ/WBGSP scholarship provides tuition, a monthly living stipend, round-trip airfare, health insurance, and travel allowance.

official_details.funding_label: Tuition, basic medical insurance through the university, monthly subsistence allowance for all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, and a US$600 travel allowance per trip; stipend amount varies by host country and is not published

records.description: Under the 2026 cycle UNESCO and the Government of Japan award 10 fellowships to young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye to carry out postgraduate research in a Japanese university or research institution. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant may cover international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary, accommodation, medical insurance, personal subsistence in Japan including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses, and other research-related expenses where applicable. It is a research fellowship, not a degree programme: the grant does not cover tuition fees, and the page publishes no award figures beyond the US$10,000 ceiling.

records.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by a Selection Committee composed of experts from UNESCO and the Government of Japan in the relevant fields, taking into account the merits of the candidates and the quality, relevance and originality of their proposed research. The final selection decision is made by the Japanese authorities based on the recommendation of the Committee, with due consideration to gender equality and diversity.
records.notes: Only 10 fellowships are awarded in the 2026 cycle, and only applications nominated by your National Commission are accepted, so the national shortlist is the binding gate. The fellowship grant is a lump sum capped at US$10,000, not a line-itemed scholarship, and the cost of the mandatory medical insurance is deducted from the total before disbursement, so the amount actually received is below the ceiling. The grant does NOT cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment including computers, publication costs, or participation in conferences, unless such participation can be clearly justified as an integral part of the research and makes a direct and significant contribution to the project. Candidates who submit incomplete applications, or who submit the online applications beyond the deadline, will not be considered. The practical deadline is at least two weeks earlier than 15 October 2026 because your National Commission must forward the file.

official_details.description: Established in 2001 under the Japanese Funds-in-Trust for the Capacity-Building of Human Resources, the UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme, also known as the UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme, is a long-standing initiative supported by the Government of Japan to strengthen research capacities and promote international knowledge exchange in areas aligned with UNESCO's mandate. Under the 2026 cycle, UNESCO and the Government of Japan will award 10 fellowships to highly qualified young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye. The fellowships support innovative and high-quality postgraduate research related to heritage conservation and management, sustainable development and artificial intelligence, with particular attention to interdisciplinary research connecting these themes with social, ethical, governance and contextual dimensions. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. Since its establishment, the Programme has enabled 300 young researchers from 100 countries around the world to pursue postgraduate research.
